title: German multicenter biobank and registry for phenotype-specific genomic research in thoracic aortic disease.
abstract: PURPOSE: To establish a national multicentre biobank and registry for future genomic and genotype-phenotype studies of distinct thoracic aortic disease entities and to report the study design and current recruitment status. METHODS: A prospective multicenter registry with integrated biobanking was established in May 2024 across eight German vascular and cardiovascular centres. Patients with Stanford type B aortic dissection (STBAD), thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA), intramural hematoma (IMH), or penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) were enrolled. Clinical characteristics, treatment, imaging parameters, and longitudinal outcomes were collected in a centralized pseudonymized database, and EDTA blood samples were stored at - 80 °C for future genomic analyses. An established retrospective Heidelberg cohort of 118 patients with isolated STBAD serves as a hypothesis-generating cohort, while the prospective multicenter cohort provides an independent population for subsequent validation and extension of genetic findings. No genomic analyses were performed for the present report. RESULTS: As of May 2026, 274 patients had been included: 118 patients with STBAD from the hypothesis-generating Heidelberg cohort and 156 patients from the prospective multicenter cohort comprising 84 patients with STBAD, 40 with TAA, 13 with IMH, and 19 with PAU. The most prominent descriptive difference between disease entities was age distribution. Among patients with STBAD, 116/202 (57.4%) were younger than 60 years, compared with 6/40 (15.0%) with TAA, 2/13 (15.4%) with IMH, and 2/19 (10.5%) with PAU. A positive family history of thoracic aortic disease was reported in 14 patients (5.1%), and hypermobility or other connective tissue features were documented in 12 patients (4.4%), and two patients (0.7%) had a documented connective tissue disorder. Overall, 217 patients (79.2%) underwent surgical or endovascular treatment. Median imaging follow-up ranged from 1.5 months in IMH to 48 months in the retrospective Heidelberg cohort. CONCLUSION: This national multicenter biobank and registry provides a deeply phenotyped platform for future investigation of the genetic basis of distinct thoracic aortic disease entities. The observed difference in age distribution provide a rationale for phenotype-specific genomic investigation but should not be interpreted as evidence of differing genetic contributions per se. Continued recruitment and longitudinal follow-up will enable future future genomic and genotype-phenotype analyses.

METHODS: A prospective multicenter registry with integrated biobanking was established in May 2024 across eight German vascular and cardiovascular centres. Patients with Stanford type B aortic dissection (STBAD), thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA), intramural hematoma (IMH), or penetrating aortic ulcer (PAU) were enrolled.

title: May - Thurner syndrome: a case report of a lethal undiagnosed left iliac vein thrombosis.
abstract: May-Thurner syndrome (MTS), also known as iliac vein compression syndrome, is a pro-thrombotic condition caused by the compression of the left iliac vein by the right common iliac artery, often resulting in deep vein thrombosis (DVT). MTS accounts for 2-5% of all DVT cases and is often underdiagnosed due to the difficulty of assessing the deep pelvic veins. We present the case of a 63-year-old female with a history of Crohn's disease and scoliosis, who developed lower limb pain and venous ulcers. Despite negative Doppler ultrasound and exclusion of other conditions such as diabetes and vasculitis, the patient deteriorated after a fall, leading to cardiogenic shock and death. Autopsy revealed a thrombus in the left iliac vein and an embolus in the inferior vena cava, causing fatal venous obstruction. Histological examination confirmed thrombotic formations in both sites and assigned the iliac thrombus to phase III of thrombus organization, indicating that it predated the terminal event by several days. This case underscores the importance of comprehensive evaluation in patients with lower limb ulcers and pain, as Doppler ultrasound alone may not detect deeper venous abnormalities such as MTS. Advanced imaging techniques, including multi-detector computed tomography venography or magnetic resonance venography, may be necessary to diagnose MTS in such cases, preventing life-threatening complications.

MTS accounts for 2-5% of all DVT cases and is often underdiagnosed due to the difficulty of assessing the deep pelvic veins. We present the case of a 63-year-old female with a history of Crohn's disease and scoliosis, who developed lower limb pain and venous ulcers.

title: Post-embolization dynamic changes in Obsidio Conformable Embolic: volume and radiodensity analysis.
abstract: PURPOSE: To characterize the temporal dynamic and clinical remodeling of the Obsidio™ Conformable Embolic (Obsidio) post endovascular delivery using longitudinal quantitative CT volumetry and Hounsfield unit (HU) attenuation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 21 patients (30 vessels) embolized with Obsidio for acute hemorrhage or hypervascular tumor between 2023 and 2026. Patients had at least two follow-up computed tomography (CT) scans. The primary endpoint was the percent change in embolic cast volume and HU attenuation, measured using standardized Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS) segmentation tools. Secondary endpoints included assessment for recanalization. RESULTS: All embolizations were technically successful (100%). On the first follow-up CT (median 12 days), the mean Obsidio volume was 89.33 ± 13.86% of the original volume (p = 0.0002). On the second follow-up (median 36 days), the volume was 79.51 ± 19.76% of baseline volume (p = 0.0004), representing 20.49% reduction. On third follow-up CT (median 76 days), volume was 85.2 ± 18.92% (p = 0.047). On the fourth follow-up CT, volume was 66.76 ± 16.9% (p = 0.0048). On the fifth follow-up CT, volume was 60.15 ± 3.15% (p = 0.00001) The average volume reduction rate decelerated from 0.99%/day to 0.71%/day to 0.17%/day then stabilized at 0.2%/day. Concurrently, mean Hounsfield unit attenuation increased by 4.85% (p = 0.06) on the second follow-up CT scan. No evidence of recanalization, distal embolization, or cast fragmentation was observed on any of CT scans. CONCLUSION: The Obsidio embolic cast undergoes progressive reduction in volume and increase in HU attenuation over time without evidence of vessel recanalization. This temporal dynamic of Obsidio embolic is consistent with bioresorption of its gelatin and water components, supporting the concept of persistent occlusion via in vivo remodeling.

title: A 78-Year-Old Man With a Previously Stable Atherosclerotic Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Presenting With Impending Rupture Following COVID-19.
abstract: BACKGROUND Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture is a life-threatening condition. Although elective repair is generally guided by aneurysm size, impending rupture can occur when rapid aneurysmal expansion or periaortic inflammatory changes develop before overt hemodynamic deterioration. This report describes the case of a 78-year-old man with a previously stable 43-mm atherosclerotic AAA who presented with impending rupture after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). CASE REPORT A 78-year-old Japanese man with a known AAA under imaging surveillance developed fever and was diagnosed with COVID-19 by nasopharyngeal polymerase chain reaction testing. Seven days later, he was admitted for recurrent fever, cough, poor appetite, and elevated inflammatory markers. His medical history included hypertension, heavy smoking, advanced chronic kidney disease, and diffuse atherosclerotic disease. The aneurysm had shown minimal growth over 2 years, with a stable maximum short-axis diameter of approximately 43 mm on serial computed tomography. After admission, C-reactive protein levels initially decreased but rose again on hospital day 11, accompanied by new-onset mild low back pain and no marked blood pressure elevation or hemodynamic instability. Repeat non-contrast abdominal computed tomography performed 18 days after COVID-19 diagnosis demonstrated rapid AAA expansion from 43 mm to 51 mm within 2 months, with periaortic fat stranding, consistent with impending rupture. Urgent endovascular aneurysm repair was performed before hemodynamic deterioration. The postoperative course was stable, and the patient was discharged without ischemic or procedural complications. CONCLUSIONS This case shows that a previously stable AAA can abruptly destabilize after recent COVID-19. Repeat imaging should be considered when inflammatory markers rise or new symptoms occur, even when symptoms are mild.

title: A Systematic Review of in vitro Modeling and Experimentation for Cerebral Thrombectomy: Applications, Insights, and Future Directions.
abstract: This systematic review focuses on in vitro research exploring specific aspects of cerebral thrombectomy. It highlights the principal applications of this research, important insights from the published literature, and areas in which controlled and reproducible in vitro experimentation may provide particular value. Predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria were set and the Public/Publisher MEDLINE (PubMed) database was searched to identify relevant peer-reviewed articles. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines were followed. A total of 92 articles were included in the qualitative review and grouped into 8 broader themes according to the principal application of the in vitro experiment and primary research question: (1) device evaluation and preclinical development, (2) thrombectomy techniques and device manipulation, (3) vessel geometry and morphology, (4) hemodynamics, (5) robotic thrombectomy, (6) angiographic clot localization, (7) in vitro validation of in silico models, and (8) clot characteristics and vessel interaction. Marked methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative synthesis or meta-analysis. Rather than seeking to establish the comparative superiority of individual devices or techniques, this review qualitatively synthesizes how in vitro experimentation has been applied to cerebral thrombectomy and what it has demonstrated. Three areas were identified as particularly suited to further controlled in vitro investigation: vascular compliance, anatomical location of vessel occlusion, and validation of in silico models. Limitations of both in vitro experimentation and the review methodology are acknowledged, and correlation with clinical practice remains essential where possible.
englishSummary: This systematic review focuses on in vitro research exploring specific aspects of cerebral thrombectomy. It highlights the principal applications of this research, important insights from the published literature, and areas in which controlled and reproducible in vitro experimentation may provide particular value. Predetermined inclusion and exclusion criteria were set and the Public/Publisher MEDLINE (PubMed) database was searched to identify relevant peer-reviewed articles.

title: Long-Term Stabilization after Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair for a Behçet-Related Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Behçet disease is a relapsing systemic vasculitis that can rarely cause aortic aneurysms or pseudoaneurysms. Endovascular repair is increasingly used for Behçet-related aortic lesions, but the long-term interaction between aneurysm remodeling, endoleak, and systemic inflammatory activity remains clinically important. CASE PRESENTATION: A 34-year-old man presented with persistent back pain due to an impending rupture of a newly developed saccular descending thoracic aortic aneurysm. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed before Behçet disease was definitively diagnosed. Postoperatively, persistent fever, elevated inflammatory markers, recurrent oral aphthous ulcers, and intestinal ulcerations led to the diagnosis of Behçet disease. The aneurysm initially regressed after corticosteroid therapy but rapidly re-expanded during steroid tapering, in parallel with fever, back pain, and increased C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate, despite no demonstrable type I or III endoleak. Additional endovascular reinforcement and intensified immunosuppressive therapy were performed. A type II endoleak from the left first lumbar artery was subsequently detected, but the aneurysm continued to regress under inflammatory control. More than 13 years after the initial repair, the treated aneurysm remains completely regressed. CONCLUSIONS: This case suggests that sac enlargement after endovascular repair for a Behçet-related aortic aneurysm should be evaluated as a potentially multifactorial event, including occult endoleak, persistent sac pressurization, stent-graft-related mechanical factors, and systemic inflammatory activity. In this case, durable stabilization was observed following combined endovascular treatment and sustained immunosuppressive therapy.

Endovascular repair is increasingly used for Behçet-related aortic lesions, but the long-term interaction between aneurysm remodeling, endoleak, and systemic inflammatory activity remains clinically important. title: Silymarin attenuates neuroinflammation after subarachnoid hemorrhage by inducing M2 microglial polarization via activation of the JAK1/STAT6 signaling pathway.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Neuroinflammation represents a key pathological process in early brain injury (EBI) following subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) and contributes significantly to poor outcomes. Silymarin, known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant activities, has been shown to exert neuroprotective effects. Nevertheless, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain to be clarified. An in vivo endovascular perforation model and an in vitro hemoglobin-stimulated model were used to investigate the pharmacological effects of silymarin in SAH. Neurological function was assessed using SAH scores and neurobehavioral scores. Neuronal apoptosis was evaluated by TUNEL staining. Neuroinflammation was measured by ELISA or qPCR, and microglial polarization status was determined by assessing CD86 and CD206 expression via Western blotting (WB) or immunofluorescence (IF) staining. Ruxolitinib and AS1517499 were applied to block the JAK1/STAT6 pathway. Silymarin attenuated early brain injury (EBI) after SAH, as indicated by improved neurological scores, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and lower brain water content. In vivo, silymarin treatment was associated with JAK1/STAT6 activation, elevated M2 markers, and decreased pro‑inflammatory cytokines. In vitro, silymarin activated the JAK1/STAT6 pathway, promoted M2 microglial polarization, and suppressed inflammatory cytokine production. In addition, pharmacological blockade of JAK1/STAT6 reversed silymarin's protective effects, confirming a causal role of this pathway in the cellular context. Our in vitro data demonstrate that silymarin directly stimulates JAK1/STAT6 to drive M2 polarization and anti‑inflammatory responses. In vivo, we observed a correlation between pathway activation and neuroprotective benefits. Together, these findings provide a rationale for further exploring silymarin‑based therapies in SAH. title: Renal pseudoaneurysm and arterial-pelvicalyceal fistula after partial nephrectomy managed with staged angioembolization: A case report.
abstract: Delayed haemorrhage after partial nephrectomy is usually attributed to a single vascular lesion and controlled by transarterial embolization. A 62-year-old man developed massive haematuria one week after left partial nephrectomy. CT angiography showed a segmental renal pseudoaneurysm, which was embolised superselectively. Bleeding recurred within 24 hours; repeat angiography revealed a separate arterial-pelvicalyceal fistula, treated by a second embolization with durable haemostasis. Recurrence after apparently successful embolization may therefore reflect a second, unrecognised lesion rather than treatment failure. A low threshold for repeat angiography and staged, lesion-specific embolization can achieve definitive control while preserving renal parenchyma.

title: Factors associated with failures and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters in hospitalized COVID-19 patients.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: to analyze factors associated with catheter progression failure and outcomes of Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters inserted by nurses in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. METHOD: observational cohort study was conducted with hospitalized COVID-19 patients, following the STROBE guidelines. Categorical variables were described as absolute and relative frequencies; quantitative variables were expressed as median and interquartile range. Non-parametric tests were applied due to non-normal distribution. Associations were analyzed using Pearson's chi-squared or Fisher's exact tests. Logistic regression was performed for variables associated with outcomes. RESULTS: a total of 1061 Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters were analyzed. The main indications were for antibiotic therapy, and most catheters were removed after treatment completion. First-attempt failure and clinical patient profile were associated with catheter progression failure. Subcutaneous heparin was a protective factor. Among Peripherally Inserted Central Catheters successfully inserted, tip confirmation via chest X-ray and catheter-to-vessel ratio between 31%-40% were associated with thrombosis, whereas Sherlock™ confirmation was protective. CONCLUSION: catheter progression failure was associated with clinical conditions and first-attempt failure. Adverse outcomes were associated with X-ray tip confirmation and catheter-to-vessel ratio, whereas Sherlock™ use and subcutaneous heparin were protective factors.

title: Staged limb salvage after an infected full-thickness shoulder-girdle flame burn with osteoarticular exposure in an elderly patient: A case report with 3.5-year follow-up.
abstract: RATIONALE: In extensive shoulder-girdle burns, the critical question may not be flap selection itself, but whether meaningful limb salvage remains justified, particularly in an elderly, frail patient with a delayed infection but preserved distal neurovascular function. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 73-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and cachexia (body mass index, 16.9 kg/m2) was transferred approximately 3 weeks after a flame burn. She presented with an extensive infected wound extending from the neck base to the distal third of the left arm. DIAGNOSES: The burn extended through deep soft tissues to the shoulder capsule, rotator cuff, proximal humerus, scapula, and acromioclavicular and glenohumeral regions, consistent with a fourth-degree injury. Cultures grew Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii. No injury to the brachial plexus and major vessels was identified. Sepsis could not be retrospectively classified. INTERVENTIONS: Following systemic and nutritional optimization, culture-directed antibiotics, 6 serial debridements, and negative-pressure wound therapy at -125 mm Hg, the infection was clinically controlled. Four weeks after admission, the defect was reconstructed with a 20 × 15 cm ipsilateral pedicled latissimus dorsi myocutaneous flap and skin grafting. OUTCOMES: The flap survived completely without significant donor-site complications. At 3.5 years, the wound remained healed without recurrent drainage, ulceration, or further surgery. Active shoulder motion remained markedly limited, whereas passive shoulder motion and distal upper-extremity function were near those of the contralateral side. The patient remained independent in daily activities, with a disabilities of the arm, shoulder and hand score of 28/100. LESSONS: Preserved distal neurovascular function and realistic residual-limb utility may justify staged salvage despite severe shoulder destruction. The favorable outcome reflects careful patient selection, stabilization, debridement, infection control, and durable vascularized coverage rather than the superiority of a specific flap or a general recommendation to delay reconstruction.

title: Central retinal artery occlusion preceding hemispheric ischemic stroke treated with mechanical thrombectomy: A case report.
abstract: RATIONALE: Central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) is a form of ischemic stroke that may signal underlying cerebrovascular or cardiac disease. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 52-year-old man developed sudden, painless vision loss in the right eye. Nine days later, he presented with left-sided weakness and speech difficulty, with a National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score of 8. His medical history included dilated cardiomyopathy, and electrocardiography revealed atrial fibrillation. DIAGNOSES: Ophthalmologic examination and fluorescein angiography supported right CRAO. Computed tomography (CT) angiography at neurological presentation showed right internal carotid artery occlusion from its origin. CT perfusion demonstrated estimated infarct core and penumbral volumes of 37 and 186 mL, respectively. INTERVENTIONS: Emergency mechanical thrombectomy with aspiration and adjunctive balloon angioplasty achieved expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction grade 2c reperfusion. OUTCOMES: The NIHSS score improved to 2 at discharge, 7 days after admission. At 3 months, the modified Rankin Scale score was 1, although right-eye visual loss persisted. LESSONS: CRAO warrants prompt cerebrovascular and cardiac evaluation, with reassessment when new neurological deficits develop. The nine-day interval between retinal symptoms and thrombectomy does not establish the duration of carotid occlusion or cerebral ischemia. The favorable individual outcome does not establish the efficacy of thrombectomy beyond 24 hours.

title: A case report of pulmonary embolism following endoscopic cervical discectomy in an elderly patient with cervical disc herniation.
abstract: RATIONALE: Posterior percutaneous endoscopic cervical discectomy (P-PECD) is a minimally invasive procedure for cervical spine disorders. Although it is associated with less surgical trauma and faster postoperative recovery, serious perioperative thromboembolic complications may still occur. PATIENT CONCERNS: A 65-year-old woman with cervical disc herniation, right upper limb pain, and multiple comorbidities underwent posterior percutaneous endoscopic cervical discectomy after unsuccessful conservative treatment. On the 2nd postoperative day, she developed dizziness and decreased oxygen saturation. On the 3rd postoperative day, she complained of chest tightness. DIAGNOSES: Laboratory testing revealed a markedly elevated plasma D-dimer level. Venous color Doppler ultrasound of both lower limbs demonstrated thrombosis in the bilateral calf muscular veins, and computed tomography pulmonary angiography confirmed multiple pulmonary emboli. INTERVENTIONS: The patient received oxygen therapy, continuous cardiorespiratory monitoring, anticoagulation with low-molecular-weight heparin, and other supportive treatments. She was transferred to the intensive care unit for further monitoring and management. OUTCOMES: The patient's respiratory and circulatory status gradually stabilized, and her chest tightness and dizziness resolved. She was subsequently transferred back to the pain ward and discharged in stable condition. LESSONS: This case highlights that minimally invasive spinal surgery does not eliminate the risk of perioperative venous thromboembolism. Comprehensive preoperative thrombotic risk assessment, individualized perioperative management of antithrombotic therapy, appropriate thromboprophylaxis, early mobilization, and timely recognition and treatment of suspected APE are important for improving perioperative safety.

Although it is associated with less surgical trauma and faster postoperative recovery, serious perioperative thromboembolic complications may still occur. title: Rifampicin-soaked versus bovine prostheses in the management of aortic graft infections: a retrospective single-center cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic vascular graft and endograft infections (aortic VGEI) remain a rare but life-threatening complication following aortic reconstruction. This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed 62 patients between January 2018 and December 2025 for aortic vascular graft or endograft infection requiring graft explantation and in-situ reconstruction. Patients received either a bovine pericardial graft (n=21) or a rifampicin-soaked Dacron prosthesis (n=41). Survival, treatment failure, perioperative variables, and microbiology were analyzed. RESULTS: Patients in the bovine and rifampicin groups were comparable in terms of age (72.57 vs. 73.58 years, p = 0.685) and sex distribution (85.71% vs. 73.17% male, p = 0.346). BMI, preoperative dialysis, and aortic clamping time were higher in the bovine group. Four treatment failures, defined as persistent or recurrent infection of the reconstructed aortic segment, occurred during follow-up; all were observed after reconstruction with rifampicin-soaked Dacron (4/41, 9.8%), whereas no treatment failure occurred in the bovine pericardial group (0/21). In-hospital mortality was comparable between groups (n=3:14.3% vs. n=8: 19.5%, p = 0.735). Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated no significant difference in survival (p = 0.256) or treatment failure rate (p = 0.833). Candida spp. were the most frequent pathogens (27.8%) and significantly associated with secondary aorto-enteric fistula (p=0.003). CONCLUSION: Survival and treatment failure rates were comparable, with a trend toward fewer infection-related complications after bovine pericardial grafting. Despite use in more complex cases, bovine grafts may represent a promising biological alternative.

This retrospective study compares outcomes between bovine pericardial graft prostheses and rifampicin-soaked Dacron grafts. METHODS: In this retrospective single-center cohort study, we analyzed 62 patients between January 2018 and December 2025 for aortic vascular graft or endograft infection requiring graft explantation and in-situ reconstruction.

title: Evaluation of morphometric characteristics and positional variations of the carotid sinus using computed tomography angiography.
abstract: PURPOSE: The aim of this study was to determine the morphometric characteristics and spatial variations of the carotid sinus (CS) using computed tomography angiography (CTA) images. METHODS: In the study, cervical CTA images of a total of 100 individuals (200 sides) comprising 55 men and 45 women were examined. The diameters of the proximal and distal segments of the common carotid artery (CCA) and the internal carotid artery (ICA), as well as the proximal diameter of the external carotid artery (ECA), were measured. In addition, measurements of the maximum transverse diameter and length of the CS were taken; the resulting data were compared according to the variables of age, gender and side. RESULTS: All artery diameters, CS length (mean 8.78 ± 1.33 mm), and maximum CS diameter (mean 8.27 ± 1.10 mm) were found to be significantly higher in men than in women (p < 0.001). It was determined that the diameters of the CCA and ICA on the left side were statistically significantly wider than those on the right side (p < 0.001). It was found that CS localization was asymmetric in 29% of cases and most commonly occurred in the proximal ICA (Type I) in 74.5% of cases. In addition, a positive and statistically significant correlation (r = 0.554; p < 0.001) was found between age and CS length. CONCLUSION: Understanding the morphological variations of the CS is of critical importance in preventing unintended CS stimulation and related complications during surgical procedures in this region, particularly carotid endarterectomy.

METHODS: In the study, cervical CTA images of a total of 100 individuals (200 sides) comprising 55 men and 45 women were examined. The diameters of the proximal and distal segments of the common carotid artery (CCA) and the internal carotid artery (ICA), as well as the proximal diameter of the external carotid artery (ECA), were measured.

title: Profound thrombocytopenia and transient leucoerythroblastosis following hip fracture surgery.
abstract: 9 An elderly man underwent hip fracture surgery with pre-/postoperative heparin anticoagulation; the platelet count fell to 5×10/L (nadir); haematopathology blood film review identified leucoerythroblastosis (circulating normoblasts, leucocyte left-shift) and schistocytosis (red cell fragments). Although screening platelet factor 4 (PF4)/heparin enzyme-immunoassay for heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) antibodies yielded a strong-positive result, the confirmatory serotonin-release assay gave an atypical profile (strong serum-induced serotonin-release but only partial inhibition by platelet Fc receptor-blocking monoclonal antibody). Bilateral lower-limb deep-vein thrombosis prompted treatment with therapeutic-dose fondaparinux and high-dose intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG) for presumptive ‘autoimmune HIT’ (aHIT), that is, HIT featuring both heparin-dependent and heparin-independent platelet-activating anti-PF4/heparin antibodies. Persistent thrombocytopenia, recurrent fibrinogen decrease and d-dimer increase indicated refractoriness to IVIG, with pulmonary embolism also identified; ultimately, additional IVIG was followed by complete recovery. Further laboratory evaluation confirmed a diagnosis of severe aHIT. A novel finding was the transient appearance of leucoerythroblastosis, compatible with overt disseminated intravascular complicating severe aHIT.

title: Chronic thoracic aortitis versus primary medial degeneration in ascending aorta: a digital morphometric analysis of aortic layers remodelling.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Chronic aortitis (CA) represents a diverse group of inflammatory conditions often diagnosed incidentally in ascending aorta biopsies. While the 2015 and 2016 Consensus Statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta provide standardised histological classifications, data quantifying structural remodelling within individual aortic layers remain limited. Furthermore, distinguishing CA from primary non-inflammatory medial degeneration (MD) can be challenging, particularly when inflammation is sparse or burnt out, and secondary degenerative changes predominate. We aimed to compare morphological changes in CA and MD aneurysms and apply digital image analysis to quantify aortic wall layers. METHODS: Retrospective histological analysis was performed on 63 ascending aortic specimens: CA (n=21), MD (n=21), and autopsy controls (n=21). Digitised elastic-stained sections were analysed using QuPath software to measure the thickness and cross-sectional area of the intima (I), media (M), and adventitia (A). Overall MD scores (i.e., summaries of each MD grade component) were evaluated. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis based on binary logistic regression models. RESULTS: CA demonstrated a profound architectural shift, characterised by medial thinning alongside marked intimal and adventitial expansion, resulting in significantly lower M/(I+A) thickness and area ratios compared with MD and controls (p <0.001). CA specimens also exhibited the most severe secondary degenerative changes, with significantly higher overall MD scores (median: 15 vs. 8; p < 0.001). ROC curve analysis revealed diagnostic utility of both the M/(I+A) thickness ratio (AUC = 0.964) and the M/(I+A) area ratio (AUC = 0.955) for identifying CA. A multivariable model combining the overall MD score with the M/(I+A) thickness ratio achieved an AUC of 0.971 (accuracy 88.1%), whereas combining it with the M/(I+A) area ratio yielded an AUC of 0.968 (accuracy 90.5%). CONCLUSION: Digital morphometric analysis provides a reproducible and feasible method for quantifying structural remodelling in chronic aortitis. Changes in the proportions of the aortic layers, specifically intimal and adventitial expansion combined with medial thinning and severe secondary medial degeneration, can facilitate accurate differentiation of aortic wall pathologies, particularly in cases with sparse inflammation.

While the 2015 and 2016 Consensus Statements on the surgical pathology of the aorta provide standardised histological classifications, data quantifying structural remodelling within individual aortic layers remain limited. Furthermore, distinguishing CA from primary non-inflammatory medial degeneration (MD) can be challenging, particularly when inflammation is sparse or burnt out, and secondary degenerative changes predominate.

title: Lesion Water Content on CT Predicts 12-Month Outcome and Modifies Thrombectomy Effect in Large-Core Stroke-A Secondary Analysis of the TENSION Trial.
abstract: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment. The primary outcome was ordinal 12-month mRS. Multivariable ordinal and logistic regression tested associations and the NWU × EVT interaction, with discrimination assessed by area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Median baseline NWU was 16.4% and NWUFU 28.9%. At 12 months, 45 patients (23%) had mRS 0-3 and 111 (56%) had died. Higher baseline NWU independently predicted worse 12-month mRS (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR], 1.10 per percentage-point; 95% CI, 1.05-1.16; P < 0.001) and modified the EVT effect (interaction acOR, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.06-1.30; P = 0.002), with greater discrimination than ASPECTS. NWUFU was the strongest single imaging predictor (acOR, 1.10; 95% CI, 1.06-1.14; P < 0.001; AUC, 0.78 for mRS 0-3) and superseded baseline NWU when co-modeled. Among 97 90-day survivors, higher NWUFU independently predicted late mortality (adjusted odds ratio, 1.09; 95% CI, 1.02-1.18; P = 0.019). Lesion water content may therefore provide a clinically accessible CT biomarker linking treatment-modifiable injury at baseline with realized post-treatment injury and long-term outcome.
englishSummary: In large-core ischemic stroke, outcomes after thrombectomy remain heterogeneous, and imaging markers that capture treatment-modifiable injury beyond lesion extent are needed. We investigated whether lesion water content on noncontrast CT, quantified as net water uptake (NWU), predicts 12-month functional outcome and modifies the effect of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). This secondary analysis of the randomized TENSION trial included 198 patients with admission CT suitable for NWU quantification and available 12-month modified Rankin Scale (mRS) scores; 168 had paired 24-h CT for follow-up NWU (NWUFU) assessment.

title: AI-enhanced intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery: from augmented reality navigation to foundation models.
abstract: Robotic surgical platforms have improved instrument dexterity, tremor filtration, and ergonomic control, yet intraoperative decisions still depend on a surgeon interpreting a moving, partially observed field under time pressure. Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used to close parts of this loop by recognizing anatomy, tracking instruments, anticipating events, and-experimentally-planning or executing selected actions. This review maps the computational technologies that support intraoperative decision-making in robotic surgery and appraises the clinical evidence for them.Because the direct robotic evidence base is still uneven, we explicitly distinguish three kinds of material: (i) studies conducted on robotic systems during surgery; (ii) non-robotic surgical evidence from laparoscopic and thoracoscopic procedures that use the same vision and workflow methods; and (iii) preclinical, preoperative, and perioperative work that is conceptually relevant but not intraoperative. Robotic and non-robotic settings are labeled throughout the tables and text. We further separate non-AI image guidance-indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence and registered overlays-from AI-based inference, and we include image-guided endovascular robotics as a complementary setting in which fluoroscopic perception, vascular-topology reasoning, and closed-loop instrument control are particularly advanced.We organize the field into four computational layers: perception, anatomical and procedural reasoning, action planning, and control and execution. Augmented-reality and fluorescence navigation can improve orientation and selected intermediate outcomes, and several randomized trials now exist. Computer-vision systems can recognize anatomy, phases, instruments, and adverse events, and in endovascular work they can track guidewires and reason over vascular topology. Foundation models broaden language and multimodal capabilities but remain, in surgery, largely preclinical. Autonomous subtasks have shown promise in phantoms, animals, and a small number of carefully bounded tissue tasks; no system has demonstrated safe, accountable patient-level autonomous decision-making.Navigation and AI-assisted systems have improved orientation, reduced ischemia, and accelerated recognition of critical events in some studies. Whether these intermediate gains improve patient outcomes, generalize across institutions, or justify their cost remains unknown. The question is not whether AI can interpret surgical scenes, but which decisions can be delegated, with what evidence, uncertainty limits, oversight, and outcome measures.

title: Mechanical and Hemodynamic Effects of Balloon-Expandable and Self-Expanding Stents in a Saccular Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Model: Fluid-Structure Interaction Analyses.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare the effects of balloon-expandable and self-expanding stents on vessel wall mechanics and hemodynamics in a patient-specific saccular abdominal aortic aneurysm model. METHODS: A patient-specific aneurysm model was constructed using computed tomography images, and balloon-expandable and self-expanding stent models were created. Aortic wall stress was evaluated by contact analysis. Fluid-structure interaction analyses were performed at 5 representative phases selected from the cardiac cycle. Mean intra-aneurysmal flow velocity, wall shear stress (WSS), pressure loss, and energy loss were compared. RESULTS: The balloon-expandable stent produced greater localized aortic wall stress than the self-expanding stent, whereas wall stress was more uniformly distributed with the self-expanding stent. Both stents reduced the mean intra-aneurysmal flow velocity, WSS, pressure loss, and energy loss compared with the no-stent model. However, greater reductions in WSS, pressure loss, and energy loss were noted with the balloon-expandable stent than with the self-expanding stent. CONCLUSIONS: Balloon-expandable and self-expanding stents exhibited different effects on vessel wall mechanics and hemodynamics. The findings indicate the importance of evaluating both hemodynamic and mechanical effects when assessing stent-vessel interactions.

METHODS: A patient-specific aneurysm model was constructed using computed tomography images, and balloon-expandable and self-expanding stent models were created. Aortic wall stress was evaluated by contact analysis.

title: Simple Site, Serious Sequelae: Septic Emboli from a Peripheral Cannula.
abstract: PRESENTATION: A young female patient presented with right arm pain and pleuritic chest pain following recent hospitalisation. Investigations demonstrated marked inflammation (CRP 296 mg/L, WCC 13.7 ×10⁹/L). DAIGNOSIS: She was diagnosed with multiple septic pulmonary emboli (SPE) secondary to cephalic vein thrombophlebitis and cellulitis at a previous cannula site. TREATMENT: Despite prolonged intravenous antibiotics, she later developed culture-proven septic arthritis requiring washout and further treatment. DISCUSSION: Peripheral venous cannula-associated SPE remain rarely reported.

title: Cannabis legalisation and cardiovascular hospitalisations in the United States: nationwide difference-in-differences analysis, 2012-2018.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To determine the association between legal recreational cannabis sales (hereafter ‘legalisation’) and cardiovascular hospitalisations. This study leverages a natural experiment wherein legalisation began earlier in the Western census region of the United States (January 2014) versus non-Western regions (November 2018). DESIGN: Using the National Inpatient Sample (NIS), we performed a difference-in-differences analysis of the association between legalisation and hospitalisation rates for six cardiovascular diagnoses, a positive control (cannabis-related diagnoses) and two negative control diagnoses (opioid-related and urinary stones). SETTING: US states before (2012–2013) and after (2014–2018) legalisation in the Western region PARTICIPANTS: Hospitalised individuals in the Western region had a median age of 51 years, 57% were female and 43% were non-white. In other regions, the median age was 55 years, 57% were female and 33% were non-white. EXPOSURE: Legal recreational cannabis sales. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASUREMENTS: Annual hospitalisations per capita for atrial fibrillation/flutter (AF), heart failure (HF), myocardial infarction (MI), ischaemic stroke, venous thromboembolism (VTE) and ventricular tachycardia (VT). RESULTS: In this fully adjusted analysis, each year of legalisation was associated with the following relative change in hospitalisation rates expressed as change in the incidence rate ratio (∆IRR): cannabis-related diagnoses (∆IRR 1.138, 95% CI 1.066 to 1.214, p<0.001), AF (∆IRR 1.023, 95% CI 1.010 to 1.035, p<0.001), HF (∆IRR 1.037, 95% CI 1.029 to 1.046, p<0.001), MI (∆IRR 1.031, 95% CI 1.014 to 1.048, p<0.001), ischaemic stroke (∆IRR 1.011, 95% CI 0.999 to 1.024, p=0.078), VTE (∆IRR 1.009, 95% CI 0.999 to 1.020, p=0.066) and VT (∆IRR 1.019, 95% CI 0.993 to 1.046, p=0.161). For falsification testing, there was no change in hospitalisations for urinary stones (∆IRR 1.006, 95% CI 0.986 to 1.027, p=0.535) or opioid-related diagnoses (∆IRR 0.966, 95% CI 0.927 to 1.006, p=0.091). CONCLUSIONS: Legalisation was associated with increased hospitalisations for AF, HF and MI. Global legalisation trends may result in epidemiologically and economically important increases in cardiovascular healthcare use.

This study leverages a natural experiment wherein legalisation began earlier in the Western census region of the United States (January 2014) versus non-Western regions (November 2018). title: Percutaneous joint preparation for tibiotalocalcaneal arthrodesis: a case series.
abstract: PURPOSE: Tibiotalocalcaneal (TTC) arthrodesis is a limb-salvaging procedure for end-stage ankle and hindfoot pathology but carries substantial risks of nonunion and complications. Minimally invasive approaches may reduce surgical morbidity while maintaining fusion outcomes. METHODS: This was a retrospective case series of patients who underwent TTC arthrodesis with percutaneous joint preparation between January 2020 and March 2025 at a single academic Level II trauma center. The primary outcome was radiographic or clinical fusion at final follow-up. Secondary outcomes included alignment, operative variables, complications, and functional recovery as measured by Patient Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) domains. RESULTS: 2 Thirteen patients (six females) met inclusion criteria with a mean age of 74.0 years and body mass index of 27.1 kg/m. The mean time from injury to surgery in trauma patients was 6.2 days. Fibular fixation was performed in six cases (46.2%), with additional fixation necessary in select patients. Mean clinical follow-up time was 15.0 ± 4.3 months. Most patients advanced to weightbearing in supportive footwear and reported functional improvement. PROMIS Pain Interference averaged 56.8 ± 10.9, Physical Function 37.7 ± 12.2, and Global Pain 38.7 ± 28.9. Radiographs and computed tomography demonstrated moderate fusion rates in this cohort. Complications included wound issues (23.1%), hardware problems (46.2%), and one tibial shaft fracture after a fall; five patients required secondary screw removal. CONCLUSION: Percutaneous TTC arthrodesis demonstrated moderate radiographic fusion rates, functional improvement, and an acceptable complication profile for this cohort of predominantly elderly, medically complex patients.

Minimally invasive approaches may reduce surgical morbidity while maintaining fusion outcomes. METHODS: This was a retrospective case series of patients who underwent TTC arthrodesis with percutaneous joint preparation between January 2020 and March 2025 at a single academic Level II trauma center.

title: Critical-sized bone defects: essential concepts for the higher orthopaedic examination.
abstract: PURPOSE: To provide a practical review of the assessment and management of critical-sized bone defects (CSDs) for candidates preparing for higher orthopaedic examinations. METHODS: This narrative review considers definitions and classification, clinical assessment, acute management, reconstructive techniques and salvage options. RESULTS: A critical-sized bone defect (CSD) is unlikely to heal without intervention because of its size and location, although no numerical threshold defines criticality. Assessment should consider skeletal stability, infection, vascularity, soft tissues, host factors and likely function. After resuscitation, priorities include debridement, skeletal stabilisation and soft-tissue cover. Definitive bone loss should be assessed after debridement, which may require multiple operations. Reconstruction may be single-stage or staged. Options include bone grafting or acute shortening in selected cases, bone transport, the induced-membrane technique and vascularised bone transfer. Patient-specific implants show promise, but long-term evidence is limited. Planning should involve an orthoplastic team, with microbiology input if infection is suspected. Amputation should be considered if reconstruction is unlikely to yield a functional limb. CONCLUSION: Successful management requires infection control, stable fixation and reliable soft-tissue cover. The reconstructive approach should reflect the defect and the patient's circumstances, balancing likely functional benefit against the burden of treatment.

title: Determinants of Futile Recanalization and the Influence of Age After Endovascular Therapy for Acute Ischemic Stroke: A Retrospective Single-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods Results n n Conclusions : Functional independence is not always achieved after successful recanalization with endovascular therapy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke, a phenomenon termed futile recanalization (FR). We investigated factors independently associated with FR and explored whether these associations differed by age.: In this retrospective single-center study, 231 consecutive patients treated with EVT between January 2021 and December 2024 were analyzed. FR was defined as a modified Rankin Scale score > 2 at 90 days despite a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) grade of 2b-3. Model 1 included all patients with successful recanalization. Model 2 was restricted to patients with anterior circulation infarction and assessable imaging and additionally included the Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) and collateral status. Age interactions were tested.: Recanalization was successful in 191 patients (82.7%), of whom 114 (59.7%) had FR. In Model 1 (= 191), admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) score (odds ratio [OR], 1.29 per point; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.18-1.42), admission glucose (OR, 1.01; 1.00-1.02), and puncture-to-recanalization time (OR, 1.02; 1.00-1.03) were independently associated with FR. In Model 2 (= 146), sufficient collateral status (OR, 0.19; 0.08-0.47), ASPECTS (OR, 0.60; 0.39-0.91), NIHSS score, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), dyslipidemia, and procedural duration were independently associated with FR, whereas glucose was not retained; Model 2 had an area under the curve of 0.88. Age ≥ 80 years was not independently associated with FR; the only significant interaction was with glucose in Model 1.: Stroke severity and procedural duration were independently associated with FR in both models. Imaging variables contributed to prognostic assessment in anterior circulation infarction. Age ≥ 80 years was not independently associated with FR. The NLR association and age-stratified findings remain exploratory.

title: Circulating Lipids, Statins, and Metformin in Thoracic and Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: I I 2 2 Thoracic and abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAA and AAA) progress silently, and no drug has been shown to slow their growth. Circulating lipids, statins, and metformin are candidate disease modifiers, but the evidence is heterogeneous and largely observational. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 24 March 2025, with an update of MEDLINE to 3 October 2026, for randomized and cohort studies of adults with established AAA or TAA. Aneurysm growth was standardized to mm/year and pooled with random-effects models when at least three comparable studies were available. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed with ROBINS-I and GRADE. Thirty-three studies were included, 32 observational and one randomized; fewer than 20% of participants were women. Circulating lipid fractions showed no consistent association with aneurysm growth. Statin use was associated with slower growth (mean difference -0.78 mm/year; 95% CI -1.13 to -0.43;= 92.4%; 95% prediction interval -2.02 to 0.46 mm/year), lower all-cause mortality, and fewer aortic complications. In AAA, metformin use was associated with slower growth in observational studies (-0.34 mm/year; 95% CI -0.48 to -0.20;= 46.3%), while the single randomized trial found no difference. Certainty of evidence was low to very low. In these largely observational data, aneurysm progression was more closely related to statin and metformin use than to circulating lipid levels, a pattern that is hypothesis-generating and from which causality cannot be inferred.

Circulating lipids, statins, and metformin are candidate disease modifiers, but the evidence is heterogeneous and largely observational. We searched MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library from inception to 24 March 2025, with an update of MEDLINE to 3 October 2026, for randomized and cohort studies of adults with established AAA or TAA.

title: Point-of-Care Ultrasound Use in Confirmed Acute Aortic Syndrome: A Five-Year Retrospective Cohort Study at the Ljubljana Emergency Medical Unit.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p p p p p Point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) is increasingly used in emergency care, but data on its use in acute aortic syndrome (AAS) remains limited. This single-center retrospective cohort described POCUS use among patients with confirmed AAS and explored factors associated with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup.Records coded ICD10 I71.0-I71.8 from the Emergency Medical Unit, University Medical Centre Ljubljana (2019-2023) were reviewed. Clinical, imaging, and outcome data were extracted, and diagnoses were confirmed by two investigators through manual chart review of ED documentation, radiology reports, and specialist consultation notes. Fisher's exact and Wilcoxon rank sum tests were used for comparisons. Associations with POCUS use and time to completion of diagnostic workup (defined from arrival at triage to completion of the emergency department workup) were assessed with univariable logistic regression and linear regression models, respectively. Survival was explored using univariable Cox proportional-hazards models. Statistical significance was set at< 0.05.Among 120,109 emergency department visits, 73 patients had confirmed AAS (type A: 48; type B: 17; intramural hematoma: 8). POCUS was performed in 62% of patients, more often in those who were hemodynamically unstable (87.5% vs. 54.4%;= 0.020) or had unclear presentations (40% vs. 7%;= 0.003). Median time to completion of diagnostic workup was shorter with POCUS (110 vs. 213 min), though not statistically significant (= 0.069). Hemodynamic instability was associated with higher odds of POCUS use (OR 5.87, 95% CI 1.22-28.2;= 0.028), whereas a clear clinical presentation was associated with lower odds of POCUS use (OR 0.12, 95% CI 0.02-0.55;= 0.007). Lower triage level was associated with longer time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 5.43, 95% CI 2.21-13.4;< 0.001 for urgent vs. immediate triage), whereas very high D-dimer levels were associated with shorter time to completion of diagnostic workup (time ratio 0.44, 95% CI 0.21-0.93;= 0.031 for highest vs. lowest quartile). In-hospital mortality was 14%, with only age associated with mortality (HR 1.06 per year, 95% CI 1.02-1.11;= 0.007).In this single-center retrospective AAS cohort, POCUS was used more frequently in unstable and diagnostically unclear patients but was not associated with time to completion of diagnostic workup. Findings are descriptive and exploratory; they do not establish that POCUS accelerates diagnosis or improves outcomes.

title: Intraoperative Measurement of Internal Carotid Artery Blood Flow Using Transit-Time Flowmetry After Carotid Endarterectomy: Results from 196 Consecutive Cases.
abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions p p : Carotid endarterectomy (CEA) is a standard surgical treatment for high-grade symptomatic and asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis. The Transit Time Flowmeter (TTF) provides an easy-to-use tool to quantify intraoperative ICA blood flow in mL/min. This study aimed to (1) describe post-CEA ICA flow quantified with TTF, (2) identify predictors of post-CEA ICA flow, and (3) examine its association with contralateral steno-occlusive disease.: We queried data from our prospective registry of patients who underwent a CEA between January 2019 and July 2024 and had intraoperative registered post-CEA ICA flow measurements using TTF. Preoperative ICA stenosis was graded according to the NASCET criteria. The clinical data was retrospectively collected.: Data from 196 CEAs in 190 patients (median age 74 [67-81]; 25% female) were included. Most patients (86%) had a symptomatic ICA stenosis. The median post-CEA ICA flow was 170 mL/min [IQR 140-242; range 40-800]. Post-CEA ICA flow was not associated with age, sex, comorbidities, symptomatic stenosis, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), or ipsilateral stenosis severity but was significantly higher in patients requiring intraluminal shunt placement during CEA (= 0.010) as well as in those with contralateral steno-occlusive disease (< 0.001).: TTF is a practical intraoperative tool for quantitative flow assessment during CEA. Higher post-CEA ICA flow in patients with an intraoperative shunt placement or with contralateral steno-occlusive disease may reflect a compensatory hyperperfusion, as the ipsilateral ICA serves as a key supplier when collateral pathways are incomplete.

title: Understanding Venous Remodeling After Minimally Invasive and Noninvasive Treatments for Varicose Veins: A Mechanistic Narrative Review.
abstract: The absence of detectable flow on duplex ultrasound after venous ablation may correspond to different tissue states. This mechanistic narrative review examines histopathological and immunohistochemical responses after thermal, chemical, mechanochemical, adhesive, and focused ultrasound treatments. The PubMed search, conducted on 6 September 2026 for publications available through 31 August 2026, resulted in the inclusion of 45 tissue-based publications; six additional references provided clinical context. Study selection and data extraction were performed by a single author. Human and experimental data were organized by wall compartment, treatment modality, and time point. Depending on the technique, the initial signatures comprised thermal injury, endothelial detergent toxicity, mechanical abrasion, adhesive polymerization, or cavitation. Luminal organization, fibrosis, and recanalization followed heterogeneous trajectories. Cyanoacrylate was distinguished by a biomaterial response with variable persistence. Early occlusion does not demonstrate mature fibrous obliteration. The depth-continuity-topography framework is a working hypothesis without validated predictive value. Combining longitudinal duplex ultrasound follow-up with end-point histological analysis of the same segment, including morphometry, immunohistochemistry, and matrix assessment, could better relate tissue status to clinical outcome.

title: Relationship Between Social Isolation, Loneliness, and Systemic Inflammation: A Scoping Review of Biological Signatures and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Social isolation and loneliness are established social determinants of health, associated with 25-30% higher mortality risk, yet their relationship with systemic inflammation and broader biological and clinical outcomes has not been comprehensively synthesized across life stages. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and ScienceDirect were searched (2015-2025), supplemented by citation searching and a targeted supplementary search, for human studies linking social isolation, loneliness, or social connectedness to inflammatory biomarkers or biological/clinical outcomes. PRISMA-ScR guidance was followed; findings were synthesized narratively across five thematic axes as an evidence map. RESULTS: n Of 3351 records identified, 73 studies were included. Isolation was most often associated with CRP and fibrinogen, and loneliness with IL-6. Isolation predicted sarcopenia, venous thromboembolism, pancreatic cancer, and cardiovascular disease, with inflammatory or metabolic markers mediating a modest (≈5-19%) share. Proteomic (= 42,062) and epigenetic analyses linked loneliness to inflammatory, antiviral, and complement-pathway proteins and to accelerated epigenetic ageing; Mendelian randomization supported causal involvement of several proteins. Social connectedness and relationship quality tracked with lower IL-6 and better functional indices. Evidence was strongest in midlife and older cohorts. CONCLUSIONS: Social disconnection shows biologically plausible but heterogeneous associations with inflammatory and molecular signatures; harmonized measurement and prospective, hypothesis-free omics designs are needed to clarify causality and inform targeted screening.

title: Co-occurrence of aortic dissection and polycystic kidney disease: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Aortic dissection is a rare and often fatal condition which arises when there is aortic wall weakening. Multiple risk factors could lead to this condition, including hypertension, atherosclerosis, connective tissue diseases such as Marfan's, Ehlers-Danlos and Loeys Dietz syndromes, as well as smoking, cocaine usage, bicuspid aortic valve, pregnancy and trauma. Polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is a rare condition characterized by the development of multiple renal cysts, which is caused by genetic abnormalities leading to autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive inheritance. However, the presentation of both pathologies simultaneously is rare and has been infrequently reported. CASE PRESENTATION: We report a death attributed to the co-occurrence of both conditions, involving a 19-year-old Caucasian male with no known past medical history, who collapsed during sexual intercourse. Post-mortem examination revealed hemopericardium with an aortic dissection, which was associated with PKD. The heart and the great vessels were sent to the author's place of practice for a detailed cardiovascular pathology examination. CONCLUSION: This case is a reminder to all forensic and clinical pathologists that an extremely uncommon manifestation can occur; therefore, a meticulous approach should always be adopted before corroborating a cause of death, especially in young individuals. The relationship between both conditions in this case remains uncertain; however, PKD may represent an associated finding and possibly a predisposing factor rather than a direct causal mechanism. The co-occurrence of both pathologies raises the likelihood of an underlying predisposition to vascular pathology and may have implications for the screening and clinical evaluation of surviving blood relatives.

title: Aspiration Thrombectomy for High-Risk Pulmonary Embolism With Life-Threatening Anemia and Active Uterine Bleeding: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND High-risk pulmonary embolism (PE) carries significant mortality, and management becomes complex when it coexists with severe anemia and active bleeding, as thrombolysis is then contraindicated. We report the case of a patient with high-risk PE complicated by severe anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L) and active uterine bleeding from adenomyosis. CASE REPORT A 48-year-old woman presented with haemodynamic instability (blood pressure 74/47 mm Hg), critical anemia (hemoglobin 41 g/L), and a 3-year history of irregular vaginal bleeding from adenomyosis. Computed tomography (CT) pulmonary angiography confirmed bilateral PE with right pulmonary artery main-trunk occlusion; echocardiography showed severe pulmonary hypertension, and duplex ultrasound showed extensive left lower-limb deep vein thrombosis. Thrombolysis was contraindicated. Emergency percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy was performed using large-bore catheters (22F, 20F, 16F) with concurrent inferior vena cava filter placement, reducing pulmonary artery pressure from 51/23 to 34/12 mm Hg; the estimated blood loss, quantified from filtered aspirate, was approximately 100 mL. Adjuncts included transfusion of 13 units of packed red cells, dilatation and curettage, gonadotropin-releasing hormone agonist therapy, and titrated anticoagulation. At discharge after a 24-day hospitalization she was hemodynamically stable, and free of dyspnea, with resolved edema and hemoglobin 72 g/L, on oral rivaroxaban. CONCLUSIONS In this thrombolysis-contraindicated patient, aspiration thrombectomy with inferior vena cava filter placement was a feasible rescue strategy that achieved rapid hemodynamic and angiographic improvement without thrombolysis, with palliative rather than curative intent. As a single case, it cannot establish comparative safety or efficacy, and broader conclusions regarding efficacy cannot be drawn. It illustrates a potentially useful approach in similarly complex scenarios where coordinated multidisciplinary care is essential.

title: Mental health in venous thromboembolism: A scoping review of the qualitative and quantitative evidence.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The effects of venous thromboembolism (VTE) on mental health have gained increasing awareness. We aimed to conduct a scoping review of the qualitative and quantitative evidence of mental health after VTE. MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and PsycInfo. The qualifying participant criteria was a VTE diagnosis, the principal concept was mental health. Studies investigating quality of life without a specific mental health focus were excluded. The outcome assessment was not restricted to specific methods. Quantitative analyses were not performed. RESULTS: Of 11,947 identified records, 104 were included. The first record dates to 1931, with a steep publication increase in the 2010s. Qualitative and mixed-methods studies (n = 37) were mostly conducted in high income countries and included vulnerable patient populations. Quantitative studies (n = 64) primarily focused on anxiety or depression but showed a high degree of heterogeneity. Several studies included VTE patients only as subgroups and no study was dedicated to prevention or treatment. We identified the following research gaps and recommendations: (1) harmonization of outcomes; (2) longitudinal outcome assessment; (3) expansion to vulnerable patient populations, such as patients with cancer, and lower income countries; (4) assessment and/or exclusion of pre-existing diagnoses or assessment of pre-VTE mental health; and (5) dedicated studies evaluating prevention and treatment of mental health disorders after VTE. CONCLUSIONS: Mental health sequelae after VTE have been investigated in various qualitative and quantitative studies. However, these studies are characterized by considerable heterogeneity and their clinical impact is limited due to the lack of investigations of prevention or treatment of mental health disorders after VTE.

title: Aspirin-Based Thromboprophylaxis Versus Anticoagulant Regimens After Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty: An Updated Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods Results Conclusions : Aspirin is widely used for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty (THA) and total knee arthroplasty (TKA); however, uncertainty remains regarding its efficacy and safety compared with anticoagulant regimens. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis versus anticoagulant regimens following THA or TKA.: PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) were searched through July 2026 for randomized controlled trials comparing aspirin-based prophylaxis with anticoagulant regimens. The primary outcomes were any deep vein thrombosis (DVT), symptomatic DVT, and symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE). Secondary outcomes included pulmonary embolism (PE), proximal and distal DVT, bleeding outcomes, wound complications, blood transfusion, and mortality. Risk ratios (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were pooled using random-effects models. Additional risk-difference sensitivity analyses incorporated CRISTAL's published cluster-adjusted estimates.: Sixteen trials involving 21,265 participants were included. Aspirin was associated with higher risks of symptomatic DVT (RR 1.79, 95% CI 1.35-2.38), symptomatic VTE (RR 1.70, 95% CI 1.33-2.18), PE (RR 1.89, 95% CI 1.33-2.68), and distal DVT (RR 1.47, 95% CI 1.06-2.06). Aspirin was associated with lower risks of minor bleeding (RR 0.47, 95% CI 0.31-0.71) and ecchymosis or bruising (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.39-0.93). No statistically significant differences were detected for the other assessed outcomes. Additional analyses incorporating CRISTAL's cluster-adjusted risk differences did not identify statistically significant differences for the three primary outcomes or PE.: The main pooled analyses associated aspirin-based thromboprophylaxis with higher risks of symptomatic thromboembolic events. However, the symptomatic DVT and symptomatic VTE associations were no longer statistically significant after exclusion of CRISTAL or restriction to trials at low risk of bias. The low-risk analysis identified a significantly higher risk of any DVT with aspirin. Aspirin reduced minor bleeding and bruising without a statistically significant reduction in major or clinically relevant non-major bleeding. These findings require cautious interpretation given dependence on CRISTAL, sensitivity to trial inclusion and analytical approach, and differences in prophylactic strategies and outcome definitions.

title: Direct Oral Anticoagulants in the Cardiorenal Patient: Pharmacology, Kidney Function Estimation and Dose Selection Across the CKD Spectrum.
abstract: Atrial fibrillation (AF) and chronic kidney disease (CKD) are not two coincident diseases but two expressions of the cardiorenal syndrome, the disorder in which dysfunction of the heart or the kidney induces dysfunction of the other. Their coexistence spans the chronic renocardiac and cardiorenal subtypes of that syndrome, and fits neither cleanly: the relationship is genuinely bidirectional, and each organ accelerates the deterioration of the other. Anticoagulation sits precisely at the point where this bidirectional relationship becomes a therapeutic dilemma: the same patient is simultaneously hypercoagulable and haemorrhagically fragile, and the drug intended to protect the brain is cleared by an organ whose function is both impaired and unstable. Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) have redefined therapeutic standards in AF and venous thromboembolism (VTE), offering predictable pharmacokinetics, fewer food and drug interactions and reduced monitoring requirements compared with vitamin K antagonists (VKAs). In the cardiorenal patient, however, these advantages are conditional. Renal elimination varies more than three-fold across the class-from approximately 27% for apixaban to approximately 80% for dabigatran-so that the choice of molecule, and not merely the decision to anticoagulate, becomes a kidney-related decision. The cardiorenal argument in favour of DOACs extends beyond bleeding: VKAs promote vascular calcification through inhibition of matrix Gla protein, are associated with calciphylaxis, and can cause anticoagulant-related nephropathy, an under-recognised cause of accelerated loss of glomerular filtration rate (GFR). Randomised and observational data indicate that GFR declines faster on VKAs than on DOACs, making the kidney an outcome of anticoagulation and not only a route of elimination. A second, largely unresolved problem is metrological rather than pharmacological. Dose thresholds for DOACs were derived from creatinine clearance (CrCl) estimated with the Cockcroft-Gault (CG) equation, whereas contemporary nephrology stages kidney disease with estimated GFR (eGFR) from the CKD-EPI or EKFC equations. The two quantities are not interchangeable, and the discordance between them translates directly into discordant doses in 4-34% of patients depending on the agent, with the largest discrepancies in the oldest patients and in those with the lowest measured function. This review reframes DOAC therapy as a cardiorenal problem. We examine the shared pathophysiological substrate of AF and CKD, the pharmacology of each agent through the lens of renal handling, the evidence across CKD stages G1-G5D including dialysis, the kidney as an outcome rather than only a covariate of anticoagulation, and the clinical consequences of the equation used to estimate kidney function at the point of prescription.

title: The effect of renal denervation on blood pressure in patients with chronic kidney disease (RDN-CKD Study): Results of a multicentre, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled and blinded investigator-initiated trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular ultrasound renal denervation (uRDN) offers the opportunity to modulate sympathetic nervous system activity, thereby lowering blood pressure (BP) and potentially improving or stabilizing renal outcomes. OBJECTIVE: We hypothesized that in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension, endovascular ultrasound-based RDN will lower BP after 6 months. METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, randomized, sham-controlled, blinded, clinical trial, investigated the effects of uRDN or sham in patients with CKD stage 3 and uncontrolled hypertension. The primary and secondary endpoints were changes in ambulatory BP (ABP) and office BP at 6 months. The study was prematurely stopped due to slow enrollment. RESULTS: Twenty subjects (uRDN: N = 10, sham: N = 10) completed the 6-month visit. At 6 months, the sham-corrected change from baseline in 24 h systolic ABP was -5.60 mmHg (95% CI -10.7, -0.54 mmHg; P = 0.170). The sham corrected change from baseline in 24-h diastolic ABP was -5.90 mmHg (95% CI -9.25, -2.55; P = 0.035) and from baseline daytime ABP -6.85 mmHg (95% CI -10.6, -3.08; P = 0.030). Sensitivity analysis restricting the analysis to those patients who were fully adherent to medication (N = 7 in each group) found a sham-corrected change from baseline 24-h diastolic ABP of -5.71 mmHg (95% CI -9.40, -2.03; P = 0.053) at 6 months. Based on the composite endpoint of 24 h ABP and office BP for systolic/diastolic BP, a win ratio of 1.71 (95% 1.26-2.34; P = 0.014) was found for systolic BP and a win ratio of 4.59 (95% CI 2.94-7.16, P < 0.001) was found for diastolic BP, indicating significant changes in BP following RDN. Estimated glomerular filtration rate remained stable over 6 months, with no difference between the groups. There were no safety signals associated with uRDN. CONCLUSIONS: This prospective randomized, sham controlled, blinded trial in patients with uncontrolled hypertension and CKD was prematurely stopped, resulted in small number of patients and we did not find a statistically significant effect on systolic BP, whereas a consistent reduction in diastolic BP following uRDN was observed. These data should guide the design of a larger confirmatory trial in patients with CKD.

title: Pulmonary hypertension and right ventricular dysfunction in hemodialysis: an overlooked cardiorenal interface and a target for dialysis prescription.
abstract: Pulmonary hypertension is an under-recognized cardiovascular complication of advanced chronic kidney disease, especially in maintenance hemodialysis. It links kidney failure, chronic volume stress, left-heart disease, pulmonary vascular remodeling, arteriovenous access flow, and right-ventricular dysfunction. This review frames pulmonary hypertension as central to the cardiorenal interface in hemodialysis and summarizes epidemiology, prognosis, mechanisms, diagnosis, and phenotyping. Echocardiography is the main screening tool, but pressure estimates should be interpreted according to dialysis timing and volume status. Right-heart catheterization remains essential to define phenotype and guide management. Treatment should target modifiable drivers: euvolemia without excessive ultrafiltration, optimized left-heart disease care, assessment of high-flow vascular access, and treatment of respiratory or hematologic contributors. Empirical pulmonary arterial hypertension-specific therapy should be avoided without hemodynamic confirmation. Pulmonary-artery denervation is promising in heart-failure pulmonary hypertension with mild to moderate CKD, but its role in hemodialysis remains unknown.

title: Adaptive Wound Care in Lower Extremity Amputation: From Rehabilitation to Athletic Performance.
abstract: Lower extremity amputation remains a significant clinical challenge, most commonly resulting from diabetes mellitus and peripheral arterial disease, and is associated with high morbidity and mortality. This review briefly summarizes the burden of lower extremity amputation and then focuses on individuals with transtibial amputation who use a prosthesis, with particular attention to residual limb health. Advances in prosthetic technology have improved functional outcomes and quality of life, enabling many individuals to achieve ambulation and, in some cases, return to high levels of physical activity. However, increased prosthetic use introduces unique challenges related to skin integrity, including friction, moisture, and pressure-related injuries within the prosthetic socket. These risks may be amplified in athletes with limb loss, who are exposed to higher mechanical and metabolic demands. This review introduces the concept of adaptive wound care, which emphasizes prevention, early detection, and management of residual limb skin complications in both general and athletic prosthesis users. Common injuries, including friction and shear injuries, pressure injuries, moisture-associated skin damage, folliculitis, contact dermatitis, volume-related injuries, and sport-related trauma, are described along with strategies for their prevention and treatment. Integrating surgical, prosthetic, rehabilitation, and wound care principles is essential to optimize outcomes, enhance function, and reduce complications following lower extremity amputation.

title: Challenges of Conducting a Feasibility Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial During COVID-19 Restrictions: Rivaroxaban Versus Acetyl Salicylic Acid in Patients with Multiple Myeloma on Lenalidomide-Based Therapy (RithMM).
abstract: Venous thromboembolism is a serious medical complication with an increased risk in patients with multiple myeloma undergoing combination treatment regimens. Acetylsalicylic acid is routinely used as a method of thromboprophylaxis in multiple myeloma patients treated with lenalidomide, and rivaroxaban has been assessed in small-scale studies in multiple myeloma patients treated with immunomodulatory drugs; yet, no study has compared the two methods. In this pilot, we asked if a full-scale trial would be feasible to assess the benefits of rivaroxaban over acetylsalicylic acid as a thromboprophylactic approach. This pilot recruited patients with multiple myeloma on lenalidomide-based therapy and randomized them to either low-dose acetylsalicylic acid or rivaroxaban, then monitored bleeding and thrombotic events throughout lenalidomide-dexamethasone treatment. A total of 55 patients were recruited across three Canadian centres, with two venous thromboembolic events and two bleeding events, all in the acetylsalicylic acid arm. We conducted a post hoc analysis of active recruitment time as a definition of recruitment feasibility, as we did not achieve our pre-defined feasibility goals. Despite the challenges in enrollment, possibly due to social restrictions during the COVID-19 pandemic, we maintain that a full-scale trial is feasible and offers insight into thromboprophylactic management in this population.

In this pilot, we asked if a full-scale trial would be feasible to assess the benefits of rivaroxaban over acetylsalicylic acid as a thromboprophylactic approach.
