title: Basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) as a candidate marker associated with venous thromboembolism risk factors in sepsis: an integrated bioinformatics and machine learning analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Sepsis affects over 19 million people worldwide annually and is associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), which significantly worsens clinical outcomes. However, current biomarkers such as D-dimer lack specificity, and the molecular signatures associated with VTE risk in sepsis remain unclear. METHODS: We applied integrative transcriptomics and machine learning approaches to identify VTE-associated biomarkers in sepsis-related datasets. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), differential gene expression analysis, and immune infiltration assessments were conducted using publicly available datasets. Candidate biomarkers were further evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, Cox regression, nomogram modeling, single-cell RNA sequencing, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) validation. RESULTS: p BATF BATF p BATF Basic leucine zipper ATF-like transcription factor (BATF) emerged as a top candidate biomarker, significantly associated with both sepsis and VTE-related datasets (fold change >1.5,< 0.001).expression showed consistent elevation across multiple independent cohorts and demonstrated discriminatory performance for disease- or risk-score-defined phenotypes, with area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.831 to 0.953. Highexpression was associated with prolonged prothrombin time and 28-day mortality in sepsis patients (= 0.024). Single-cell analysis showedenrichment in macrophages and dendritic cells. CONCLUSION: BATF may serve as a candidate biomarker associated with high VTE risk phenotypes and 28-day mortality in sepsis-related cohorts. However, BATF was not validated against adjudicated or imaging-confirmed VTE events in this study; therefore, it should not be interpreted as a diagnostic marker for confirmed VTE or a direct predictor of thrombosis. Prospective cohorts with adjudicated VTE outcomes are required to confirm its clinical utility.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of reocclusion after endovascular treatment for acute ischemic stroke: an updated systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE. Post hoc sensitivity analyses included only same-site reocclusion definitions. RESULTS: Ten studies (3,381 patients) were included; 244 (7.2%) reoccluded. Reocclusion was associated with lower 90-day functional independence (OR 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.38) and higher mortality (OR 1.86, 1.29-2.68), both moderate certainty. Reocclusion was more frequent with large-artery atherosclerosis (OR 2.24, 1.41-3.55; same-site 3.04, 1.73-5.33) and less frequent with cardioembolism (OR 0.40, 0.28-0.57) and atrial fibrillation (OR 0.39, 0.26-0.59), mutually confounded associations reflecting one embolic-versus-atherothrombotic axis. Prestroke antiplatelet therapy (OR 0.43, 0.28-0.67) lost significance under the same-site definition (0.60, 0.31-1.16). Exploratory data (two cohorts) linked eTICI 2c-3 reperfusion with less reocclusion (OR 0.44, 0.28-0.69). No study reported when etiology was adjudicated; the atherosclerosis association may be partly outcome-induced. CONCLUSIONS: Early reocclusion is uncommon but carries a substantial prognostic penalty. Its determinants appear to lie in the vascular substrate rather than thrombectomy technique; prospective studies with uniform same-site definitions and systematic follow-up imaging are needed.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Early reocclusion after endovascular treatment (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is underrecognized; its determinants and impact remain poorly defined. METHODS: Random-effects meta-analysis of early reocclusion after successful EVT (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library through January 2026). Crude odds ratios (ORs) were pooled and certainty rated with GRADE.

title: Knee Flexion and Popliteal Artery Contrast Arrival in Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Pilot Analysis of Bolus Tracking Monitoring Data.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) symptoms can worsen with knee flexion. We examined whether time-enhancement curve (TEC) analysis of discarded bolus tracking data could detect positional differences in popliteal arrival. METHODS: In this secondary analysis of a dedicated research protocol (not routine practice), 22 patients with PAD underwent bilateral lower-extremity CT angiography in extended and flexed positions, at ≈90-degree and at maximum flexion. Arrival time, rise rate, and initial area under the curve (iAUC) were extracted. The flexed and extended limbs were compared with Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: At maximum flexion, the flexed limb showed a median arrival delay of +1.5 s (p = 0.0002); the within-subject increase from 90-degree flexion to maximum flexion was significant (+0.5 s; p = 0.018). Exploratory subgroup analysis showed significant delays at both angles in unilateral (contralateral ankle-brachial index ≥0.9; n = 15) but not bilateral PAD (n = 7). The rise rate and iAUC did not differ. CONCLUSIONS: The flexed (affected) limb showed delayed popliteal arrival, which was greater at maximum flexion. Because limb position and disease severity were confounded by design, this association is not evidence of causation. These preliminary findings support the feasibility of bolus tracking-derived TEC analysis and motivate within-limb repeated-measures studies.

We examined whether time-enhancement curve (TEC) analysis of discarded bolus tracking data could detect positional differences in popliteal arrival. METHODS: In this secondary analysis of a dedicated research protocol (not routine practice), 22 patients with PAD underwent bilateral lower-extremity CT angiography in extended and flexed positions, at ≈90-degree and at maximum flexion.

title: An Entropic Value-at-Risk-Inspired Load-Balancing Routing Algorithm for LEO Satellite Networks.
abstract: In sixth-generation (6G) space-air-ground integrated networks, risk-neutral reinforcement-learning-based routing methods for low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks remain susceptible to severe tail latency. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel Entropic Value-at-Risk (EVaR)-inspired routing algorithm with risk regularization for low-return actions. The routing process in an LEO satellite network is formulated as an event-driven partially observable Markov decision process. Within a multi-agent soft actor-critic framework, an EVaR-inspired state-level risk proxy for low-return actions is introduced and incorporated into the actor loss as a risk regularizer. This design enables the joint optimization of expected routing returns and the mitigation of low-return action risk. Simulation results obtained in a simplified LEO network using Iridium orbital parameters demonstrate that, compared with the multi-agent soft actor-critic algorithm, the proposed algorithm reduces the average end-to-end delay and the 99th-percentile end-to-end delay by 19.2% and 32.9%, respectively. It also reduces the average and maximum queueing delays by 79.4% and 57.0%, respectively, with approximately no packet loss observed during the simulations. These results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm enables efficient and reliable routing in LEO satellite networks under high-load conditions.

The routing process in an LEO satellite network is formulated as an event-driven partially observable Markov decision process.

title: TNF-α and IL-8 Are Helpful in the Prediction of Late Post-COVID-19 Venous Thromboembolic Disease-Single-Center Prospective Study.
abstract: SARS-CoV-2 p p p Post-COVID-19 syndrome is associated with persistent inflammation and an elevated risk of late venous thromboembolism (VTE). The role of proinflammatory cytokines has been well documented in the acute phase of the disease, but their potential role in late post-COVID-19 VTE remains unknown. What is the prevalence of VTE among symptomatic post-COVID-19 patients, and which laboratory parameters could enhance the diagnostic accuracy for VTE in these patients? Consecutive patients with objectively confirmed previousinfection, admitted to a single department of lung diseases in a tertiary hospital due to sustained symptoms of dyspnea and/or exercise intolerance, were included. Clinical assessment and laboratory testing, including cytokine profiling (Il-1β, IL-6, IL-8, IL-10, TNF-α), PAI-1, and ferritin, were performed. VTE events (pulmonary embolism and/or deep vein thrombosis) were confirmed by standard imaging. Clinical and laboratory parameters were compared between participants with and without VTE. 108 patients: 69 (63.9%) males and 39 (36.1%) females, entered the study. VTE episodes were diagnosed in 39.8% (16.7% in the course of COVID-19 and 23.1% after the acute phase of the disease). Patients who entered the study ≤6 months and >6 months from acute COVID-19 infection were compared. Median D-dimer concentration was higher in patients with VTE that occurred within 6 months from the COVID-19 diagnosis compared to the non-VTE group (607 ng/mL vs. 428 ng/mL, borderline significance,= 0.0595). Median_IL-8 concentration was significantly higher in those who developed VTE more than 6 months after COVID-19 compared to non-VTE patients: 10.19 pg/mL vs. 6.61 pg/mL, respectively,= 0.048. The same was noted for TNF-α (39.02 pg/mL vs. 24 pg/mL, respectively,= 0.011). The best diagnostic utility for VTE prediction was obtained for TNF-α concentration in symptomatic patients diagnosed >6 months from acute COVID-19 infection (ROC AUC 0.73, 95% CI 0.57-0.91). TNF-α was an independent risk factor of VTE episodes in the whole study group. Detection of elevated IL-8 and TNF-α levels later than 6 months from acute COVID-19 disease may help to identify patients at increased risk of late venous thromboembolism; nevertheless, further studies are needed to validate this observation.

title: The Impact of Multiple Biologic Failures on Surgical Outcomes: A Retrospective Cohort Study of Elective Subtotal Colectomy for Ulcerative Colitis.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Subtotal colectomy (STC) with end ileostomy (EI) is usually the first surgical stage for patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) who fail medical treatment, most often with biological agents. Is there a difference in surgical outcome after failure of one or two biologicals vs. three or four?A retrospective study of all patients who underwent STC with EI for UC (5-2018 to 1-2022). After excluding emergent cases, the elective cohort was divided into patients who failed 1-2 biologicals (group 1-2) vs. patients who failed 3-4 biologicals (group 3-4), and surgical outcomes were compared. Data collected included patients' demographics, preoperative clinical manifestations, and operative and postoperative outcomes.Ninety-eight patients underwent STC for UC, and of them, 53 were elective. Thirty patients failed 1-2 biologics (group 1-2), and 23 failed 3-4 biologics (group 3-4). The groups were similar in average age (37.6 ± 11 vs. 32.7 ± 10), BMI (26.7 ± 6 vs. 27.7 ± 7), number of years with UC (9.5 ± 9 vs. 9 ± 8), rate of steroid dependence (20 (67%) vs. 13 (57%)) but differed in sex; there were 25 (83%) males in group 1-2, and 8 (35%) in group 3-4 (< 0.01). The operative approaches were similar, as was the operative time (217 ± 74 vs. 210 ± 79 min). The length of hospital stay was 3.2 ± 1 days for group 1-2 and 5 ± 6 days for group 3-4 (= 0.14). Postoperative complications were seen in 10 patients (33%) vs. 7 patients (30%) (= 0.82), and of them, two (7%) and two (9%) (= 0.82) had Venous thromboembolism (VTE), respectively. Only 20 patients (67%) in group 1-2 and 16 patients (70%) in group 3-4 (= 0.82) progressed to a second stage of an Ileoanal pouch (IPAA) at 11.1 ± 4 and 9.2 ± 2 months, respectively. The overall average follow-up time was 41.1 months.Ulcerative Colitis patients who fail 3-4 biological agents and choose to go to elective STC with EI have very similar surgical outcomes compared to patients who choose elective surgery after failing only 1-2 biological agents in the same time span of known disease. UC patients with severe colitis and poor quality of life who fail two lines of biological agents may be better off electing surgical treatment than failing more biologics and then going to surgery. On the other hand, patients who try 3-4 biologics may expect no worse surgical outcomes than after 1-2 biologics.

Is there a difference in surgical outcome after failure of one or two biologicals vs. three or four?A retrospective study of all patients who underwent STC with EI for UC (5-2018 to 1-2022).

title: Chronic Venous Disease in Pregnancy: Pathophysiology, Diagnostic Pitfalls, and a Trimester-Stratified Management Framework-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Chronic venous disease (CVD) in pregnancy is common, poorly codified, and interpreted with diagnostic thresholds, severity instruments and treatment algorithms all derived outside pregnancy. This narrative review synthesises the mechanistic, epidemiological, diagnostic and therapeutic literature, keeping pregnancy-specific evidence separate from evidence extrapolated from non-pregnant populations. Gestational change is characterised principally by increased venous capacitance and vein-wall distension; ambulatory venous hypertension was not demonstrated in the two pregnancy studies assessing it; and new reflux develops in a minority, undetectable postpartum in the one study reporting it. Physiological adaptation, CVD and thrombotic pathology overlap clinically, deep vein thrombosis and superficial vein thrombosis being at once the principal differential diagnoses and potential complications. Management is correspondingly conservative: compression relieves symptoms but has not been shown to prevent varicose veins, routine initiation of venoactive drugs is not supported, and intervention is deferred other than in exceptional circumstances. A venous finding first detected in pregnancy warrants postpartum reassessment before it is taken for established disease. A trimester-stratified framework spanning preconception to late postpartum reassessment is proposed; it is evidence-informed rather than prospectively validated, and is not a guideline.

title: Coenzyme Q10 for Acute Stanford Type A Aortic Dissection: Protocol for a Prospective, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Single-Center Feasibility Trial.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection (TAAD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency. Emergency surgery is the standard life-saving treatment, but some patients decline operative repair, and no established pharmacological therapy has been shown to stabilize acute TAAD. Preclinical work by our team implicates mitochondrial dysfunction and smooth muscle cell phenotypic switching in aortic dissection and suggests that coenzyme Q10 may reduce dissection-related injury. This study aims to determine the feasibility of a future definitive randomized trial and to obtain preliminary safety and exploratory efficacy information.This prospective, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, single-center feasibility trial will enroll 60 adults with CTA-confirmed Stanford type A aortic dissection within 24 h of symptom onset who decline emergency surgical repair after standard surgical counseling. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to oral coenzyme Q10 100 mg three times daily or matched placebo for 14 days, in addition to the same guideline-directed supportive medical care. The primary feasibility outcome is recruitment feasibility, defined as randomization of 60 participants within 12 months after recruitment initiation. Secondary feasibility outcomes include treatment adherence, follow-up completion, dropout, missingness, outcome-assessment feasibility, and candidate endpoint event rates. The primary exploratory clinical outcome is 14-day all-cause mortality; additional exploratory outcomes include aortic rupture death, false-lumen thrombosis, cardiac tamponade, worsening pericardial effusion, and organ malperfusion syndromes. Safety outcomes include adverse events, serious adverse events, adverse drug reactions, suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions, and prespecified laboratory indices.The trial is designed to establish whether recruitment, blinded treatment delivery, follow-up, outcome collection, and safety monitoring are operationally feasible and to provide estimates for planning a larger confirmatory trial.This feasibility trial will inform the design and conduct of future definitive evaluation of coenzyme Q10 in acute TAAD. Trial registration: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2600123230.

title: Etiology and Anatomical Level of Lower-Limb Amputations in Two Iranian Referral Hospitals: A Retrospective Record-Based Study.
abstract: Background Methods Results Conclusions p p : Lower-limb amputation arises from heterogeneous pathways ranging from severe trauma to dysvascular disease and infection, yet comparative data across Iranian hospitals remain limited. We aimed to characterize demographic, etiologic, and anatomical patterns of lower-limb amputation and to evaluate between-hospital heterogeneity.: This retrospective, two-hospital, record-based study included 229 eligible hospitalization records with lower-limb amputation at Al-Zahra and Kashani hospitals in Isfahan, Iran, from 13 April 2014 through 18 March 2020. Primary etiology was reconstructed from ordered diagnostic codes using a predefined hierarchical algorithm; external-cause codes were reviewed as supporting contextual information and to characterize documented traumatic mechanisms. Amputation level was derived from ICD-9-CM procedure codes. Analyses used Python 3.13.5 (NumPy, pandas, SciPy, and statsmodels).: Trauma was the leading etiology (49.3%), followed by dysvascular disease (28.8%) and infection (10.5%). Age differed strongly across etiologies (H = 93.71; Holm-adjusted< 0.001; epsilon-squared = 0.398, 95% CI 0.307-0.509), with trauma-related hospitalizations occurring at younger ages. Toe (35.4%) and below-knee (34.5%) amputations were most frequent. Hospital was associated with both etiology and amputation level (both Holm-adjusted< 0.001; bias-corrected Cramer's V = 0.374 and 0.471, respectively). In an adjusted major-versus-minor model, older age and treatment at Al-Zahra Hospital were associated with major amputation, whereas female sex was not statistically significant.: The hospitalizations showed marked descriptive differences by age, etiology, and hospital. Trauma-related hospitalizations occurred at younger ages, whereas dysvascular and infection-related hospitalizations occurred later in life. The substantial between-hospital differences indicate that pooled hospital-based estimates may obscure institutional case mix and should not be interpreted as population-level incidence.

title: Safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System in acute intermediate-risk pulmonary embolism: the SPIRARE II pivotal trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE. METHODS: SPIRARE II was a prospective, single-arm, multicentre pivotal investigation conducted at 19 sites in the United States and Europe. Eligible patients had acute PE (≤14 days), a computed tomography angiography-assessed RV to left ventricle (RV/LV) ratio>0.9, and haemodynamic stability (systolic blood pressure ≥90 mmHg). Co-primary endpoints were composite major adverse events (MAE) within 48 hours and core laboratory-assessed RV/LV change from baseline to 48 hours. Prespecified secondary endpoints were collected immediately pre- and post-procedure in all patients including mean pulmonary artery pressure, total pulmonary vascular resistance, and cardiac index. RESULTS: In 123 patients, the 48-hour composite MAE rate was 2.4% (3/123), meeting the prespecified performance goal (one-sided p<0.0001). The mean RV/LV diameter ratio decreased from 1.44±0.33 at baseline to 1.05±0.21 at 48 hours, a mean reduction of 0.39±0.33, exceeding the prespecified performance goal (p<0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System met its prespecified safety and effectiveness endpoints in acute intermediate-risk PE. TFX delivered precise, stable control with reliable vessel access, enabling consistent right ventricular unloading. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06576427).
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Percutaneous aspiration thrombectomy can rapidly reduce afterload in acute pulmonary embolism (PE), but catheter stiffness and instability may limit access and prevent effective right ventricle (RV) unloading. The Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System with Transforming Fixation (TFX) technology is designed to address current limitations of existing catheter-based systems by separating the flexibility necessary for safe navigation from the support that is essential for procedural control. AIMS: We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of the Vertex Pulmonary Embolectomy System for mechanical aspiration thrombectomy in acute intermediate-risk PE.

title: Endovascular salvage of dysfunctional native haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas: Clinical outcomes and predictors of patency.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas are an important cause of inadequate dialysis, access failure and morbidity in patients with chronic kidney disease (CKD), and timely catheter-based intervention may help restore access function and prolong fistula usability. OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy, feasibility, and safety of catheter-based interventional procedures for hypofunctioning haemodialysis fistulas in patients with CKD. METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational follow up study, enrolled with 100 CKD patients on maintenance haemodialysis with dysfunctional native arteriovenous fistulas who underwent fistulogram and catheter-based intervention. RESULTS: The mean age was 57.2 ± 12.4 years, 62.0% were male, Hypertension (80.0%) and diabetes mellitus (57.0%) were the major comorbidities. Radio cephalic fistula was the commonest access type (46.0%), and inadequate dialysis was the leading presentation (73.0%). Fistulography showed significant stenosis in 96.0%, with central vein involvement in 43.0% and long-segment lesions in 56.0%. Angioplasty was attempted in 96.0%, achieving technical success in 91.7% of attempted interventions and clinical success in 85.0%. Stenosis and pressure gradient reduced significantly after intervention (both p < 0.001). Complications occurred in 13.0%, with no deaths. Primary patency declined from 82.0% at 1 month to 58.0% at 6 months and 38.0% at 12 months. Patency loss was independently predicted by older age, central vein lesions, long lesions, residual stenosis, and absent post-procedure thrill. CONCLUSION: Catheter-based endovascular intervention may be an effective fistula-salvage strategy for hypofunctioning haemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas, although long-term patency was influenced by lesion complexity, residual stenosis and restoration of post-procedure thrill.

METHODS: This single-centre, retrospective observational follow up study, enrolled with 100 CKD patients on maintenance haemodialysis with dysfunctional native arteriovenous fistulas who underwent fistulogram and catheter-based intervention.

title: Heterogeneity in Time-Outcome Associations After Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Binational Registry Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although "time is brain" remains a core principle in acute stroke care, the association between treatment timing and functional outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) varies across patients. Some individuals treated in extended time windows still achieve favorable outcomes, a phenomenon termed the "late window paradox." Differences in stroke pathophysiology across etiologies may contribute to heterogeneity in the time-outcome relationship after EVT. We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology. METHODS: We analyzed data from two multicenter registries in Korea (CRCS-K) and Taiwan (TREAT-AIS) from January 2019 to April 2023. Patients with anterior circulation acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism (CE) or large artery atherosclerosis (LAA) were included. Multivariable regression and interaction analyzes were performed to evaluate the association between onset-to-puncture (OTP) time and 90-day functional outcomes and to identify effect modifiers. RESULTS: _interaction Among 4,719 patients (mean age 72.0 years; 42.9% women; median NIHSS 15), longer OTP time was associated with lower odds of 90-day functional independence (adjusted OR per hour, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.96-0.98; p = 0.001). The impact of OTP time varied by stroke characteristics. CE etiology, MCA occlusion, higher NIHSS, and male sex were associated with greater time sensitivity. In CE strokes, each hour of delay reduced the odds of functional independence by 4% (aOR, 0.96; 95% CI, 0.94-0.97; p < 0.001), whereas no significant association was observed in LAA strokes (P=0.028). CONCLUSION: The association between EVT timing and functional outcome varies according to stroke etiology and clinical characteristics, highlighting heterogeneity in time-outcome relationships among EVT-treated patients and providing observational insight into outcome variability in extended treatment windows.

We investigated factors associated with heterogeneity in time-dependent EVT responsiveness, with particular attention to stroke etiology.

title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes. METHODS: This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria. RESULTS: A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak. CONCLUSIONS: Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.

title: Clinical Risk Factors and Inflammatory Markers as Predictors of Postoperative Delirium in Patients Undergoing Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Surgery.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common and serious neurological complication following acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) repair, contributing to increased morbidity and mortality. Given the critical role of systemic inflammation in POD pathogenesis, this study aimed to evaluate perioperative inflammatory profiles in patients undergoing ATAAD repair and to develop a predictive nomogram for early POD risk stratification.This retrospective, single-center study included 355 patients who underwent total arch replacement for ATAAD. Serial inflammatory markers were assessed across multiple perioperative time points. A two-stage variable selection process, incorporating variance inflation factor (VIF) and the Boruta algorithm, was utilized to identify robust predictors. A predictive nomogram was constructed via multivariable logistic regression. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples.POD occurred in 29.86% of the cohort. Patients who developed POD had higher inflammatory marker levels at several individual postoperative time points compared to the non-delirium group. The final predictive model integrated 11 key variables: age, EuroSCORE I, CPB time, SIRI_6h, PLR_6h, IL-10_6h, IL-8_6h, IL-8_pre, IL-6_6h, IL-6_pre, and PCT_6h. The nomogram demonstrated acceptable internal discrimination with an AUC of 0.835 (95% CI: 0.794-0.876) and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.811. Notably, IL-6_6h and PCT_6h emerged as strong independent risk factors, while SIRI_6h demonstrated an inverse association with POD. Calibration and DCA analyses confirmed the model's acceptable performance and potential clinical utility, though independent external validation remains essential prior to any clinical translation. An exploratory, web-based risk calculator was developed to facilitate bedside implementation.This study develops and internally validates an exploratory biomarker-based prediction model for POD in ATAAD patients. By integrating early inflammatory profiles with established clinical variables, this preliminary model provides a preliminary foundation for early risk stratification, though rigorous prospective multicenter external validation is required before real-world clinical implementation can be considered.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging vs computed tomography for baseline imaging evaluation in acute basilar artery occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The optimal imaging modality, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) or computed tomography (CT), for identifying good treatment candidates among patients with acute basilar-artery occlusion (BAO) remains unclear. METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality. The primary outcome was mRS 0-3 at 90 days. The secondary outcomes included mRS score shift on an ordinal scale, early neurological deterioration, time from stroke onset to arterial puncture, and time from onset to randomization. The safety outcome was mortality within 90 days. Clinical outcomes and workflow times were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Among 340 patients (CT: n = 277; MRI: n = 63), baseline imaging was not significantly associated with 90-day mRS 0-3 in the overall cohort (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.50-1.95; P = 0.976). It remained highly consistent across both the endovascular treatment and best medical management subgroups. Baseline MRI assessment was not associated with significant workflow delays compared with CT, including time from stroke onset to randomization (mean difference [MD] 5.23 min; P = 0.843) and time to puncture (MD 13.16 min; P = 0.701). Furthermore, the association between imaging modality and outcomes was consistent across different time windows. DISCUSSION: In patients with acute BAO, we did not observe evidence supporting the preferential use of MRI over CT as the primary imaging strategy for patient selection. Conventional imaging appears sufficient as a first-line tool for selecting patients in clinical practice.

METHODS: This was a post hoc analysis of the ATTENTION trial. Patients were categorized into MRI or CT groups according to the baseline imaging modality.

title: The Diabetes Paradox in Aortic Aneurysms: An Unexpected Inverse Association.
abstract: Aortic aneurysms are associated with substantial morbidity and mortalitbecause of the risk of progressive dilation, rupture, and related acute aortic complications. Although diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major cardiovascular risk factor, epidemiological studies have consistently reported an inverse association between DM and the prevalence and progression of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). More limited evidence suggests an inverse association between diabetes and thoracic aortic aneurysm. Accordingly, this review focuses primarily on AAA; where available, evidence concerning TAA and aortic dissection is discussed separately. This review examines the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying the inverse association between DM and aortic aneurysm development. Key mechanisms include the effects of hyperglycemia on extracellular matrix remodeling, particularly through modulation of matrix metalloproteinase (MMP-2 and MMP-9) activity, increased formation of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), and enhanced collagen cross-linking. Experimental and translational evidence suggests that diabetes may influence inflammatory cell states and mural neoangiogenesis, although these effects appear to be context- and model-dependent. Antidiabetic therapies, including metformin, DPP-4 inhibitors, GLP-1 receptor agonists, thiazolidinediones, sulfonylureas, and SGLT2 inhibitors, may also contribute to the observed association through glucose-lowering and/or pleiotropic vascular effects. Furthermore, diabetes-related changes in aortic wall biomechanics, including increased wall thickness and potentially altered wall stress, may contribute to aneurysm stabilization. Overall, DM is associated with a lower prevalence and slower progression of AAA, potentially through a combination of metabolic, inflammatory, structural, and treatment-related mechanisms. These observations should not be interpreted as evidence that diabetes or chronic hyperglycemia is clinically beneficial; rather, they may help identify biological pathways relevant to aneurysm development and progression.

Although diabetes mellitus (DM) is a major cardiovascular risk factor, epidemiological studies have consistently reported an inverse association between DM and the prevalence and progression of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA). More limited evidence suggests an inverse association between diabetes and thoracic aortic aneurysm.

title: Multistage Preclinical Evaluation of MRI-Guided Stenting for Coarctation of the Aorta using in vitro and Porcine Models.
abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluated the technical and procedural feasibility of MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA using a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A commercially available MR Conditional guidewire and dedicated research prototypes comprising nitinol stents, delivery systems, and balloon catheters were assessed in a three-stage protocol. Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T. In a polymer-based CoA vessel phantom, 10 stent implantations were performed by novices (n = 6) and experts (n = 4), with four separate expert-led balloon dilatations. MRI-guided stent implantation was subsequently performed in five porcine models. RESULTS: All devices were visible at both field strengths, with lateral artifact widths of 5.3-7.8 mm for the guidewire, 20.9-38.5 mm for the stent delivery system, 13.1-19.9 mm for the expanded stents, and 17.4-30.5 mm for the balloon catheter. Phantom stenting duration was 10.2 ± 7.2 mins for novices and 6.2 ± 2.7 mins for experts. MRI-guided stent implantation was successfully performed in all five animals, with a mean duration of 13.6 ± 7.5 mins. In one animal, balloon post-dilatation was additionally performed as a procedural proof of concept. CONCLUSION: MRI-guided stent implantation for CoA is feasible within a structured multistage preclinical evaluation protocol and supports further clinical translation of radiation-free endovascular treatment.

Device visibility was evaluated in a standardized water phantom at 1.5 T and 3.0 T.

title: Unintended Shifts in High-Priority Adult Heart Transplant Listings after the OPTN's September 2025 Policy Change.
abstract: The Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network amended Status 2 heart allocation criteria in September 2025, requiring documented failure of high-dose inotropes before candidates could qualify via intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) or percutaneous endovascular ventricular assist device (PEVAD) support. Using OPTN data, we compared seasonally matched pre-policy (September 2024-June 2025, n=4,206) and post-policy (September 2025-June 2026, n=4,231) adult candidates. While standard Status 3 high-dose inotrope listings increased 2.0% to 4.1% and standard Status 2 IABP/PEVAD listings decreased 18.2% to 11.0%, Status 1 listings and Status 2 exceptions increased 7.7% to 10.6% and 17.5% to 21.5%, respectively (all p<0.001). Consequently, combined initial Status 1/2 listings were unchanged (44.5% vs 44.0%, p=0.71). Furthermore, overall transplant volume remained similar, but status at transplant shifted from standard Status 2 toward Status 2 exceptions and Status 1. Tightening standard Status 2 eligibility was associated with redistribution across high-priority pathways rather than reduced high-priority listings.

title: Probable Loeys-Dietz Syndrome with aortic root dilatation and multiple arterial tortuosity in resource-limited setting : A case report.
abstract: Loeys-Dietz Syndrome (LDS) is a rare hereditary connective tissue disorder that is characterized by multisystem disorders predisposing individuals to arterial and aortic aneurysms. We present the case of a 17-year-old Bangladeshi male referred to cardiology for assessment of systemic abnormalities and cardiovascular risk. He presented with craniofacial, musculoskeletal, and cutaneous abnormalities including hypertelorism, mandibular ectopic hair, joint hypermobility with mild thoracic scoliosis, residual talipes equinovarus. He had past medical history of surgically corrected congenital anomalies. Based on clinical and radiological findings, he was diagnosed with clinically suspected Loeys-Dietz Syndrome as genetic testing was unavailable. He was managed through a multidisciplinary approach with regular follow-up. This report adds to literature on Loeys-Dietz Syndrome, emphasizing on aortic root dilatation and carotid artery tortuosity as important clinical and radiological features supporting diagnosis of LDS particularly in young patients presenting with characteristic craniofacial abnormalities or suggestive radiological findings. Early recognition and multidisciplinary management are crucial in resource-limited settings to prevent life-threatening vascular complications.

We present the case of a 17-year-old Bangladeshi male referred to cardiology for assessment of systemic abnormalities and cardiovascular risk. He presented with craniofacial, musculoskeletal, and cutaneous abnormalities including hypertelorism, mandibular ectopic hair, joint hypermobility with mild thoracic scoliosis, residual talipes equinovarus.

title: Cervical Spine Oncology: Perioperative Management and Complications.
abstract: STUDY DESIGN: Narrative review. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize contemporary evidence on perioperative complications in primary and metastatic cervical spine tumor surgery and to provide an evidence-informed framework for their prevention and management. SUMMARY OF BACKGROUND DATA: Cervical spine tumor surgery converges dense neurovascular and aerodigestive anatomy with a medically fragile, frequently irradiated patient population. Although cervical metastases represent only about 8-20% of spinal metastatic disease, their mismanagement carries disproportionately severe consequences, ranging from disabling pain to high-level paralysis and death. Cervical-specific risk-stratification tools are lacking, and most available evidence is extrapolated from degenerative anterior cervical cohorts. METHODS: This is a narrative review of perioperative complications in cervical spine oncology. PubMed/MEDLINE and Google Scholar were searched for English-language articles published through May 2026, prioritizing literature from the past 5 years while including seminal earlier references where foundational, using combinations of the terms "cervical spine," "spinal metastasis," "spinal tumor," "perioperative complications," "airway," "vertebral artery," "wound," "dysphagia," "venous thromboembolism," and "hardware failure." Reference lists of included articles were hand-searched for additional sources. Studies were selected by author consensus for relevance to the complication domains discussed; formal risk-of-bias assessment and quantitative pooling were not performed, consistent with a narrative design. Because oncology-specific evidence is limited, data derived from degenerative cervical cohorts are identified as such throughout. RESULTS: Major complication domains include airway compromise (highest with multilevel corpectomy, combined approaches, and cervicothoracic constructs), vascular and neurologic injury, CSF leak, wound failure and infection in irradiated fields, hardware failure, venous thromboembolism, and dysphagia. CONCLUSIONS: Outcomes depend on preoperative risk stratification, multidisciplinary coordination, and individualized postoperative care rather than any single intraoperative maneuver. Because the evidence base remains largely Level III-IV without validated cervical oncology-specific tools, described practices should be regarded as reasonable, evidence-informed considerations rather than standards of care.

title: Dapagliflozin After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation According to Frailty in DapaTAVI Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Frailty is common in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation and portends worse outcomes. Whether the benefit of posttranscatheter aortic valve implantation dapagliflozin differs by frailty is uncertain. METHODS: In this post hoc analysis, we investigated the efficacy of dapagliflozin according to frailty status in the DapaTAVI (Dapagliflozin in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation) trial. Frailty was assessed through the Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of Weight scale (robust=0, prefrail=1-2, frail=3-5). The primary outcome was the composite of all-cause death or worsening heart failure at 1 year. RESULTS: P P Among 1222 patients with baseline frailty assessment, 47.2% were frail, 40.3% prefrail, and 12.4% robust. Over 12 months, 215 patients (17.6%) experienced the primary end point. Patients who were prefrail and frail had higher risk than robust patients (adjusted hazard ratios [HRs], 1.88 [95% CI, 1.05-3.38] and 2.29 [1.29-4.07], respectively;=0.004). Dapagliflozin was associated with a lower risk of the primary end point in patients who were frail (HR, 0.53 [95% CI, 0.36-0.77]) but not in those who were prefrail (HR, 1.01 [95% CI, 0.66-1.55]) or robust patients (HR, 1.26 [95% CI, 0.42-3.75]);for interaction=0.021. There was no evidence that frailty modified the safety profile of dapagliflozin. CONCLUSIONS: Frailty was common and independently associated with worse outcomes after transcatheter aortic valve implantation. Dapagliflozin appeared to confer greater relative benefit in patients with frailty.

title: Vein of Galen malformation in newborns and children: contemporary advances and future directions.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Vein of Galen malformation is a rare and complex cerebrovascular disorder associated with significant morbidity and mortality from the fetal period through childhood. Advances in perinatal care, neuroimaging, endovascular therapy, and multidisciplinary management have improved survival and expanded therapeutic options, while generating new challenges in clinical strategies and long-term outcomes. OBJECTIVE: This review integrates evidence and expert perspectives presented during the II International Meeting on Vein of Galen Malformation in Newborns and Children, held in Camogli, Italy, in October 2025 and summarizes current advances, emerging developments, and priorities for research and clinical innovation. RECENT ADVANCES: Current developments include improved fetal and neonatal imaging, emerging prognostic biomarkers, fetal intervention, advances in endovascular treatment, and increasing understanding of underlying genetic and molecular mechanisms. Contemporary management increasingly integrates cardiovascular and neurological assessment, advanced neuroimaging, individualized endovascular strategies, and structured long-term neurodevelopmental follow-up. The development of a disease-specific registry reflects the growing impact of international collaboration. FUTURE DIRECTIONS: Major priorities include validation of risk-stratification tools, development of standardized imaging and neurodevelopmental biomarkers, refinement of fetal and neonatal interventions, improved understanding of disease biology, and multicenter data sharing. Family-centered care and standardized long-term outcome assessment should remain integral components of future VOGM research and clinical practice. CONCLUSIONS: VOGM management is rapidly evolving from survival-focused treatment toward individualized, multidisciplinary care extending from fetal diagnosis through childhood and adulthood. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current knowledge and emerging developments in this field, while defining a multidisciplinary, internationally informed roadmap for future research.

title: Development and internal validation of a parsimonious model for neurological deterioration at 48 h after endovascular thrombectomy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The incremental value of routine admission measurements for predicting early neurological deterioration after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) remains unclear. METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. END48 was defined as an increase of at least 4 National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) points from admission to the fixed 48-h postoperative assessment. The conservative primary cohort excluded an unresolved longitudinal data segment. A revision-stage locked five-predictor logistic regression model included admission NIHSS scores, age, glucose levels, white blood cell count, and ln triglyceride value, with the NIHSS-only model serving as the comparator. Internal validation used 1,000 bootstrap samples and paired nested intervals of 1,000 outer × 100 inner samples. RESULTS: Post-hoc Of the 253 records representing 251 unique patients, 214 adults entered the primary cohort; 51 (23.8%) had END48. The primary model had an apparent area under the curve (AUC) of 0.651 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.601 (0.511 to 0.723). The corrected AUC difference vs. the NIHSS-only model was 0.038 (-0.025 to 0.171). The corrected Brier score was 0.180, compared to a prevalence-only reference of 0.182, resulting in a Brier skill score of 0.9%. The corrected primary calibration slope was 0.731 (0.519 to 0.892). Incremental net benefit was -0.015, 0.036, and 0.013 at 10%, 20%, and 30% thresholds, respectively; all corresponding 95% confidence intervals crossed zero.Riley assessments across plausible model-fit assumptions indicated that the available cohort was below the sample size desirable for model development. The reconstructed cohort sensitivity analysis did not change the overall interpretation. CONCLUSION: Discrimination was limited, improvement in probability accuracy was marginal, and incremental discrimination and net benefit were uncertain. The model should be regarded as exploratory rather than clinically implementable; independent validation and improved outcome ascertainment are required.

METHODS: This retrospective single-center reanalysis used a 2020-2022 registry. title: The snake-head sign on MRI in craniocervical junction dural arteriovenous fistulas: a novel imaging feature and a hypothesis of venous remodeling and congestion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Craniocervical junction (CCJ)-region dural arteriovenous fistulas (dAVFs) are rare but potentially reversible causes of venous congestive myelopathy, often difficult to recognize due to non-specific presentation. We observed a characteristic pattern of intramedullary T2 hyperintensity on sagittal MRI, involving the medulla and upper cervical cord with a rostral end divided into ventral and dorsal limbs, which we termed the "snake-head sign." This study aimed to characterize the prevalence of this feature among reported CCJ-region dAVF cases and explore its clinical and anatomical correlates. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed published cases of CCJ-region or adjacent dAVFs reported between 1996 and 2026 that included retrievable sagittal T2-weighted or FLAIR images. The presence of the snake-head sign was assessed, and clinical, angiographic, and treatment-related variables were extracted, including fistula location, feeding artery, draining vein direction, treatment modality, and outcome. Associations with the sign were evaluated using univariate analyses. Given the retrospective, literature-based design and limited sample size, findings were considered hypothesis-generating. RESULTS: Among 64 reported cases, the snake-head sign was identified in 31 (48.4%). No significant associations were found between the sign and age, sex, symptom duration, feeding artery, treatment modality, or outcome. However, a non-significant trend was observed for venous drainage configuration: cases with cranial convergence of the draining vein toward the CCJ more frequently demonstrated the sign, whereas purely caudal drainage patterns showed it less often. Fistulas at lower cervical nerve-root sleeves, requiring a longer cranial venous course, also showed higher sign frequency. These findings suggest the sign may reflect venous outflow geometry rather than arterial source or fistula location. CONCLUSION: The snake-head sign is a recognizable MRI feature present in roughly half of reported CCJ-region dAVF cases. Its identification may raise clinical suspicion for CCJ-related dAVF, particularly in unexplained venous congestive myelopathy. The trend toward a higher frequency of the sign in cases with cranially convergent venous drainage raises the hypothesis that it reflects concentrated venous congestion at this anatomical transition zone. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized imaging review and angiographic correlation are needed to confirm its diagnostic value and clarify the underlying mechanism.

title: Prognostic Value of Serial Alkaline Phosphatase-to-Albumin Ratio for Mortality After Transjugular Intrahepatic Portosystemic Shunt.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: p p p Conclusions: Prognostic assessment after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) remains challenging, and currently available scores are based mainly on pre-procedural variables. The alkaline phosphatase-to-albumin ratio (APAR) is a simple laboratory-derived marker that may provide additional prognostic information during the early post-TIPS period.This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 45 adults who underwent TIPS between February 2019 and December 2024. APAR was calculated at baseline, 48 h, and 1 week after the procedure. The primary outcome was one-year all-cause mortality; 90-day mortality was a secondary outcome. Prognostic performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and associations with mortality were examined using Cox regression adjusted for age and baseline MELD score.Within one year, 17 patients (37.8%) died; nine (20.0%) died within 90 days; and 22 (48.9%) died during overall follow-up. Median APAR was higher in patients who died within one year than in those alive at one year at baseline (5.98 vs. 3.89;= 0.006), 48 h (10.79 vs. 3.78;< 0.001), and 1 week (13.93 vs. 4.57;< 0.001). ROC areas under the curve were 0.748 (95% CI, 0.578-0.893), 0.876 (0.748-0.964), and 0.873 (0.726-0.977), respectively. After adjustment for age and MELD, APAR remained associated with one-year mortality at baseline (hazard ratio [HR] 1.140; 95% CI, 1.049-1.238), 48 h (HR 1.225; 1.111-1.350), and 1 week (HR 1.193; 1.092-1.302).Serial APAR measurements were associated with one-year mortality after TIPS and may support early post-procedural risk assessment. Prospective multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

title: Peripheral Arterial Disease: Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate and Interleukin-6 as Markers of Disease Severity and Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia.
abstract: p p p p Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a manifestation of systemic atherosclerosis in which chronic inflammation contributes to disease severity. This retrospective study included patients who underwent arteriography for PAD at a single center in 2019. Of 238 arteriographies performed, inflammatory and hematologic biomarker panels were available for a subset of 71 patients with angiographically confirmed PAD. Serum tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), white blood cell count, platelet count, and uric acid were compared across sex, age, diabetes, and obesity subgroups, correlated with disease severity by the Leriche-Fontaine classification, and analyzed for their association with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI; Fontaine stages III-IV vs. IIA-IIB). ESR (r = 0.408,= 0.001) and IL-6 (r = 0.310,= 0.009) correlated significantly with disease severity, whereas TNF-α, white blood cell count, platelet count, and uric acid did not. Both markers showed modest but significant discriminative performance for CLTI (IL-6: area under the curve = 0.674,= 0.012; ESR: area under the curve = 0.673,= 0.021). ESR and IL-6 were both associated with PAD severity suggesting a more pronounced systemic inflammatory phenotype in CLTI; their prognostic value after revascularization warrants evaluation in larger, prospective cohorts.

title: Heart Failure Is Associated with Limb-Related Adverse Events in Patients Hospitalized for Diabetic Foot Ulcers.
abstract: Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p p To evaluate the impact of heart failure (HF) on one-year outcomes in patients hospitalized for diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs).A retrospective observational study including consecutive patients admitted in 2024 to a tertiary multidisciplinary diabetic foot service for DFUs. Patients were stratified according to the presence of HF (HF+ vs. HF-). One-year outcomes included wound healing, major amputation, non-fatal major adverse limb events (NF-MALCE), including myocardial infarction, stroke, recurrent chronic limb-threatening ischaemia (CLTI) requiring revascularization, and mortality.Overall, 270 patients were included (104 HF+ [38.5%] vs. 166 HF- [61.5%]). Patients with HF exhibited a more severe cardiorenal phenotype, with worse cardiac and renal biomarkers. At one-year follow-up, patients with HF showed lower wound healing rates than patients without HF (58.6% vs. 71.7%,= 0.03), higher incidence of NF-MALCE (43.3% vs. 18.7%,< 0.001), mainly driven by recurrent CLTI requiring revascularization (48.9% vs. 27.0%,< 0.001), and higher mortality (21.1% vs. 7.2%,= 0.001). Conversely, no differences were observed in major amputation, myocardial infarction, or stroke. After multivariable adjustment for age, sex, ischaemic heart disease, atrial fibrillation, dialysis, haemoglobin, albumin, foot infection and peripheral arterial disease (PAD), HF remained independently associated with NF-MALCE (adjusted odds ratio (aOR) 2.90, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.38-6.09,= 0.005) and recurrent CLTI requiring revascularization (aOR 2.43, 95% CI 1.11-5.32,= 0.026); the association remained consistent in the subgroup with PAD.HF identifies a high-risk cardio-renal phenotype and is independently associated with increased limb-related adverse events in patients hospitalized for DFUs, supporting closer vascular surveillance and integrated multidisciplinary cardio-renal-foot care.

title: Pharmacokinetics, Safety, and Exploratory 12-Month Clinical Follow-Up of a Novel BIOtorcin™-Coated Balloon for Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The BRight PK Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) provide local antiproliferative therapy during endovascular revascularization without leaving a permanent vascular scaffold. Sirolimus is an attractive cytostatic antiproliferative agent, although its relatively low lipophilicity creates challenges for rapid arterial uptake and sustained tissue residence following balloon delivery. The BRight DCB is a novel peripheral DCB coated with BIOtorcin™ (CRC-015), a highly lipophilic synthetic derivative of sirolimus. The BRight PK study primarily evaluated the systemic pharmacokinetics of BIOtorcin™ and its metabolite sirolimus following treatment of femoropopliteal disease and secondarily assessed procedural performance, safety, patency, and functional outcomes over 12 months.BRight PK was a prospective, single-center, non-randomized pharmacokinetic study involving six adults with symptomatic peripheral artery disease (PAD; Rutherford-Becker category 2-4) caused by de novo superficial femoral and/or proximal popliteal artery disease. Following mandatory predilatation, lesions were treated with one or two BRight DCBs. Whole-blood BIOtorcin™ and sirolimus concentrations were measured before treatment and serially from 5 min to 24 h after removal of the final DCB. Non-compartmental pharmacokinetic analysis was performed. Angiography and duplex ultrasound were independently assessed by a core laboratory, and endpoint-related clinical events were independently adjudicated.All six participants completed 12-month follow-up. Mean age was 70.8 ± 7.4 years, and four (66.7%) were male. Seven BRight DCBs treated six lesions. Mean core-laboratory lesion length was 140.85 ± 136.23 mm, and baseline diameter stenosis was 78.50 ± 23.39%. Mean BIOtorcin™ exposure was 3976.8 ± 1665.7 µg (0.051 ± 0.0188 mg/kg). BIOtorcin™ Cmax was 23.60 ± 9.88 ng/mL at 5 min, terminal half-life was 21.87 ± 10.17 h, AUC0-t was 28.30 ± 12.19 h·ng/mL, and AUC0-∞ was 47.47 ± 18.27 h·ng/mL. Sirolimus Cmax was 0.692 ± 0.462 ng/mL at 24 h, when concentrations remained on the ascending portion of the concentration-time curve, indicating that the 24 h sampling window captured only early systemic sirolimus exposure rather than a complete pharmacokinetic profile. Device success was 100% (7/7); core-laboratory technical and procedural success were each 66.7% (4/6). No deaths, major or minor amputations, clinically driven target lesion revascularizations (cd-TLR), or clinically driven target vessel revascularizations (cd-TVRs) occurred. Visit-based 12-month primary patency was 83.3% (5/6); the single binary restenosis was detected at day 391, resulting in Kaplan-Meier primary patency of 100% at calendar day 365. The mean overall Walking Impairment Questionnaire (WIQ) score increased from 21.87 ± 19.16 at baseline to 62.28 ± 38.78 at 12 months.BIOtorcin™ demonstrated rapid systemic appearance following BRight DCB treatment, followed by a progressive decline in circulating parent drug concentrations and low systemic exposure to its metabolite, sirolimus. These pharmacokinetic findings, together with successful device delivery and the absence of major safety concerns over 12 months, demonstrate procedural feasibility and support continued clinical evaluation of the BRight DCB. Given the pharmacokinetic study design and small sample size (= 6), the 12-month clinical, functional, and patency findings are exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as evidence of clinical efficacy.

Sirolimus is an attractive cytostatic antiproliferative agent, although its relatively low lipophilicity creates challenges for rapid arterial uptake and sustained tissue residence following balloon delivery. The BRight DCB is a novel peripheral DCB coated with BIOtorcin™ (CRC-015), a highly lipophilic synthetic derivative of sirolimus.

title: Thrombotic Complications in Women Undergoing Assisted Reproductive Technologies: Pathophysiology, Prevention, and Clinical Management-A Narrative Review.
abstract: Thrombotic complications represent uncommon but potentially life-threatening adverse events associated with assisted reproductive technologies (ARTs), particularly in the setting of controlled ovarian stimulation and ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS). The relationship between thrombophilia, infertility, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains complex and only partially understood. While antiphospholipid syndrome is a well-established acquired thrombophilic disorder associated with recurrent pregnancy loss, the association between common inherited thrombophilias and recurrent pregnancy loss is less consistent, and their contribution to primary infertility and implantation failure remains uncertain. Conversely, severe OHSS is consistently recognized as the principal treatment-related determinant of thrombotic events during IVF because of profound endothelial activation, hemoconcentration, and hypercoagulability. This narrative review summarizes the current evidence regarding the epidemiology, pathophysiology, and clinical presentation of thrombotic complications associated with assisted reproductive technologies, including deep vein thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, cerebral venous thrombosis, upper-extremity thrombosis, splanchnic vein thrombosis, and arterial thrombotic events. Current recommendations for thromboprophylaxis, diagnostic strategies, and therapeutic management are critically discussed, with particular attention to individualized risk assessment and the role of low-molecular-weight heparin in high-risk patients. Although routine thromboprophylaxis is not recommended for all women undergoing in vitro fertilization (IVF), careful evaluation of patient-specific thrombotic risk factors remains essential. Future prospective studies are needed to improve risk prediction, optimize preventive strategies, and establish evidence-based recommendations for women undergoing assisted reproduction.

The relationship between thrombophilia, infertility, ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains complex and only partially understood. While antiphospholipid syndrome is a well-established acquired thrombophilic disorder associated with recurrent pregnancy loss, the association between common inherited thrombophilias and recurrent pregnancy loss is less consistent, and their contribution to primary infertility and implantation failure remains uncertain.

title: The emerging molecular landscape of abdominal aortic aneurysms: non-coding RNAs as diagnostic and therapeutic targets.
abstract: An abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a progressive, often asymptomatic condition whose rupture is associated with a high mortality rate. Ultrasonography and computed tomography are established diagnostic methods, while molecular biomarkers may provide additional information about disease activity. This review discusses the potential role of non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) as diagnostic and therapeutic tools in AAAs. These molecules, including microRNAs (miRNAs), long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) and circular RNAs (circRNAs), are strongly involved in the regulation of gene expression. Through binding to their target mRNAs, miRNAs primarily suppress translation or promote mRNA degradation. Some lncRNAs and circRNAs act as miRNA sponges, affecting their availability. Here, these mechanisms are discussed by pathological function, distinguishing human tissue and circulating studies from animal, cellular and computational findings. Particular attention is given to miR-21, H19, GAS5, circCdyl and miR-26b-3p, which have functional experimental evidence or human biomarker data beyond expression profiling. Abnormal expression can be detected in peripheral blood or aortic tissue, but these findings do not necessarily predict aneurysm growth or rupture. Integration of ncRNA profiling with imaging and clinical parameters may improve the assessment of AAAs. However, prospective validation and further studies of delivery and safety are needed before these molecules can be used in clinical practice.

title: Age-dependent impact of diabetes on limb events and mortality in patients with peripheral artery disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is associated with substantial risks of limb events and mortality. Although diabetes is a recognized risk factor for adverse outcomes in PAD, its prognostic impact across different ages at PAD onset remains unclear. METHODS: In this retrospective population-based cohort study, adults with PAD were identified from Clalit Health Services, Israel (2000-2026). Patients were stratified by diabetes status and age at PAD diagnosis (35-50 vs > 50 years). The primary outcome was major adverse limb events (MALE), defined as lower-extremity revascularization or major amputation. All-cause mortality was a secondary outcome. Multivariable Cox regression, interaction analyses, and propensity score overlap weighting were performed. RESULTS: P P P P Among 4538 patients aged 35-50 years at PAD diagnosis, 1902 (42%) had diabetes. During a median follow-up of 12.0 years, diabetes was independently associated with higher risks of MALE (hazard ratio [HR] 1.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.03-2.01,= .032) and mortality (HR 1.41, 95% CI 1.18-1.70,< .001). Diabetes was associated with increased MALE risk in both age groups, with no significant interaction by age (for interaction = .498). In contrast, the association between diabetes and mortality was significantly stronger in patients aged 35-50 years than in those aged >50 years (adjusted HR 2.00, 95% CI 1.72-2.33 vs 1.30, 95% CI 1.27-1.33,for interaction < .001). Excess mortality associated with diabetes emerged during longer-term follow-up. CONCLUSION: Diabetes was associated with increased risks of MALE and mortality in PAD, with a stronger association with mortality among patients diagnosed before age 50. These findings identify diabetes as a marker of particularly high risk in premature PAD.

title: Cardiovascular complications as a consequence of coronavirus infection in pregnant women managed in ambulatory settings.
abstract: BACKGROUND: SARS-CoV-2 has been linked to cardiovascular complications in the general population. However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. In this retrospective population-based matched cohort study, we evaluated whether COVID-19 infection during pregnancy is associated with an increased incidence of cardiovascular complications among pregnant women managed predominantly in outpatient settings. METHODS: p We conducted a retrospective population-based matched cohort study using electronic health record data from pregnant women between 2020 and 2025. Women with COVID-19 during pregnancy were matched 1:1 to women without documented COVID-19 during pregnancy according to demographic, obstetric, and clinical characteristics. The final analytical cohort included 4,068 women in each group. Cardiovascular outcomes during pregnancy and within a year since last menstrual period were assessed. Baseline demographic and obstetric characteristics were comparable between the COVID-19 and control groups. No significant differences were observed between the groups in the incidence of major cardiovascular complications, either when analyzed individually or as a composite endpoint (0.15% vs. 0.15%; OR 1.00, 95% CI 0.27-3.74). Specifically, there were no significant differences in the occurrence of atrial fibrillation/flutter, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, or deep venous thrombosis. In contrast, cough and backache were significantly more frequent among women with COVID-19 than among matched controls (6.88% vs. 4.87%; OR 1.45, 95% CI 1.19-1.75; 13.8% vs. 11.8%; OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05-1.37; = 0.007 respectively). CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that among pregnant women in ambulatory community settings, COVID-19 infection is not associated with an increased risk of major cardiovascular complications.

However, data regarding cardiovascular outcomes among pregnant women remain limited, particularly in community-based ambulatory populations, as most previous studies focused primarily on hospitalized or critically ill patients. title: Anxiety in patients with lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis: a patient-centred sequential explanatory mixed-methods study of prevalence, associated factors, and patient experiences.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lower extremity deep vein thrombosis (LEDVT) is associated with substantial psychological burden. Anxiety after DVT may reflect not only an emotional consequence of thrombosis, but also a signal of unmet informational, functional, and supportive care needs. This study aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with anxiety among LEDVT patients and to explore their lived experiences, perceived triggers, and support needs using a mixed-methods design. METHODS: A sequential explanatory mixed-methods study was conducted. In the quantitative phase, 175 LEDVT patients completed the Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7 (GAD-7), Brief Illness Perception Questionnaire (B-IPQ), and Multidimensional Scale of Perceived Social Support (MSPSS). Clinical and care-process variables were collected, including the perceived adequacy of structured counselling at diagnosis using an 8-item checklist. Clinically significant anxiety was defined as GAD-7 score ≥10. Multivariable logistic regression was performed according to a prespecified conceptual framework. In the qualitative phase, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 purposively selected participants; data were analyzed using thematic analysis. RESULTS: P P P P The prevalence of clinically significant anxiety was 41.1% (72/175; 95% CI: 33.9%-48.6%). Younger age (OR = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.92-0.98, = 0.002), higher B-IPQ score (OR = 1.18, 95% CI: 1.11-1.26, < 0.001), lower MSPSS score (OR = 0.94, 95% CI: 0.90-0.98, = 0.005), and adequate counselling at diagnosis (OR = 0.42, 95% CI: 0.20-0.88, = 0.022) were independently associated with anxiety. Qualitative analysis generated five major themes: fear of complications, treatment-related anxiety, role and functional impairment, information delivery and illness meaning-making, and insufficient emotional and social support. CONCLUSION: Anxiety affects approximately two in five LEDVT patients in this single-centre cross-sectional cohort. Anxiety was associated not only with younger age, negative illness perception, and low social support, but also with symptom burden and perceived inadequacy of counselling at diagnosis; qualitative findings additionally highlighted symptom burden and functional limitations as key experiential drivers of anxiety. Integrated DVT care should address anticoagulation management, structured education, risk communication, cognitive reframing, functional recovery, and psychosocial support.

title: Risk factors of major bleeding associated with direct oral anticoagulant treatment in patients with venous thromboembolism: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are commonly prescribed for venous thromboembolism (VTE), but major bleeding (MB) remains an important complication of treatment. Despite their widespread use, systematic evaluations of prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment remain scarce. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE. This study seeks to enhance the safety and efficacy of anticoagulation therapy for VTE patients. METHOD AND RESULTS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to search the PubMed and Web of Science databases for studies published before September 18, 2026. The review adhered to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria to identify studies that investigated risk factors for major bleeding associated with DOAC treatment in patients diagnosed with VTE. Among the evaluated prognostic factors, quantitative pooling was possible only for age, which was reported in two studies; the remaining factors were summarized individually. Low-certainty evidence from a single study suggested a possible association between non-recommended dosing regimens and major bleeding. Evidence regarding declining adherence was also limited and of very low certainty. For age, very low-certainty evidence from the pooled analysis of two studies did not demonstrate a statistically significant association with major bleeding. CONCLUSION: The available evidence suggests possible associations between several prognostic factors and major bleeding in patients with VTE treated with DOACs; however, most findings are supported by low- or very low-certainty evidence and frequently by single studies. These findings should therefore be interpreted cautiously and require validation in larger, high-quality prospective studies.

To address this gap, we conducted a systematic review to identify prognostic factors associated with major bleeding during DOAC treatment in patients with VTE.

title: Case Report: Brucella-associated complications following thoracic endovascular aortic repair: a case series of three patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Brucellosis is a rare but potentially fatal cause of vascular graft infection. Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. Case presentation: We report three elderly male patients who developed severe aortic complications following TEVAR, including pseudoaneurysm formation and aorto-esophageal fistula. All patients had a history of epidemiological exposure to Brucella and were diagnosed with active infection through serological testing (Rose Bengal test, serum agglutination test, Brucella IgG and IgM antibodies). Endovascular re-intervention combined with targeted anti-brucellosis therapy was performed in all cases. RESULTS: One patient achieved sustained clinical remission after repeat endovascular repair and prolonged antimicrobial therapy. Two patients developed catastrophic infectious complications, including mediastinal abscess and aorto-esophageal fistula, resulting in death despite aggressive management. CONCLUSIONS: Brucella infection should be considered in patients presenting with unexplained symptoms after TEVAR, especially in endemic regions. Endovascular repair plays a critical role in acute stabilization; however, long-term outcomes remain highly dependent on effective infection control.

Evidence regarding Brucella-associated complications after thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) remains limited. title: Circle of Willis Anatomical Variations on CT Angiography: Prevalence and Clinical Associations in a Turkish Cohort.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Materials and Methods: Results: Conclusions: Anatomical variations in the Circle of Willis (CoW) may influence cerebral collateral pathways and the interpretation of vascular imaging. This study characterized their prevalence and clinical associations in a Turkish computed tomography angiography (CTA) cohort using complementary patient-level and component-level classifications.This retrospective, single-center study included 248 patients who underwent cranial CTA during 2024. Two radiologists independently assessed CoW anatomy, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Mutually exclusive patient-level configurations and non-exclusive arterial components were recorded. Associations with demographic and clinical characteristics were evaluated using logistic regression.A normal configuration was identified in 142 patients (57.3%), and 106 (42.7%) had at least one variant. Isolated posterior communicating artery (PComA) hypoplasia/aplasia was the most frequent configuration (14.5%); PComA involvement reached 19.0% when mixed configurations were included. Isolated fetal-type posterior cerebral artery, P1 hypoplasia, and A1 hypoplasia occurred in 7.3%, 6.5%, and 4.8%, respectively. Older age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] per 10 years, 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.23-2.01) and migraine (aOR, 5.67; 95% CI, 2.06-15.56) were associated with variant anatomy. Previous stroke/transient ischemic attack and carotid stenosis showed inverse associations.CoW variants were common in this Turkish clinical cohort, particularly in the posterior circulation. Reporting both overall configurations and individual arterial components provides complementary information relevant to anatomical assessment, vascular imaging interpretation, and procedural planning.
