title: Aneurysm Sac Expansion After EVAR: Associated Factors, Prognostic Impact, and Preventive Strategies-A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Aneurysm sac expansion is an adverse marker of durability after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). We assessed factors associated with expansion, its prognostic significance, and the effect of preventive embolisation.PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched through 23 August 2026 (PROSPERO CRD420261386132). Random-effects meta-analyses analysed odds ratios (ORs), hazard ratios (HRs), and risk ratios (RRs) separately; risk of bias and certainty were assessed with RoB 2, ROBINS-I, QUIPS, and GRADE.Thirty-three reports (20 independent quantitative studies) were included. Type II endoleak (OR 5.16, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.53-10.50; HR 3.08, 95% CI 2.11-4.49) and type I endoleak (OR 11.94, 95% CI 5.30-26.90) were associated with expansion (low certainty). Expansion was associated with higher late mortality in a single independent adjusted cohort (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.14-1.51; very low certainty). Preventive embolisation was associated with lower risks of persistent type II endoleak (RR 0.58, 95% CI 0.34-0.97; low certainty) and reintervention (RR 0.44, 95% CI 0.24-0.82; very low certainty), but neither association remained statistically conclusive in sensitivity analyses.Endoleaks are consistently associated with sac expansion, which appears to identify patients at increased late risk. Effects of preventive embolisation on surrogate outcomes are not robust; prevention of sac expansion and clinical events is unproven.

title: Aortic Endograft Infection After COVID-19: A Single-Centre Case Series and a Proposed Descriptive Clinical-Radiological PET/CT Staging Framework.
abstract: Background Methods Results Conclusions n n : Aortic endograft infection (AEI) after endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is rare but life-threatening. The Management of Aortic Graft Infection Collaboration (MAGIC) criteria define infection, but there is no standard way to report the extent of infection. We describe patients who developed AEI after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and propose a descriptive clinical-radiological PET/CT staging framework.: Retrospective, single-centre case series of EVAR patients who underwent [18F] fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) between 2020 and 2023. Six index patients (Group A) were managed for AEI after PCR-confirmed COVID-19. Five reference patients without COVID-19, imaged during the same period for suspected infection at another site (Group B,= 2) or malignancy (Group C,= 3), were included to describe endograft uptake in the absence of AEI; they were not matched controls. Each patient was classified according to MAGIC, with the finding supporting each criterion recorded. Each endograft was assigned a descriptive clinical-radiological stage (0-III): Stages 0-II were defined by PET/CT uptake pattern and anatomical extent, and Stage III by an additional imaging-defined (e.g., endograft limb thrombosis) or clinical (sepsis) complication, recorded separately.: Mean age was 76 years (9 men). Of the six index patients, one (Case 6, organism cultured from the explanted endograft) met the MAGIC definition of diagnosed AEI and five met that of suspected AEI. All six presented with fever, and every index patient had at least one additional source of bacteraemia or cause of immunosuppression, including corticosteroids given for COVID-19 pneumonia. Five had iliopsoas abscess. Four index endografts were classified as Stage III (clinical complication, sepsis, in all four; imaging-defined complication, endograft limb thrombosis, also in one) and two as Stage II; all five reference endografts were Stage 0. The median interval from COVID-19 to AEI diagnosis was 14 months (IQR 10-16), and from EVAR to PET/CT 15 months (IQR 4-35). Three index patients died (two infection- or aorta-related), and all three Group C patients died of malignancy progression.: This case series describes late AEI, frequently with iliopsoas involvement, in patients with prior COVID-19 and multiple other risk factors. The design does not permit any conclusion as to whether COVID-19 contributes to endograft infection. The proposed descriptive clinical-radiological PET/CT framework may help standardise the reporting of disease extent alongside MAGIC-based diagnosis but requires validation in larger, independent cohorts before any diagnostic or therapeutic use.

The Management of Aortic Graft Infection Collaboration (MAGIC) criteria define infection, but there is no standard way to report the extent of infection. We describe patients who developed AEI after coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) and propose a descriptive clinical-radiological PET/CT staging framework.: Retrospective, single-centre case series of EVAR patients who underwent [18F] fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (FDG PET/CT) between 2020 and 2023.

title: MicroRNAs as Diagnostic Biomarkers for Deep Vein Thrombosis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusion: In patients with suspected acute deep vein thrombosis (DVT), new blood biomarkers with high specificity for DVT could potentially lower the proportion of patients requiring imaging. The plasma microRNAs (miRs) miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p and miR-210-3p have been proposed as diagnostic biomarkers of venous thromboembolism, but their diagnostic accuracy for acute DVT has not been investigated. We aimed to assess the diagnostic performance of miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p and miR-210-3p for DVT in patients with suspected first-lifetime acute lower-extremity DVT.This prospective cross-sectional study consecutively included outpatients with suspected first-lifetime acute lower-extremity DVT. Plasma levels of miRs were measured using reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction. DVT status was determined by whole-leg duplex compression ultrasonography. Diagnostic test performance was assessed by the area under the curves (AUCs) from receiver operating characteristic curves with corresponding 95% confidence intervals (95% CI). The diagnostic accuracy of D-dimer was also assessed for comparison.Among the 360 patients included in this study, 28% had a first-lifetime acute lower-extremity DVT. The AUCs for miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p, and miR-210-3p ranged from 0.53 to 0.57, with 95% CIs overlapping 0.50. D-dimer had a sensitivity of 97% and specificity of 41% using the cut-off value of 0.5 µg/mL.Plasma miR-134-5p, miR-103a-3p and miR-210-3p showed poor diagnostic test performance for DVT. Our findings suggest that these miRs would not be helpful in discriminating between patients in whom DVT can be safely excluded and those who require imaging.

title: Parenteral Nutrition as a Strategic Therapeutic Option for Onco-Geriatric Rehabilitation After Total Gastrectomy and Anastomotic Stenosis Complicated by an Aorto-Esophageal Fistula: A Case Report.
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance Case Presentation Conclusions : The nutritional management of onco-geriatric patients after a total gastrectomy remains a challenge, especially in the context of postoperative complications, such as stenosis of the esophagojejunal anastomosis, and in the presence of an aorto-esophageal fistula. Parenteral nutrition is a relevant therapeutic option to maintain nutritional support and enable rehabilitation when oral and enteral feeding are no longer feasible in this specific clinical context;: We report here the case of a 76-year-old patient who underwent a total gastrectomy for gastric adenocarcinoma with several dilated and stented esophagojejunal anastomoses. During the first postoperative year, the nutritional adaptation facilitated rehabilitation and helped him recover well. However, the occurrence of an aorto-esophageal fistula and its treatment with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) made oral and enteral feeding impossible. This was associated with persistent asthenia, physical deconditioning, sarcopenia, weight loss, exercise intolerance, and increased dependence for activities of daily living. Although parenteral nutrition allowed for nutritional stability and the beginning of rehabilitation, a suspected nosocomial infection involving the aortic endograft led to his death before his treatment was complete;: This case highlights the relevance of parenteral nutrition as a therapeutic option to continue rehabilitation when enteral access is judged unacceptably risky. However, the risk of infectious complications in the context of malnutrition can compromise the prognosis, and any suspicion of infection involving prosthetic material should be documented microbiologically as completely as possible whenever compatible with the patient's care objectives. Onco-geriatric assessment to manage older patients with esophagogastric cancer is recommended.

title: A clinical risk score for early thrombosis detection in acute and chronic pancreatitis: insights from a large cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of preventable in-hospital mortality, yet disease-specific risk profiles remain poorly defined. In pancreatitis, one of the most common gastrointestinal causes of hospitalisation, thromboembolic complications are under-recognised, with limited data, especially on extrasplanchnic events. Evidence guiding screening and management remains scarce. We analysed VTE events in a large prospective cohort of patients with acute and chronic pancreatitis and derived a simple admission-time clinical risk score to support early identification of high-risk individuals. METHODS: We performed a retrospective analysis of a prospectively recruited cohort at LMU Klinikum Munich, a referral centre for pancreatic diseases. Patients with acute, acute-on-chronic or chronic pancreatitis evaluated between January 2018 and June 2023 were included. Comprehensive clinical, laboratory, imaging and outcome data were extracted. The primary objective was to identify admission-time factors associated with VTE and develop a clinically actionable risk score. Continuous variables were dichotomised using receiver operating characteristic (ROC)-derived optimal cut-points. Binary predictors were entered into a multivariable logistic regression model, and coefficients were scaled to generate an integer-based point score. Discrimination was assessed using the area under the ROC curve (AUC), and patients were stratified into low-risk, intermediate-risk and high-risk groups. RESULTS: Among 647 patients, 114 (17.6%) developed VTE, with similar incidence rates in acute (59, 16.2%) and chronic pancreatitis (55, 19.5%). Deep vein thrombosis (5.9%) and pulmonary embolism (4.2%) were the most frequent events. Patients with VTE experienced significantly worse clinical courses, including longer hospitalisation (15 vs 7 days, p<0.001), higher rates of severe pancreatitis and increased need for advanced analgesia. Thrombosis was associated with lower diastolic blood pressure, reduced oxygen saturation, tachycardia, older age and lower body mass index at admission as well as higher rates of systemic and local complications. Mortality was markedly higher in patients with VTE (8.8% vs 2.1%, p=0.029). A six-item admission-only risk score (0-8 points) demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.71) and effectively stratified patients into low-risk (7.6%), intermediate-risk (22.0%) and high-risk groups (38.5%). CONCLUSION: VTE is common in pancreatitis and strongly associated with adverse outcomes. A simple admission-time clinical score reliably identifies high-risk patients and may support earlier recognition, targeted diagnostic evaluation and risk stratification.

In pancreatitis, one of the most common gastrointestinal causes of hospitalisation, thromboembolic complications are under-recognised, with limited data, especially on extrasplanchnic events. Evidence guiding screening and management remains scarce.

title: In-hospital vascular surgery consultation is associated with improved follow-up and earlier identification of aneurysmal degeneration after acute Type A aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute Type A aortic dissections (TAAD) are historically managed by cardiac surgery. However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD. METHODS: Patients who underwent surgical intervention for acute TAAD from 2014 to 2025 were identified. Patients who experienced death within 30-days or those with dissection limited to Zone 0/Zone 1 were excluded. Vascular surgery evaluation and time to consultation (index-hospitalization, outpatient, none) was documented. Follow-up was classified as complete, incomplete, or lost (LTF) according to the frequency of contrasted thoracoabdominal imaging, consistent with clinical practice guidelines. Trends in completeness of follow-up were described. Demographics, anatomic/operative characteristics, and perioperative outcomes were compared between complete follow-up and incomplete follow-up/LTF groups. Long-term outcomes (aortic degeneration, planned secondary intervention, survival) were assessed with Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox regression analysis. RESULTS: 241 patients were included; 80% had vascular surgery consultation (70% inpatient, 30% outpatient) and 86% of consultations occurred within 1-year of index procedure. In total, 46% of patients had complete follow-up, 41% had incomplete follow-up, and 13% were LTF. In-hospital consultation increased by 58% over the study period. Demographics, comorbidities, and anatomic characteristics were similar between groups. Patients with complete follow-up had higher rates of complex arch repair (Zone 1-3) (complete 56% vs. incomplete/LTF 27%, p<0.001), were more likely to undergo genetic testing (complete 52% vs. incomplete/LTF 18%, p<0.001), in-hospital TEVAR extension (7% vs. 2%, p=0.028), and TEVAR extension within 3 months (complete 17% vs. incomplete/LTF 5%, p=0.002). In time-to-event analysis, complete follow-up was associated with more planned secondary interventions (complete: 12% vs. incomplete: 5%, p=0.007) and identified aneurysmal degeneration (32% vs. 15%, p=0.002) within 1-year of acute dissection. Long-term survival differed by completeness of follow-up; 1-year (complete: 97% vs. incomplete: 97% vs. LTF: 91%), 3-years (complete: 92% vs. incomplete: 95% vs. LTF: 81%, p=0.021). There were no aortic-related deaths for patients with complete follow-up and five aortic-related deaths (5%) in patients with incomplete follow-up (p=0.13). In-hospital vascular surgery consultation was associated with complete follow-up (HR 2.87, 95% CI 1.6-5.1) and planned secondary interventions (HR 2.07, 95% CI 1.1-3.9). CONCLUSION: Vascular surgery consultation is associated with increased identification of aneurysmal degeneration, planned secondary interventions, and mid-term survival. These data suggest that longitudinal vascular surgical care, starting with in-hospital consultation, is a critical component of care following acute TAAD and should be strongly considered to ensure appropriate postoperative surveillance and improve long-term patient outcomes.

However, subsequent treatment of residual dissection within the thoracoabdominal aorta often requires vascular surgical intervention and lifelong surveillance. This study assesses long-term outcomes by completeness of follow-up after operative intervention for acute TAAD.

title: Optimizing Vessel Preparation in Femoropopliteal Lesions: Does the Chocolate Balloon Deliver on Its Clinical Promise?
abstract: The "leave nothing behind" paradigm using drug-coated balloons (DCBs) has reshaped femoropopliteal peripheral artery disease treatment, though clinical success remains heavily contingent upon optimal vessel preparation. In a recent issue of The American Journal of Cardiology, Li and colleagues address the limitations of conventional plain old balloon angioplasty (POBA) through a propensity score-matched analysis of 508 patients from the multicenter PROMISING registry, comparing specialized vessel preparation using the nitinol-constrained Chocolate balloon against POBA before DCB angioplasty. The Chocolate balloon significantly reduced the primary endpoint of bailout stenting (20.47% vs 29.92%) and facilitated larger final DCB diameters, though these acute mechanical advantages did not translate into statistically significant differences in clinical outcomes at 12 months. This commentary examines this striking "procedural-to-clinical paradox," highlighting how the potent antiproliferative effect of DCBs and the acute compensatory function of bailout stents may temporarily mask early clinical divergence. Given that cumulative mechanical failures of permanent metallic implants typically emerge beyond one year in hostile biomechanical environments, longer-term observation remains essential to capture the true clinical dividend of a stent-free strategy.

title: The Moderating Effects of Race and Ethnicity on a Motivational Interviewing Intervention for Improving Physical Health Among Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease: Secondary Analysis of a Pilot Randomized Trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In a pilot randomized trial, face-to-face or telephone motivational interviewing (MI) was more efficacious than a smartphone app after 3 months for increasing 6-minute walk distance (primary outcome) and reducing body weight (secondary outcome) in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD). Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses. METHODS: Community dwellers in Wichita, Kansas, were recruited through community outlets and screened for PAD. Consented participants were randomly assigned to MI (n=16) or an app (n=13). Survey instruments were used to measure SDOH, demographics, and adverse childhood experiences, which were assessed for their associations with 6-minute walk distance change and weight loss. Difference-in-differences (DiD) comparisons of median changes between SDOH strata were conducted using Wilcoxon and Kruskal-Wallis nonparametric tests. RESULTS: For 6-minute walk distance, pretest-posttest changes were significantly greater among participants of "other" race and ethnicity than among non-Hispanic White participants (DiD=44.0 m, 95% CI 19.2-164.2; P=.004), and no DiDs for other SDOH were significant. Significant median pretest-posttest increases in walking distance were observed in those with a college or higher educational attainment (48.8 m, 95% CI 28.0-61.4), unmarried individuals (40.4 m, 95% CI 0.5-56.0), those living with family (55.7 m, 95% CI 30.5-199.5), those who talked to and saw family or friends 3 or more times a week (46.4 m, 95% CI 17.2-69.4), and those without unmet daily needs (46.5 m, 95% CI 7.6-67.1). For weight loss, we did not observe significant DiDs with any SDOH. However, a significant median weight loss was observed in every SDOH stratum where we observed a significant increase in 6-minute walk distance. Significant weight loss was also observed in 5 additional SDOH strata: male individuals, household income below US $30,000, never served in military, employed status, and no stress. The improvements in weight loss and walking distance were highly consistent in both direction and size across SDOH strata. CONCLUSIONS: This pilot study was the first to explore potential SDOH-related intervention effect modification and heterogeneity. The significant association between walking distance and race and ethnicity suggested a potential effect modification. Significant pretest-posttest improvements in both outcomes were found in the same SDOH strata. The highly consistent evidence across both outcomes and all SDOH strata provided confidence in potential intervention efficacy and heterogeneity despite the small sample size. Our findings were consistent with established associations between SDOH and general functions in patients with PAD, suggesting likely mediation pathways through health literacy and social support. Future interventions should consider heterogeneity to target socially disadvantaged patients with PAD to bridge disparities and maximize benefits. Little is known about intervention heterogeneity related to social determinants of health (SDOH). OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore whether SDOH are associated with the MI intervention effects on walking distance and weight loss and generate intervention heterogeneity hypotheses.

title: Stent-graft placement for an axillosubclavian artery injury in a pediatric patient: A case report.
abstract: Axillosubclavian artery injury is a rare traumatic vascular injury associated with a high mortality rate. Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. Although endovascular stent-graft placement has emerged as a less invasive alternative to open surgery, its application in pediatric trauma patients remains poorly documented. In this report, we present the case of a pediatric patient with traumatic axillosubclavian artery injury successfully treated with stent-graft placement. A 13-year-old boy was transported to a referring hospital following a traffic accident and transferred to our emergency and critical care center. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography conducted on hospital day 2 revealed a pseudoaneurysm due to right axillosubclavian artery injury, prompting endovascular stent-graft placement. The patient was discharged on hospital day 23. Although contrast-enhanced computed tomography at 1-year after discharge confirmed severe stenosis within the stent graft, distal perfusion was maintained. Notably, no ischemic symptoms or growth disturbances were observed in the right upper limb at the 3-year follow-up. Endovascular stent-graft placement appears to be a viable treatment for axillosubclavian artery injury in selected pediatric patients, particularly adolescents.

Therefore, rapid diagnosis and appropriate treatment selection are critical for patient survival. title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies. AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design. METHODS: 2 2 PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using Iand τ. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE. RESULTS: 2 2 2 Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001). CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

title: Saint-Bonnet Doppler waveform classification system: a scoping review and evidence-based appraisal using AGREE II and AGREE-REX.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Doppler waveform interpretation is central to the diagnosis and surveillance of lower limb peripheral arterial disease (PAD). Despite widespread clinical use of duplex ultrasound (DUS) and hand-held Doppler (HHD), waveform terminology remains highly variable and non-standardised across institutions. The Saint-Bonnet classification, proposed by the French College of Teachers in Vascular Medicine (CEMV), offers a structured eight-category morphological framework mapped to haemodynamic severity. Its evidence base and methodological quality have never been formally appraised. METHODS: A scoping review was conducted following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). MEDLINE (Ovid) and Embase (Ovid) were searched from 1946 to November 2025. Studies describing, applying, validating, or evaluating the Saint-Bonnet classification were eligible. Data were extracted using a standardised form. Methodological quality was appraised using AGREE II (six domains) and AGREE-REX (three domains), independently by two reviewers (H.A. and F.A.). RESULTS: κ κ κ Seven studies met the inclusion criteria; all published between 2017 and 2022 from a single French vascular research group. The Saint-Bonnet classification achieved a categorisation rate of 98.2% across 1,033 waveforms, outperforming alternative systems. Inter-rater reliability was moderate ( ≈ 0.55). Waveform grade independently correlated with maximal walking distance, and waveform-guided ankle-brachial index (ABI) selection achieved near-perfect agreement with guideline standards (up to 1.00). Automated neural network classification reached = 0.79, approaching expert agreement. AGREE II appraisal revealed high scores for Clarity of Presentation and Scope & Purpose (97% and 83%), but low scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability (44% and 40%). AGREE-REX demonstrated high Clinical Applicability and Implementability. CONCLUSION: The Saint-Bonnet classification is a promising and practical framework for Doppler waveform interpretation, with consistent findings across the available studies. Low AGREE II scores for Rigour of Development and Applicability reflect gaps in its documented development and reporting rather than evidence against its clinical performance. However, all supporting evidence originates from a single, non-independent French research group, and the classification has not undergone external validation; broader adoption should await independent, multicentre confirmation of these findings.

Despite widespread clinical use of duplex ultrasound (DUS) and hand-held Doppler (HHD), waveform terminology remains highly variable and non-standardised across institutions. The Saint-Bonnet classification, proposed by the French College of Teachers in Vascular Medicine (CEMV), offers a structured eight-category morphological framework mapped to haemodynamic severity.

title: Optimization of direct oral anticoagulant prescribing in primary care: a pharmacotherapeutic review in real-world clinical practice and therapeutic efficiency.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Direct oral anticoagulants are among the first-line treatments for stroke prevention in patients with non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for the treatment and secondary prevention of venous thromboembolism. The increasing use of these agents poses challenges related to prescribing appropriateness, clinical safety. This study aims to evaluate the impact of a primary care pharmacist-led intervention on the appropriateness of DOAC prescribing, pharmacotherapeutic efficiency, and clinical outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective, quasi-experimental before-and-after study was conducted in the healthcare area of Xarxa Santa Tecla (Tarragonès and Baix Penedès, Spain). 791 patients receiving DOAC therapy were included. The intervention comprised multidisciplinary educational activities, individualized pharmacotherapeutic review, and communication of recommendations to prescribers. RESULTS: The mean age was 78.2 years, and 43.2% of patients had moderate or severe renal impairment. The pharmacotherapeutic review identified 527 patients (66.6%) as candidates for treatment optimization, through a proposed switch from apixaban to dabigatran. The pharmacist intervention was associated with changes in prescribing patterns among newly initiated patients, increasing the use of dabigatran. The economic analysis estimated savings of €75,508.81 from new treatment initiations and €31,288.25 from therapeutic switches, resulting in total savings of €106,797.06 in 2025. The overall bleeding rate remained stable (5.3% in 2024% vs. 5.2% in 2025), with no deterioration in clinical safety. In conclusion, a structured, multidisciplinary, and coordinated primary care pharmacist-led intervention promoted a more efficient use of healthcare resources, while no deterioration in population-level safety indicators was observed. These findings reinforce the role of primary care pharmacists in optimizing anticoagulant therapy.

title: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair: case report and analysis of existing literature.
abstract: Abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR) is an exceptionally rare and aggressive malignancy that may mimic common EVAR-related complications. We report the case of a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive lower back pain and was initially suspected of having a graft infection. Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm. Biopsy confirmed aortic angiosarcoma. No regional lymph node or distant metastases were identified. The patient underwent neoadjuvant chemotherapy with gemcitabine and docetaxel, followed by radiotherapy and surgical resection of the abdominal aorta and EVAR graft with aortic reconstruction. Histopathological examination demonstrated complete pathological response without evidence of residual angiosarcoma. Our literature review identified only 21 reported cases of abdominal aortic angiosarcoma following EVAR, including the present case, underscoring the exceptional rarity of this entity and the limited evidence available to guide diagnosis and treatment. This case highlights the importance of considering aortic angiosarcoma in patients with persistent symptoms and atypical periaortic findings after EVAR and suggests that early biopsy and a multidisciplinary, multimodal treatment approach may improve outcomes despite the generally poor prognosis associated with this disease.

We report the case of a 72-year-old man who presented with progressive lower back pain and was initially suspected of having a graft infection. Imaging revealed a periaortic mass involving a previously treated abdominal aortic aneurysm.

title: The prediagnostic period of Behçet's disease: a nationwide population-based study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD. METHODS: We conducted a nationwide retrospective matched case-control study using the electronic health records of Leumit Health Services. Patients with BD fulfilling the International Criteria for Behçet's Disease or International Study Group classification criteria were identified by manual chart review and matched 1:5 with controls by sex, age, socioeconomic category and year of first observation. Clinical diagnoses, diagnostic investigations and laboratory measurements and medication dispensing recorded during the five years preceding diagnosis were compared between groups. Early and late laboratory measurements within the prediagnostic period were analyzed to assess temporal trends. Manifestations documented over the entire available record were analyzed separately. RESULTS: 9 9 The study included 218 patients who subsequently developed BD and 1,090 matched controls. During the five years preceding diagnosis, future patients with BD more frequently exhibited oral aphthosis (36.2% vs 3.0%; OR 18.2), panuveitis (4.6% vs 0.1%; OR 52.4), inflammatory polyarthritis (7.3% vs 0.6%; OR 14.3), and venous thromboembolism (4.6% vs 0.2%; OR 26.2) (all P<0.001). Over the entire available record, oral aphthosis was documented in 61.0% of patients with BD and 11.8% of controls. Autoimmune serology was frequently requested but remained largely negative. Laboratory analyses demonstrated a biphasic trajectory. Absolute monocyte count and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio were lower than in controls at the early assessment (0.40 vs 0.44 ×10/L, P = 0.009, and 1.45 vs 1.49, P = 0.023) but significantly higher near diagnosis (0.64 vs 0.58 ×10/L, P = 0.025, and 2.44 vs 2.09, P = 0.003). This transition was accompanied by rising CRP, ESR, platelet count and globulin levels, persistently lower mean corpuscular volume and consistently higher IgA at both assessments (247 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.009, and 256 vs 189 mg/dL, P = 0.012), whereas IgG and IgM remained comparable between groups. CONCLUSIONS: BD seems to be preceded by a clinically and biologically active prediagnostic phase characterized by a distinct inflammatory multisystem footprint.
englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: The diagnosis of Behçet's disease (BD) is often delayed because its characteristic manifestations may emerge sequentially over time. Whether BD is preceded by a clinically active prediagnostic phase remains unclear. We aimed to characterize the clinical and laboratory features during the five-year period preceding the formal diagnosis of BD.

title: Anatomical distribution of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism: a retrospective study with finite-element analysis of calf muscle-vein mechanics.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Muscular calf vein thrombosis is frequently detected by whole-leg ultrasonography, but its relationship with pulmonary embolism (PE) and the mechanical response of the intramuscular veins during calf-muscle contraction remain incompletely defined. We examined PE prevalence across anatomical categories of lower-extremity deep vein thrombosis (DVT) and used a structural finite-element model to quantify contraction-related venous compression and identify the regions in which deformation was greatest. METHODS: This retrospective study included patients evaluated for a first episode of lower-extremity DVT between May and October 2022. DVT was classified as isolated muscular calf vein thrombosis, isolated axial calf DVT, isolated proximal DVT, or combined muscular calf and proximal DVT. PE was diagnosed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography or pulmonary perfusion imaging. Because several cells contained few observations, the four-group distribution was compared using a Fisher-Freeman-Halton exact test. A separate finite-element analysis used one normal computed tomography angiography geometry. Gastrocnemius contraction, soleus contraction, and co-contraction were modeled as structural loading conditions. Spatial stress and strain maps were examined to localize venous regions with the greatest structural response. No blood-flow, venous-valve, or thrombus model was included. RESULTS: p 3 Among 160 patients with DVT, 30 had PE. PE was present in 14 of 125 patients with isolated muscular calf vein thrombosis [11.2%, exact 95% confidence interval (CI): 6.3%-18.1%], 1 of 4 with isolated axial calf DVT (25.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-80.6%), 3 of 10 with isolated proximal DVT (30.0%, 95% CI: 6.7%-65.2%), and 12 of 21 with combined muscular calf and proximal DVT (57.1%, 95% CI: 34.0%-78.2%). The overall distribution differed across groups (exact < 0.001). At the final recorded model-loading parameter, mean muscle von Mises stress was 21.51 kPa during gastrocnemius contraction, 1.16 kPa during soleus contraction, and 9.68 kPa during co-contraction. The corresponding changes in modeled venous-domain volume were -49.25, -17.07, and -64.08 mm, respectively. The spatial maps showed nonuniform venous deformation, with the most prominent response concentrated around proximal branching regions and adjacent intramuscular venous segments. CONCLUSIONS: PE prevalence differed across the anatomical DVT categories and was highest when muscular calf and proximal veins were involved concurrently. The structural model provided direct evidence that calf-muscle contraction compresses deep veins and localized the regions of greatest deformation. These findings support targeted dynamic venous imaging, while effects on blood flow and thrombus behavior require prospective patient-specific validation.

title: Association of red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Critically ill patients with aortic dissection remain at high risk of adverse ICU outcomes, including ICU mortality. The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection. METHODS: Data were extracted from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database. ICU mortality was defined as the primary outcome. Secondary outcomes included sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay, acute kidney injury (AKI), and renal replacement therapy (RRT) use. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to assess the discriminative performance of RAR for ICU mortality. The optimal RAR cutoff was determined using Youden's index and was considered exploratory. Calibration plots and decision curve analysis were used to evaluate model performance. RESULTS: P P P RAR showed modest discrimination for ICU mortality (AUC: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.552-0.765). The exploratory cutoff value of RAR was 5.182. Compared with the low-RAR group, the high-RAR group had higher ICU mortality (21.8% vs. 6.7%; < 0.001), a higher prevalence of sepsis during hospitalization/ICU stay (82.8% vs. 61.1%; < 0.001), and more frequent RRT use (33.3% vs. 9.4%; < 0.001). The AUC increased from 0.706 for SOFA alone to 0.731 for SOFA plus RAR, indicating only limited incremental discrimination. CONCLUSION: Higher early-ICU RAR was associated with ICU mortality and other adverse ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection, but its discrimination was modest, its incremental value beyond SOFA was limited, and external validation is required.

The red cell distribution width-to-albumin ratio (RAR) has been investigated as a prognostic marker in various clinical settings. This study aimed to evaluate the association of RAR with ICU outcomes in patients with aortic dissection.

title: Organ Malperfusion and Mortality in Acute Type 1 Aortic Dissection with Iliac Extension: A Retrospective Single-Center Study Focused on Mesenteric Malperfusion and the Source-Clearance Hypothesis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n n n Mesenteric malperfusion is the most lethal and least recognizable complication of acute type A aortic dissection. This study aimed to examine organ-specific malperfusion patterns and 30-day mortality in acute type 1 aortic dissection with iliac extension, and to evaluate whether the lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR) and superior mesenteric artery (SMA) origin pattern add predictive value for mesenteric malperfusion syndrome within a "source-clearance" framework.In this retrospective single-center study, 80 consecutive patients with acute type 1 aortic dissection extending to the iliac arteries who underwent surgical repair between January 2020 and March 2026 were reviewed. Malperfusion (preoperative finding) and malperfusion syndrome (end-organ injury persisting despite central repair) were defined for six organ systems; visceral branch origin and planimetric true lumen ratio were assessed on computed tomography angiography (CTA). The primary endpoint was 30-day mortality.Thirty-day mortality was 33.8%; 60% of patients had malperfusion, and mortality rose with the number of organs involved (0/1/≥2: 12.5%/32.1%/70.0%). Mesenteric malperfusion (= 21) carried the highest mortality (71.4%); all nine patients who developed mesenteric syndrome died. Cerebral malperfusion was most frequent (= 27); all nine who improved postoperatively survived, whereas mortality was 81.8% in the 22 who developed the syndrome. Preoperative shock or cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) (odds ratio [OR] = 7.02), mesenteric malperfusion (OR = 6.24), LAR (OR = 1.07 per 0.01 unit) and Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS; OR = 0.75 per point) were independent predictors. LAR and SMA origin pattern were uncorrelated (r = -0.04) and together raised the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for mesenteric syndrome from 0.861 to 0.955; mortality was 75% with mixed SMA origin (= 8).Malperfusion is a dose-dependent risk spectrum; mesenteric involvement is its most lethal component, increasing mortality six-fold independently of hemodynamic and metabolic status. Joint interpretation of LAR and SMA origin pattern offers a practical, validation-pending framework for perioperative management of the mesenteric circulation in centers without a hybrid operating room.

title: Factors Associated with Major Versus Minor Lower Extremity Amputation in Hospitalized Patients with Diabetes in Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Background Methods Results Conclusions : Major lower extremity amputation (LEA) is a severe complication of diabetes with substantial disability and mortality. Evidence from Saudi Arabia with distinguishing factors linked to major versus minor amputation is limited. We examined demographic, clinical, vascular, and wound-related factors associated with amputation level among hospitalized patients with diabetes who had already undergone LEA.: We conducted a retrospective comparative observational study of 230 adults with diabetes who underwent non-traumatic LEA at Al Noor Specialist Hospital, Makkah. Because the cohort comprised exclusively patients who had already undergone amputation, the analysis was explanatory in purpose and characterized factors associated with the level of amputation (major versus minor) rather than predictors of amputation occurrence in the broader population of patients with diabetic foot disease. Independent associations were examined using multivariable binary logistic regression with Firth's penalization; adjusted odds ratios (aORs) with 95% confidence intervals were the principal results, and exploratory model diagnostics.: Major amputation occurred in 92 patients (40.0%); 138 (60.0%) underwent minor amputation. Mean age was 58.4 ± 12.6 years; 77.0% were male. After adjustment, ischemic heart disease (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 5.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.63-16.55), multiple foot ulcers (aOR 4.65, 95% CI 1.53-14.17), ulcer duration >1 month (aOR 3.15, 95% CI 1.09-9.10), and documented peripheral neuropathy (aOR 7.46, 95% CI 1.13-49.35) were independently associated with major amputation. The neuropathy estimate was imprecise, reflecting the small number of documented cases, and should therefore be regarded as highly uncertain. These exploratory associations describe the conditional comparison of amputation level within this operated cohort and should not be interpreted as individual probabilities of amputation or amputation level.: Ischemic heart disease, multiple ulcers, prolonged ulcer duration, and documented peripheral neuropathy were associated with major amputation. These associations should be interpreted within the limits of a retrospective, single-center design with possible underascertainment of neuropathy and peripheral arterial disease. These exploratory findings require replication in independent, prospectively designed cohorts before they can be generalized to other settings or applied clinically.

Evidence from Saudi Arabia with distinguishing factors linked to major versus minor amputation is limited. We examined demographic, clinical, vascular, and wound-related factors associated with amputation level among hospitalized patients with diabetes who had already undergone LEA.: We conducted a retrospective comparative observational study of 230 adults with diabetes who underwent non-traumatic LEA at Al Noor Specialist Hospital, Makkah.

title: Baseline D-Dimer Predicts Subsequent Venous Thromboembolism in 23,505 Patients with One of 11 Solid Malignancies: An 11-Year Retrospective Cohort Study.
abstract: Background/Objectives Methods Results Conclusions : Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of cancer. The predictive performance of baseline D-dimer and factors influencing its levels among patients with cancer remain unclear. We aimed to identify predictors of subsequent VTE development and evaluate the cancer-specific predictive performance of baseline D-dimer.: This retrospective study included 23,505 patients with any of 11 malignancies who underwent baseline D-dimer measurement at initial diagnosis at Gifu University Hospital between January 2015 and December 2025. Patients with pre-existing VTE were excluded. Predictors were identified using logistic regression analyses. Cancer-specific predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analyses, with optimal cutoff values determined by the Youden index. Factors associated with baseline D-dimer were also assessed.: The median follow-up was 45.3 months (30.4-59.1 months), during which VTE occurred in 784 (3.3%) patients. Higher baseline D-dimer levels and distant metastasis were independent predictors of subsequent VTE. Cancer type was significantly associated with VTE overall, and breast cancer was associated with lower odds than esophageal cancer. D-dimer performance varied among cancer types, with optimal cutoff values of 0.55-2.35 μg/mL. Older age and higher platelet counts were independently associated with elevated baseline D-dimer levels, whereas a higher cholesterol level was inversely associated.: Baseline D-dimer level is an independent predictor of subsequent VTE in patients with cancer. Its predictive performance and exploratory thresholds vary among cancers, suggesting that cancer type should be considered when interpreting baseline D-dimer levels. External validation is required before these cancer-specific thresholds can be applied clinically.

title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Renal Safety of Carbon Dioxide Angiography in Lower Limb Angiography: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 2 p p 2 Iodinated contrast media (ICM) used in lower limb angiography carry risks of contrast-induced nephropathy (CIN) and allergic reactions, particularly in patients with peripheral arterial disease (PAD) and renal dysfunction. Carbon dioxide (CO) angiography offers a potential non-nephrotoxic alternative. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy and renal safety of COangiography compared with ICM in patients undergoing lower limb angiography for PAD.A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was performed from inception to 4 September 2025. Studies comparing COangiography with ICM in adult PAD patients were included. Risk of bias was assessed with QUADAS-2 for diagnostic accuracy studies and RoB 2 for randomised trials, and the methodological quality of comparative observational studies with the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Pooled sensitivity, specificity, adverse events, CIN, contrast volume, serum creatinine, and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were analysed using random-effects models.Nine studies (527 patients) were included. In three studies (111 patients) with extractable diagnostic accuracy data, COangiography showed pooled sensitivity of 0.89 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.78-0.95) and specificity of 0.96 (95% CI: 0.85-0.99). Adverse events did not differ significantly between groups (four studies; risk ratio [RR] 0.63, 95% CI: 0.15-2.71), but discomfort during COinjection was common. CIN risk was lower with CO(two studies; RR 0.31, 95% CI: 0.14-0.73;= 0.007), and contrast volume was reduced by a mean of 80.71 mL (two studies;< 0.00001). Pooled serum creatinine and eGFR estimates showed extreme heterogeneity (I= 98-99%), with the two contributing studies reporting effects in opposite directions.In a small number of comparative studies, COangiography showed pooled sensitivity and specificity compatible with clinically useful diagnostic performance, although these exploratory estimates derive from three studies with unblinded reference standards. The lower risk of CIN with CO, observed in two studies, is hypothesis-generating, and COhas adverse effects of its own, principally discomfort during injection. These findings should be confirmed in larger prospective trials before COcan be regarded as an established alternative for patients at risk of CIN or iodine allergy.

title: Peripheral vascular trauma in a civilian Asian trauma centre: Epidemiology, management and outcomes over 9 years.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Peripheral vascular injuries (PVI) are uncommon but potentially limb-threatening complications of extremity trauma. Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore. METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the institutional trauma registry of Tan Tock Seng Hospital between January 2013 and December 2021. Patients presenting with upper or lower extremity vascular injuries were identified using Abbreviated Injury Scale (AIS) coding. Demographics, injury characteristics, anatomical injury patterns, interventions, and outcomes including limb salvage, complications, and inpatient mortality were analysed. Comparisons between upper and lower limb injuries were performed using appropriate statistical tests. RESULTS: Among 77,990 trauma admissions, 180 patients sustained PVI (incidence 0.23%). Median age was 36 years and 87% were male. Overall, penetrating trauma was more common (58.9%), but lower limb injuries were predominantly due to blunt trauma (68%), particularly road traffic accidents. Lower limb PVIs were associated with higher injury severity than upper limb PVIs (p < 0.001). Operative management was required in most arterial and venous injuries. Primary repair and endovascular interventions demonstrated excellent limb salvage, whereas bypass procedures were associated with lower salvage rates. Overall limb salvage for lower limb PVI was 88%, with an amputation rate of 10% and mortality of 3%. Most (93%) were functionally independent at discharge. CONCLUSIONS: PVI predominantly affects young male patients and are commonly associated with blunt trauma from road traffic accidents. Despite significant injury severity, favourable limb salvage and functional outcomes can be achieved with timely multidisciplinary management. These findings highlight the importance of coordinated multidisciplinary trauma care in optimizing outcomes following extremity vascular trauma.

Most existing literature originates from military settings or Western trauma systems. We aimed to describe the epidemiology, management strategies, and outcomes of traumatic PVI in a civilian tertiary trauma centre in Singapore.

title: Prevalence of Guideline-Recommended Genetic Testing in Patients at Risk for Heritable Thoracic Aortic Disease.
abstract: Heritable thoracic aortic diseases (HTAD) include genetic conditions that increase risk of thoracic aortic aneurysm and dissection. The 2022 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association (ACC/AHA) guidelines recommend genetic testing for at-risk individuals, but real-world uptake remains unclear. We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts. We conducted a retrospective study using the TriNetX Research Network (2005-2025). Three guideline-based cohorts were identified using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision, Clinical Modification (ICD-10-CM) codes: (1) thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, (2) family history of thoracic aortic disease, and (3) nonthoracic arterial aneurysms. Genetic testing was defined by ICD-10-CM codes for genetic screening or susceptibility. Testing prevalence was stratified by age, sex, race, and ethnicity, and annual testing incidence (2005-2024) was evaluated. Among 57,935 patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm/dissection before age 60, 1,205 (2.09%) underwent genetic testing. Among 2,811,862 patients with a family history of thoracic aortic disease, 66,699 (2.38%) received testing. Among 347,000 patients with nonthoracic arterial aneurysms, 4,913 (1.42%) underwent testing. Testing was consistently higher in females than males and varied across age groups. Annual testing incidence increased over time but remained <0.6% by 2024. In conclusion, genetic testing for HTAD remains markedly underutilized, with <2.5% of at-risk patients tested despite guideline recommendations, highlighting persistent implementation gaps and the need to improve equitable access to genetic evaluation.

We evaluated adherence to testing recommendations and demographic differences across major HTAD risk cohorts.

title: From recanalization to recovery: inflammation and futile reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) has markedly improved reperfusion outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by large-vessel occlusion. However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion. This clinical-angiographic mismatch may reflect persistent tissue injury, including inflammatory injury, alongside pretreatment damage and other determinants of outcome. Experimental findings and clinical associations implicate persistent inflammatory activation, thrombo-inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, microvascular no-reflow, and blood-brain barrier disruption as contributors to secondary tissue injury after MT. Here, we examine potential inflammatory contributions to futile reperfusion and consider how inflammatory biomarkers might inform risk stratification after MT. Ischemia activates microglia, endothelial cells, platelets, complement pathways, and circulating immune cells. Subsequent reperfusion may amplify oxidative stress, cytokine signaling, neutrophil-endothelial interactions, neutrophil extracellular trap formation, matrix metalloproteinase activity, and barrier failure. Together, these processes can promote microvascular obstruction, cerebral edema, hemorrhagic transformation, infarct growth, and impaired neurological recovery despite successful angiographic reperfusion. Among circulating biomarkers, the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio has been studied repeatedly, alongside platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio, systemic immune-inflammation index, systemic inflammation response index, interleukin-6, matrix metalloproteinase-9, and other molecular markers. Their specificity, incremental predictive value, and clinical utility require further validation in standardized thrombectomy cohorts. We therefore view inflammation as a plausible biological link between macrovascular reperfusion and persistent tissue-level injury after MT. From a translational perspective, the immediate priorities are to standardize sampling protocols, characterize dynamic inflammatory trajectories, develop multimodal prediction models, and test biomarker-guided therapeutic strategies.

However, successful angiographic reperfusion does not invariably translate into functional independence. Poor functional outcome despite successful angiographic reperfusion is commonly described as futile reperfusion.

title: Knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding venous thromboembolism prevention in patients with lung cancer.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with lung cancer are at high risk of venous thromboembolism (VTE), yet their awareness and preventive behaviors remain insufficiently characterized. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VTE prevention among patients with lung cancer and explored factors associated with these dimensions. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 patients with lung cancer recruited at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital between January and May 2026. Participants completed a KAP questionnaire regarding VTE prevention. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify factors associated with KAP outcomes, and Pearson correlation analysis was used to examine the associations among knowledge, attitudes, and practices. RESULTS: The mean knowledge, attitude, and practice scores were 8.98 ± 3.52, 31.18 ± 3.37, and 19.19 ± 4.49, respectively. Rural or suburban residence (adjusted OR = 0.447, 95% CI 0.201-0.992) and no previous VTE education (adjusted OR = 0.271, 95% CI 0.147-0.501) were associated with lower odds of meeting the operational knowledge threshold. Higher knowledge scores were associated with more favorable attitudes and higher self-reported preventive practice scores, while higher attitude scores were associated with higher self-reported preventive practice scores. CONCLUSION: Patients with lung cancer showed persistent gaps in VTE-related knowledge, generally favorable responses to several attitude items, and heterogeneous self-reported preventive behaviors. The findings highlight potential targets for patient education, particularly among rural or suburban residents and those without previous VTE education.

This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and practices (KAP) regarding VTE prevention among patients with lung cancer and explored factors associated with these dimensions. METHODS: This cross-sectional study included 244 patients with lung cancer recruited at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital between January and May 2026.

title: Machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with venous thromboembolism and acute kidney injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI. METHODS: n n In this retrospective study, data from 585 ICU patients with VTE and AKI were analyzed. Patients were divided into a training cohort ( = 409) and a validation cohort ( = 176). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with standardization was applied for feature selection. Five machine learning models-logistic regression (LR), random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM), and support vector machine (SVM)-were developed and evaluated using 5-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Decision curve analysis (DCA), SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and feature importance were performed for the optimal model. The performance of the best machine learning model was compared with conventional ICU severity scores (APSIII, LODs, and OASIS). RESULTS: The standardized LASSO regression identified ten optimal predictors: creatinine (cr), age, tumor/cancer, body mass index (BMI), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), urine output, D-dimer (D_D), Charlson comorbidity index, anticoagulant use, and alanine aminotransferase (ALT). Among the five models, XGBoost achieved the best predictive performance with a validation AUC of 0.882 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.832-0.924], followed by RF (AUC = 0.878), LightGBM (AUC = 0.870), LR (AUC = 0.838), and SVM (AUC = 0.662). The 5-fold cross-validation AUC for XGBoost was 0.901 ± 0.042, with minimal overfitting (CV-test difference = -0.019). Decision curve analysis demonstrated favorable clinical net benefit of the XGBoost model across a wide range of threshold probabilities. SHAP analysis and feature importance consistently identified urine output, age, LDL, BMI, and D-dimer as the top contributors. Compared with conventional ICU severity scores, the XGBoost model significantly outperformed APSIII (AUC = 0.661), LODs (AUC = 0.652), and OASIS (AUC = 0.647). The logistic regression-based nomogram achieved a C-index of 0.838, providing a user-friendly bedside tool for clinicians. CONCLUSION: The machine learning-based XGBoost model, incorporating ten readily available clinical variables, demonstrated excellent predictive performance for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with VTE and AKI. This model offers a practical and interpretable tool for early risk stratification and may guide proactive nutritional and therapeutic interventions in this vulnerable population.
englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Hypoalbuminemia is a prevalent and critical complication among intensive care unit (ICU) patients with venous thromboembolism (VTE) and acute kidney injury (AKI), significantly associated with increased mortality and prolonged hospitalization. However, reliable tools for early prediction of hypoalbuminemia in this high-risk population remain limited. This study aimed to develop and validate a machine learning-based prediction model for hypoalbuminemia in ICU patients with coexisting VTE and AKI.

title: Factors associated with mortality in patients with atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
abstract: BACKGROUND: This study synthesized published meta-analyses to assess the quality, bias, and strength of evidence regarding mortality risk factors in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: Web of Science, Embase, PubMed, and Cochrane database were used to search the literature up to May 2025. Eligible studies were systematic reviews or meta-analyses investigating AF-related mortality risk factors. AMSTAR tool was used to assess methodological quality and GRADE was used to evaluate evidence certainty. RESULTS: A total of 216 risk factors were identified. Among them, 86 showed significant associations with mortality, while 130 did not. Based on GRADE ratings, 11 were high-quality significant factors, and 9 were of moderate-quality. Factors linked to increased mortality included certain medications (digoxin, dronedarone, sotalol; warfarin/VKA vs. NOAC was associated with higher mortality), comorbidities (cancer, COPD, diabetes, anemia, frailty, LVH, peripheral artery disease), demographic characteristics (older age, smoking, BMI <18.5, Latin American ethnicity), and AF subtype (persistent or non-paroxysmal). In contrast, reduced mortality was associated with NOAC or DOAC use, higher BMI (25-30 or ≥30), surgical interventions (catheter ablation, LAAC/LAAO), other medications (SGLT2 inhibitors, statins), and early rhythm control. CONCLUSION: Systematic Review Registration: This review highlights key factors associated with mortality in AF. Increased risk was observed with warfarin/VKA use (vs. NOAC), certain antiarrhythmic drugs, comorbidities, low BMI, older age, smoking, and non-paroxysmal AF. In contrast, NOAC use, surgical interventions, high BMI, statin and SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, and early rhythm-control strategies were linked to reduced mortality risk.https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024533372, PROSPERO CRD42024533372.

title: Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Pulmonary Embolism: Prevalence, Severity and the Association of Sleep-Disordered Breathing with Thromboembolic Disease.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p p Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and pulmonary embolism (PE) share several risk factors, while emerging evidence suggests a potential pathophysiological link beyond these common determinants. We aimed to characterize the prevalence and severity of OSA in patients with acute PE and to investigate whether the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) is independently associated with PE and its clinical course.In this prospective, single-center, case-control study, 128 consecutive patients with acute PE and 252 outpatient controls with other respiratory diseases underwent home respiratory polygraphy. In patients with PE, the sleep study was performed at least three months after the acute event. OSA was diagnosed and graded according to international consensus criteria. Logistic regression models were used to evaluate associations between AHI and PE, acute PE severity, chronic deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and venous thromboembolism (VTE) recurrence.OSA was present in 55.5% of patients with PE, with severe OSA in 28.9%, compared with 42.1% and 13.9%, respectively, among controls (= 0.013 and= 0.001). Patients with PE had a higher AHI (21.21 ± 19.29 vs. 14.81 ± 14.26 events/h;= 0.007) and oxygen desaturation index (19.86 ± 18.77 vs. 13.30 ± 13.79;= 0.003). Each 10-events/h increase in AHI was independently associated with PE after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and established VTE risk factors (OR 1.205, 95% CI 1.019-1.426;= 0.029). AHI was not independently associated with intermediate-high/high-risk PE or chronic DVT. Among patients who discontinued anticoagulation, VTE recurrence was higher in those with OSA (36.0% vs. 13.3%;= 0.049).OSA is highly prevalent and frequently severe in patients with acute PE. Increasing AHI is independently associated with the presence of PE, supporting a clinically relevant association between sleep-disordered breathing and thromboembolic disease. Because OSA was not systematically reassessed after documented resolution of PE, persistence of OSA independently of residual thromboembolic disease cannot be definitively established. Whether the observed association between OSA and recurrent VTE after anticoagulation withdrawal is confirmed in larger prospective studies remains to be determined.

abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Candida Staphylococcus aureus Candida S. aureus S. aureus S. aureus Catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSIs) may lead to metastatic complications. title: Deep Learning-Based Versus Threshold-Based Bone Removal for CT Angiography of Head and Neck Arteriovenous Fistulas: A Retrospective Comparison of Image Quality, Key-Structure Display, and Post-Processing Time.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p Bone overlap at the skull base limits CT angiography (CTA) in head and neck arteriovenous fistulas (hAVFs), and threshold-based bone removal fails where bone and contrast attenuation overlap. Whether deep learning-based removal improves the display of the structures that determine endovascular planning is unknown in a DSA-confirmed cohort. We therefore compared the two methods within the same CTA datasets.In this single-centre retrospective study, 35 patients with DSA-confirmed hAVF underwent head and neck CTA and digital subtraction angiography (DSA) within two weeks of each other, and each CTA dataset was post-processed with both methods on one workstation. Two blinded readers scored the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein (0 to 2 each) and overall image quality (5-point scale). Scores were compared with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests, vessel edge sharpness and post-processing time with paired t tests, and technical visualisation with McNemar's test.Deep learning-based removal displayed the fistula site, feeding artery and draining vein more completely (median total anatomical score 6.00 versus 3.00;< 0.001 for both readers) and overall image quality was higher (5.00 versus 4.00;< 0.001). Objective vessel edge sharpness was concordant (316.47 ± 46.68 versus 273.70 ± 45.66 HU/mm;< 0.001). Technical visualisation was numerically higher (97.1% versus 88.6%) but not significantly so (= 0.248; three discordant pairs), which makes this endpoint inconclusive rather than negative. Post-processing time was shorter (40.56 ± 1.61 s versus 101.70 ± 4.39 s; mean paired difference 61.14 s, 95% CI 59.53 to 62.74 s; paired t test,< 0.001).In DSA-confirmed hAVF, deep learning-based bone removal displayed the structures that determine endovascular planning more completely than threshold-based removal and was about one minute faster per case. It does not replace DSA for definitive assessment of fistula architecture, and the apparent advantage at the cavernous sinus is exploratory and requires external validation in larger multicentre cohorts.

title: Structural basis of DnaB ring opening by the ancestral helicase loader DciA.
abstract: Ring-shaped helicases must be opened and loaded onto DNA to initiate genome replication. In bacteria, most species lack canonical AAA+ helicase loaders and instead rely on DciA, an evolutionarily conserved, ATP-independent factor whose mechanism has remained unclear. Here we define how DciA remodels the bacterial replicative helicase DnaB. A 3.5 Å cryo-EM structure reveals a DnaB6·DciA3 complex in which DciA binds the periphery of the helicase and stabilizes a right-handed open-helical conformation with a single cracked interface. Three DciA molecules dock onto alternate linker-helix/docking-helix modules, while one N-terminal domain (NTD) engages the cracked interface, occupying the pocket vacated by the displaced linker helix and acting as a wedge to promote ring opening. Functional analyses reveal how DciA couples ATPase suppression with efficient helicase loading through coordinated actions of its NTDs and C-terminal domains. Together, these findings define a minimal, ATP-independent mechanism for helicase loading and show how an ancestral loader remodels DnaB to overcome a fundamental topological barrier.

title: A selective NVL inhibitor suppresses tumor growth by targeting ribosome biogenesis.
abstract: Ribosome biogenesis is highly upregulated in cancer and essential for malignant growth, yet efforts to selectively target this process pharmacologically have been unsuccessful. Here we identify nuclear valosin-containing protein-like (NVL), a hexameric AAA+ ATPase required for large ribosomal subunit (60S) assembly, as a druggable target in this pathway. Using forward genetics, we discovered that the cytotoxic dibenzothiazepinone MM17 inhibits NVL. Mutations conferring resistance to MM17 in cancer cells also rendered recombinant NVL refractory to enzymatic inhibition in vitro, providing convergent genetic and biochemical evidence of target engagement. Cryo-electron microscopy structures revealed two MM17-binding sites within the NVL hexamer, with resistance mutations clustering around the ligand pocket. NVL inhibition disrupts 60S biogenesis and activates p53 without inducing DNA damage. A more potent, bioavailable analog, MM927, recapitulates these effects and suppresses tumor growth in vivo without detectable toxicity. These findings establish NVL inhibitors as first-in-class therapeutics targeting ribosome biogenesis in cancer.

title: Phenotype-based risk stratification for deep vein thrombosis in Behçet's disease: a global 10-year longitudinal study.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Vascular involvement, particularly deep vein thrombosis (DVT), is a major cause of morbidity and mortality in Behçet's disease (BD). This study aimed to identify independent risk factors for DVT and establish a robust framework for phenotype-based risk stratification. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX global health research network and identified 19,739 patients with BD. Three independent propensity score-matched cohorts were established to evaluate the impact of intestinal involvement, thrombophlebitis, and antiphospholipid syndrome (APS). A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used to identify independent predictors of DVT over a 10-year follow-up. To ensure the robustness of our findings and minimise peri-diagnostic detection bias, a 90-day landmark analysis was performed as a sensitivity analysis. RESULTS: Multivariable analysis identified APS (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 6.28, 95% confidence interval [CI] 4.56-8.64) and a history of thrombophlebitis (aHR 5.92, 95% CI 4.72-7.41) as the strongest independent predictors of DVT. In the 90-day landmark analysis, these associations remained significant, with persistent risk observed for APS (aHR 5.10) and thrombophlebitis (aHR 2.50), confirming their long-term predictive value. Additional independent predictors included intestinal involvement (defined as non-infective inflammatory colitis; aHR 1.51), obesity (aHR 1.98), glucocorticoid use (aHR 1.78), and male sex (aHR 1.77). CONCLUSIONS: APS and thrombophlebitis, markers of heightened inflammatory and thrombotic activity at diagnosis, also appear to be persistent indicators of elevated DVT risk in BD. These findings support phenotype-based risk stratification and highlight the need for intensive monitoring and individualised preventive strategies to improve long-term outcomes.

title: Association Between Breast Arterial Calcification on Mammography and Carotid Artery Stenosis on CT Angiography: A Retrospective Study in a Selected Cohort of Women Aged 60-65 Years.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p Breast arterial calcification (BAC) is an incidental mammographic finding that may be associated with systemic vascular disease. We investigated the association between mammographic BAC and carotid artery stenosis on cervical computed tomography angiography (CTA) in a clinically selected cohort of postmenopausal women aged 60-65 years.This retrospective, single-center study screened 3421 women aged 60-65 years who underwent both mammography and cervical CTA between November 2021 and May 2025. CTA examinations requested from the emergency department or cardiology clinics, examinations not performed within the same calendar year, and prespecified clinical exclusions were removed, leaving 180 women who underwent outpatient CTA for nonspecific symptoms. The median interval between examinations was 131 days. BAC was graded on a 0-3 scale, and carotid stenosis was assessed according to the North American Symptomatic Carotid Endarterectomy Trial (NASCET) criteria, using the greater degree of stenosis on either side as the patient-level value. BAC was analyzed as an ordinal variable, as a categorical variable, and using binary definitions of presence and severity. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, diabetes mellitus, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, and smoking.Clinically significant stenosis (≥50%) was present in 44 women (24.4%). Its prevalence increased from 5.4% in BAC grade 0 to 75.0% in grade 3 (for trend < 0.001). Each one-grade increase in BAC was associated with clinically significant stenosis (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 4.23; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.50-8.03;< 0.001). The corresponding aORs were 16.70 (95% CI, 4.99-73.27) for any BAC and 18.49 (95% CI, 5.93-70.46) for BAC grade ≥2. Adding BAC to the clinical model increased the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) from 0.90 to 0.96 (DeLong= 0.005); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.95. Inter-reader agreement for BAC grading was substantial (weighted κ = 0.79).In this selected cohort of women aged 60-65 years who underwent clinically indicated CTA, BAC was associated with carotid artery stenosis independently of conventional cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not establish BAC as a screening or prediction tool and require prospective, population-based validation.

title: Development and internal validation of a clinical prediction model for postoperative venous thromboembolism after neurosurgical intervention in patients with traumatic brain injury.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a critical complication after traumatic brain injury (TBI) surgery. Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability. OBJECTIVE: To develop and internally validate an interpretable clinical prediction model for postoperative VTE in TBI surgery patients. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 1,450 TBI patients who underwent surgery (2016-2024). Seven predictors were selected using Recursive Feature Elimination. Six machine learning algorithms were compared, with logistic regression (LR) selected as the final model. Performance was evaluated using AUC-ROC, calibration, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: Among 1,450 patients, 205 (14.1%) developed postoperative VTE. The LR model achieved AUC-ROC of 0.868 (95% CI: 0.815-0.920) with good calibration (Brier score: 0.085). Seven predictors were identified: age, Barthel index, ASA classification, multiple surgeries, general anesthesia, limb AIS score, and serum magnesium. Compared with Caprini score (AUC: 0.686), the model showed improved discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.182; NRI: 0.559). CONCLUSION: An interpretable model based on seven routinely available variables demonstrated promising performance for postoperative VTE risk stratification in TBI surgery patients. A nomogram and web-based calculator are provided for clinical use.

Conventional risk assessment tools were not developed for neurosurgical trauma populations, limiting their applicability.
