title: A clinical-deep learning model for prolonged length of stay following endovascular aortic repair.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Prolonged length of stay (PLOS) after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) for abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is associated with increased complications, resource burden, and patient distress. Early identification of high-risk patients remains challenging. This study aimed to develop and externally validate a predictive model integrating clinical variables and three-dimensional deep learning (3D-DL) features from preoperative computed tomography angiography (CTA) to predict PLOS after EVAR. METHODS: A total of 788 patients with AAA who underwent elective EVAR were enrolled from two hospitals. The internal training cohort consisted of 556 patients, and the external validation cohort included 232 patients. PLOS was defined as a LOS above the 75th percentile of the distribution. A clinical nomogram was developed using LASSO regression followed by multivariate logistic regression. Deep learning (DL) features were extracted from manually segmented computed tomography angiography (CTA) images using a 3D ResNet200 network, and LASSO regression was applied to select the most informative features. An ensemble model integrating the clinical predictors and the selected DL features was constructed. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots, and decision curve analysis. RESULTS: LASSO combined with multivariate logistic regression identified five independent clinical predictors: age, hemoglobin, albumin, maximum aneurysm diameter, and diabetes. The clinical model achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.917 in the internal cohort and 0.944 in the external cohort. From the 3D ResNet200 network, 32 DL features were extracted. LASSO regression further selected two of these features. The ensemble predictive model, which integrated the clinical predictors and DL features, demonstrated improved discrimination, with an AUC of 0.971 in the internal cohort and 0.958 in the external cohort. Internal validation with 1,000 bootstrap resamples yielded optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.911 for the clinical model and 0.966 for the ensemble model. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent model performance across age and diabetes strata, while performance in the female subgroup warrants further evaluation in larger cohorts. CONCLUSION: This study developed an ensemble predictive model to predict PLOS following EVAR. The model demonstrated excellent discrimination and provided significant prognostic value beyond clinical variables alone. This nomogram may serve as a preoperative tool for risk stratification and resource planning in this population. Future studies should focus on prospective validation and clinical integration.

title: Case Report: staged segment-specific open and endovascular treatment of chronic post-dissection aortic disease with descending thoracic and giant infrarenal aneurysmal components.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Contemporary management of chronic post-dissection aortic disease includes open repair, thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with or without adjunctive false-lumen occlusion, fenestrated/branched endovascular repair, and staged open-endovascular strategies. Selection depends on anatomy, rupture risk, malperfusion, physiological reserve, and device availability. CASE PRESENTATION: 2 A 56-year-old woman with body mass index 47.2 kg/mand major cardiometabolic comorbidity presented with progressive abdominal pulsation. CTA demonstrated chronic Stanford type B/DeBakey III dissection with descending thoracic aneurysmal degeneration to 52.7 mm, a dominant symptomatic infrarenal aneurysmal component measuring approximately 11-12 cm, bilateral common iliac involvement, and residual paravisceral dissection without treatment-triggering enlargement or malperfusion. No Crawford extent was assigned because complete longitudinal centerline imaging was unavailable. Stage I comprised transperitoneal open aorto-bi-iliac reconstruction. After 118 days, elective morphology-driven zone 2 TEVAR was performed to cover the reported proximal entry region and reduce antegrade false-lumen inflow. Intentional left subclavian artery (LSA) coverage without prophylactic revascularization was followed by symptomatic subclavian steal requiring unplanned carotid-subclavian bypass. RESULTS: No perioperative death, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, bowel ischemia, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, graft thrombosis, prosthetic infection, or access complication occurred. At latest follow-up, the patient was asymptomatic and all reconstructions were patent. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates competing priorities in segment-specific management of chronic post-dissection aortic disease. The unequivocal indication for urgent infrarenal repair contrasted with discretionary pre-emptive thoracic intervention below the conventional diameter threshold. The LSA-related complication emphasizes prophylactic LSA preservation/revascularization, spinal collateral planning, and lifelong surveillance of the untreated paravisceral segment after previous abdominal aortic reconstruction.

Selection depends on anatomy, rupture risk, malperfusion, physiological reserve, and device availability. title: Case Report: Endovascular repair for true lumen collapse after frozen elephant trunk for type A aortic dissection.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Frozen elephant trunk (FET) was applied in the treatment of type A aortic dissection, enabling one-stage repair of the aortic arch and proximal descending aorta while promoting true lumen expansion. However, inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen is a rare but catastrophic complication that may cause true lumen collapse and life-threatening visceral malperfusion, with limited reports on its endovascular management. CASE PRESENTATION: Here, we present the case of a 44-year-old female who underwent Bentall procedure, total arch replacement, and FET implantation for acute type A aortic dissection at a local hospital. Postoperatively, she developed visceral malperfusion manifesting as abdominal distension, hepatic and renal dysfunction, and elevated lactate levels. Computed tomography angiography revealed that the FET stent had been inadvertently deployed into the false lumen, resulting in true lumen collapse. Emergency thoracic endovascular aortic repair was performed, establishing a "FET-false lumen-true lumen" pathway with an additional stent graft to redirect aortic flow into the true lumen. Computational fluid dynamics analysis showed that the postoperative hemodynamics have been significantly improved. The patient's organ function normalized, and she was discharged two weeks later, remaining asymptomatic at 8-month follow-up. CONCLUSION: Endovascular reintervention with additional stent grafting to establish a flow-redirection pathway is a feasible and effective strategy for true lumen collapse following inadvertent FET deployment into the false lumen. Prompt recognition, timely imaging confirmation, and immediate intervention are paramount to mitigating the risks associated with this serious complication.

CASE PRESENTATION: Here, we present the case of a 44-year-old female who underwent Bentall procedure, total arch replacement, and FET implantation for acute type A aortic dissection at a local hospital.

title: Lipoprotein(a) and Triglycerides as Independent Predictors of Long-Term Aortoiliac Stent Failure After Endovascular Revascularisation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Restenosis and occlusion remain important after aortoiliac stenting, and device choice does not fully explain late patency loss. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is implicated in atherosclerotic progression and residual vascular risk. OBJECTIVE: To determine whether baseline Lp(a) is associated with long-term restenosis or occlusion after aortoiliac stenting. METHODS: This post hoc biomarker analysis of COBEST included 125 patients and 168 treated iliac arteries randomised to the Advanta V12 covered stent (Atrium Medical Corporation, Hudson, NH, USA) or bare-metal stents for symptomatic aortoiliac occlusive disease. The primary outcome was loss of primary patency, defined as restenosis or occlusion during 5-year follow-up. Cox proportional hazards modelling and cumulative failure curves were the main analyses. RESULTS: p p p p In the Lp(a)-adjusted Cox model, covered stent use was associated with a lower hazard of restenosis or occlusion (HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.31-0.97;= 0.039), whereas each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration was associated with a higher hazard (HR, 1.08; 95% CI, 1.06-1.10;< 0.001; equivalent to HR, 2.16; 95% CI, 1.79-2.59 per 10 mg/dL increase). In the biomarker-adjusted model, each 1 mg/dL higher Lp(a) concentration (HR, 1.05; 95% CI, 1.02-1.08;< 0.001; HR, 1.63; 95% CI, 1.22-2.16 per 10 mg/dL increase) and each 1 mmol/L higher triglyceride concentration (HR, 1.89; 95% CI, 1.34-2.68;< 0.001) remained associated with restenosis or occlusion. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) and, to a lesser extent, triglycerides were independently associated with long-term aortoiliac stent failure after adjustment for stent type.

title: Retinal Microvascular Abnormalities, White Matter Injury, and Cognitive Impairment in Carotid Stenosis or Occlusion.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe carotid artery stenosis or occlusion (CASO) is associated with white matter injury and cognitive impairment, but markers of accompanying microvascular dysfunction remain incompletely characterized. We investigated the relationships among retinal microvascular abnormalities on optical coherence tomography angiography, white matter hyperintensities (WMH), and cognitive impairment in severe unilateral CASO. METHODS: In this multicenter cross-sectional study, 860 participants were included: 566 patients with severe unilateral CASO without acute cerebral infarction and 294 control participants with similar age and sex distributions. All participants underwent multimodal imaging, including automated WMH segmentation on brain magnetic resonance imaging and macular optical coherence tomography angiography. Cognitive function was assessed using the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. RESULTS: P Compared with controls, patients with CASO showed lower vessel length density across retinal layers and greater WMH burden. Within the group with CASO, the retina ipsilateral to the stenosis showed lower vessel length density and greater vessel dilation, paralleling the greater burden of deep WMH in the ipsilateral hemisphere (all adjusted<0.05). Retinal microvascular abnormalities and greater WMH burden were both associated with worse concurrent cognitive performance. Adding optical coherence tomography angiography metrics to clinical and WMH-based models provided modest additional discrimination for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment in internal cross-validation, increasing the area under the curve from 0.652 to 0.695 (Δarea under the curve, 0.043 [95% CI, 0.021-0.064]). CONCLUSIONS: In severe unilateral CASO, retinal microvascular abnormalities were associated with ipsilateral white matter injury and lower cognitive performance. Optical coherence tomography angiographymetrics provided modest complementary discriminatory information beyond conventional clinical variables and WMH for identifying concurrent cognitive impairment, although external validation is required. title: Advances in Design and Preparation of Biodegradable Inferior Vena Cava Filters.
abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with pulmonary embolism (PE) constituting its most fatal clinical consequence. Inferior vena cava filters (IVCFs) have been employed as a mechanical prophylactic strategy for patients with contraindications to anticoagulation or recurrent embolic events. However, permanent implantation and limited retrieval success are associated with device-related complications, including caval perforation, migration, fracture, and filter-induced thrombosis. Biodegradable IVCFs have been investigated as an alternative approach to provide temporary protection while avoiding the complications associated with long-term implantation. This review discusses recent advances in biodegradable IVCFs from a material perspective, focusing on material selection, structural design, degradation characteristics, and biological responses. Biodegradable polymers, degradable metallic materials, and shape-memory systems are evaluated regarding their mechanical stability, degradation behavior, vascular compatibility, and functional requirements. Strategies for improving radiopacity while preserving biodegradability are also summarized. Despite ongoing progress, key challenges remain in precisely controlling degradation kinetics, maintaining adequate mechanical support during the therapeutic period, and validating long-term safety through clinical studies. Further efforts in material optimization, biofunctional modification, and individualized fabrication may facilitate the future development of biodegradable IVCFs.

title: Redox Dysregulation in the Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Wall: Ferroptosis and Experimental Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a spatially heterogeneous disease of the aortic wall for which no pharmacological treatment has reliably arrested enlargement. The term oxidative stress encompasses processes that differ in chemical form, anatomical location and cellular effect. This narrative review examines haem and redox-active iron, phospholipid peroxidation and antioxidant defence at the intraluminal thrombus-wall interface and within medial and inflammatory cells. We distinguish ferroptosis from redox effects on coagulation, migration and secretion and relate these functions to wall remodelling. Experimental studies show that manipulating iron uptake and ferritin turnover, membrane phospholipid susceptibility or peroxide detoxification can alter vascular smooth muscle cell survival, macrophage behaviour and aortic injury. The cellular function affected helps determine which process an intervention should preserve or suppress. Based on evidence from human tissue and animal models, we review opportunities to localise, manipulate and monitor these processes and assess their relevance to established AAA. Testing after confirmation of aneurysm formation, with target engagement in defined wall cells and parallel assessment of systemic effects, is needed to determine whether these approaches can limit continued enlargement.

title: Ten tips for the management of vascular access in hemodialysis patients.
abstract: Vascular access management represents one of the central challenges in hemodialysis care, requiring the nephrologist to navigate a complex and dynamic process that begins well before the first dialysis session and continues throughout the patient's entire treatment trajectory. This challenge is further amplified by the growing age and comorbidity burden of the hemodialysis population, and by the recent shift toward high-convection-volume hemodiafiltration, which depends on a reliably functioning access. Drawing on current evidence and clinical experience, this narrative review argues that optimal outcomes depend not on any single intervention, but on a coherent, longitudinal approach integrating timely planning, careful patient selection, surgical precision, and structured follow-up. In this context, the nephrologist plays a pivotal coordinating role, and assuming ownership of this field through continuous training, multidisciplinary engagement, and education of patients and colleagues remains essential to improving outcomes along the entire course of kidney disease.

title: Predicting 365-Day Lower-Limb Amputation at Discharge After Diabetes-Related Foot Ulcer Hospitalization: Development and Temporal Validation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients discharged after diabetes-related foot ulcer hospitalization remain at risk of limb loss. We developed and temporally validated discharge-time models for 365-day amputation, comparing clinical-plus-discharge predictors with a fuller set including contextual information. METHODS: Epic Cosmos provided 431 493 development patients discharged in 2016-2024 and 36 823 temporal-validation patients discharged in January-June 2025. Cause-specific Cox models estimated any and major amputation with death as a competing event. Model C included clinical, contextual, and discharge variables; Model D omitted contextual variables. Models were compared using discrimination, calibration, and decision curves. RESULTS: Observed 365-day cumulative incidences were 19.3% for any amputation and 6.4% for major amputation. Model C areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.710 and 0.737, compared with 0.711 and 0.736 for Model D. Corresponding calibration slopes were 1.003 and 1.026 for Model C and 1.010 and 1.025 for Model D. Brier scores were similar. Gangrene and peripheral artery disease had the largest joint Wald statistics in Model C. Its highest-risk quintile contained 40.6% of any-amputation and 49.6% of major-amputation events. CONCLUSIONS: Models C and D showed similar performance, with moderate discrimination and risk enrichment. These findings do not establish superiority of the fuller model, irrelevance of contextual factors, or improved patient outcomes. Independent validation, local recalibration, and prospective impact evaluation are required before clinical use.

title: Biomarkers of Apoptosis and Systemic Inflammation in Patients with COVID-19 Undergoing Targeted Anticoagulant Therapy.
abstract: BACKGROUND: We assessed apoptosis biomarkers alongside systemic inflammatory indices in patients diagnosed with COVID-19 undergoing targeted anticoagulant therapy. METHODS: A prospective cohort study involved a total of 370 patients hospitalized with COVID-19 from 2021 to 2022. One hundred ninety patients with COVID-19 received low-molecular-weight heparins, LMWH (group 1), one hundred twenty-three patients received unfractionated heparin, UFH (group 2), and fifty-seven patients received direct oral anticoagulants, DOAC (group 3). The diagnostic protocol included assessment of clinical and anamnesis data, evaluation of biomarkers of apoptosis (phosphatidylserine and calreticulin) and systemic inflammation (C-reactive protein, ferritin, procalcitonin) alongside duplex venous ultrasonography of the lower extremities executed to screen for venous thromboembolic complications. RESULTS: p p The LMWH regimen elicited a substantial chronological surge in phosphatidylserine concentrations, demonstrating an 18.4% increment from baseline parameters (= 0.012) in COVID-19 patients. Baseline phosphatidylserine levels above 62.75 pg/mL were a protective factor associated with attenuating the odds of developing an episode of venous thromboembolism by 1.033 (= 0.02). CONCLUSIONS: Phosphatidylserine can be used as a prognostic measure to evaluate the odds of developing a VTE episode. LMWHs exert more potent pleiotropic anti-inflammatory and systemic anticoagulant activities within this infectious framework compared to alternative ACT protocols.

title: Functional Benefit and Safety of Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Thrombolysis After Successful Endovascular Thrombectomy: An Updated and Cumulative Meta-Analysis of Randomized Trials.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Methods: Results: Conclusions: 2 p Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) after successful endovascular thrombectomy has been associated with a higher probability of excellent functional recovery in previous randomized-trial meta-analyses. Since those syntheses, the evidence base has expanded to include IAT-TOP, restricted to basilar artery occlusion, and CHOICE-2, in which 90-day mortality was 12.1% with adjunctive alteplase and 6.4% with thrombectomy alone. We therefore examined how the efficacy and mortality profiles changed as randomized evidence accumulated.This PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic review and meta-analysis was prospectively registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251006577). Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing adjunctive intra-arterial fibrinolytic therapy administered after trial-defined successful or near-successful post-thrombectomy reperfusion with no adjunctive intra-arterial fibrinolysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL were searched through 15 August 2026, with ClinicalTrials.gov searched separately. Nine RCTs comprising 2828 randomized participants were included at the systematic-review level. Event counts were re-extracted from primary trial publications and pooled as risk ratios (RRs) using random-effects models with restricted maximum likelihood estimation and Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals (CIs). Cumulative meta-analysis tracked how the efficacy and mortality estimates changed as evidence accumulated, while fragility analyses assessed the stability of the corresponding statistical inferences. This research received no external funding.Adjunctive IAT increased excellent functional recovery (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] 0-1; 8 RCTs; RR 1.266, 95% CI 1.135-1.412; I= 0.0%), with a 95% prediction interval of 1.047-1.530 and a meta-analytic Fragility Index of 15. Ninety-day all-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (8 RCTs; RR 1.036, 95% CI 0.817-1.314); immediately before CHOICE-2 entered the cumulative synthesis, the corresponding estimate was RR 0.984 (95% CI 0.801-1.209). In the bidirectional reverse-fragility analysis, the earliest significance transition identified by the search occurred after 24 one-patient event-status modifications and was in the direction of increased mortality with adjunctive IAT (RR 1.174, 95% CI 1.002-1.377;= 0.048). No transition toward reduced mortality was identified through the same modification depth. No trial was judged to be at high risk of bias using RoB 2. GRADE certainty was moderate for excellent functional recovery, 90-day mortality, and functional independence and low for hemorrhagic outcomes.The efficacy and mortality components of the benefit-risk profile of adjunctive IAT have not evolved in parallel. The improvement in excellent functional recovery persisted as randomized evidence accumulated and remained comparatively stable to perturbation of the observed event data, whereas mortality remains unresolved. The cumulative and reverse-fragility findings do not establish a treatment-related mortality excess; however, the absence of statistical significance should not be interpreted as affirmative evidence of mortality neutrality. The current randomized evidence therefore supports a reproducible functional benefit while preserving clinically relevant uncertainty regarding survival.

title: Agkistrodon piscivorus Multistage Limb Salvage After Severe Cottonmouth () Envenomation: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Cottonmouth envenomation typically produces prominent local tissue injury, with systemic toxicity occurring less commonly. We report a limb-threatening presentation with delayed deterioration after initial antivenom therapy. METHODS: A man in his 50s sustained a suspected cottonmouth bite to the plantar midfoot and received 10 vials of Crotalidae immune F(ab')2 (equine) antivenom during his initial hospitalization. RESULTS: Five days after the bite, severe edema, progressive pain, paresthesia, pallor, delayed capillary refill, and nonpalpable pedal pulses raised clinical concern for delayed compartment syndrome and threatened tissue viability. Compartment pressures were not obtained. Operative drainage and debridement were independently indicated by plantar necrosis and suspected secondary infection after contaminated floodwater exposure. Surgery confirmed purulent fluid under pressure and nonviable tissue. The patient subsequently received adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen therapy, acellular fish-skin grafts, and definitive split-thickness skin grafting. CONCLUSIONS: This case underscores the importance of serial examinations and laboratory monitoring following pit viper envenomation, toxicology-guided antivenom management, careful distinction between suspected compartment syndrome and established necrosis or infection, and staged reconstruction for severe soft-tissue injury.

title: Aortic versus non-aortic cryopreserved allograft and donor-specific outcome: a retrospective observational study.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cryopreserved arterial allografts are an established conduit for vascular reconstruction in patients with vascular graft infection (VGI). Although outcomes after aortic and peripheral implantation have been reported separately, comparative data including donor- and graft-specific characteristics are limited. This study compared clinical, procedural, and donor-related factors between aortic and non-aortic allograft implantation and evaluated their association with postoperative outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: n n This retrospective single-center study included all consecutive patients undergoing arterial allograft implantation between January 2023 and December 2025. Patients were stratified into aortic position (AP; = 22) and non-aortic position (NAP; = 29). Clinical, procedural, microbiological, donor-, and graft-specific variables were analyzed. Primary endpoints were in-hospital and 30-day mortality. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, primary graft patency, limb salvage and reintervention. RESULTS: p p p p p Fifty-one patients received 112 cryopreserved arterial allografts in multisegment reconstructions. VGI was present in 76.5% of patients. Compared with NAP, AP reconstruction required longer operative time (343 vs. 262 min, = .002) and greater blood loss (1,125 vs. 550 mL, = .001). In-hospital/30-day mortality was higher after AP reconstruction (22.7% vs. 3.5%, = .073), whereas primary graft patency and reintervention rates were comparable. Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly reduced survival after aortic reconstruction (log-rank = .011). Donor age, sex, graft storage duration, and transport characteristics were similar between groups. Non-aortic allografts showed significantly better histological quality ( = .012). DISCUSSION: Aortic allograft reconstruction was associated with greater procedural complexity and reduced overall survival, likely reflecting the severity of underlying disease and extent of surgery. Histological graft quality differed significantly between implantation sites and may represent an underrecognized determinant of allograft outcomes. CONCLUSION: Cryopreserved arterial allografts provide effective vascular reconstruction in both aortic and non-aortic positions, with favorable graft patency. Inferior survival after aortic reconstruction occurred despite largely comparable donor characteristics, aside from a higher histological quality grade in NAP. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants further evaluation. Prospective multicenter studies should determine whether histological graft assessment improves allograft selection and predicts long-term outcomes.

title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) addresses valvular obstruction but leaves concomitant ascending aortic dilatation untreated. Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain. METHODS: n n This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, = 87; TAV, = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR. Annualized aortic expansion rates were evaluated utilizing linear mixed-effects models derived from serial computed tomography angiography over a median 27.0-month follow-up. RESULTS: P P No ascending aortic dissection, rupture, or elective aortic interventions occurred during follow-up. The adjusted annualized expansion rate at the mid-ascending aorta was low and comparable between the BAV and TAV cohorts (0.43 vs. 0.39 mm/year; interaction = 0.364). Progression rates at the distal ascending aorta and sinuses of Valsalva similarly demonstrated no significant morphological differences. No patient exhibited rapid progression (>5 mm/year). Although moderate or greater paravalvular leakage occurred exclusively in BAV patients (4.8% vs. 0.0%; = 0.043), its overall incidence was low (2.2%); however, the extremely small number of cases precluded a definitive statistical assessment of its impact on longitudinal aortic expansion. CONCLUSIONS: In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are maintained.

title: Sitting Baduanjin-based rehabilitation programme following endovascular therapy in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia: protocol for a WeChat mini program-assisted multicentre randomized controlled trial.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Endovascular therapy (EVT) is an important revascularization strategy for limb salvage in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). However, despite restoration of blood flow, patients may continue to experience residual haemodynamic impairment and ischaemia-related burden after EVT, with a persistently high risk of adverse limb outcomes. Therefore, effective post-EVT rehabilitation strategies are needed to further improve limb perfusion and promote functional recovery and symptom improvement in this population. Exercise rehabilitation is widely recommended for patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), but current evidence is largely derived from individuals with intermittent claudication, and its applicability and additional benefits in patients with CLTI after EVT remain uncertain. Sitting Baduanjin (SBDJ) is a low-intensity mind-body exercise modality that reduces lower-limb loading and postural demands while providing exercise stimulation, with potential cardiovascular regulatory effects, and may therefore be suitable for patients with limited exercise tolerance after EVT. However, evidence regarding the effects of SBDJ on target-limb haemodynamic status and patient-centred outcomes in patients with CLTI following EVT remains limited. METHODS: This prospective, multicentre, parallel-group randomised controlled trial incorporates blinded outcome assessment. A total of 146 eligible patients with CLTI following EVT will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to the intervention group or the control group. The intervention group will receive SBDJ combined with ankle pump exercise, whereas the control group will receive ankle pump exercise. A WeChat mini program will support exercise delivery, adherence monitoring, follow-up management, and questionnaire data collection during the home-based phase. The primary outcome is the longitudinal change in target-limb ABI over the 12-week rehabilitation period. Secondary outcomes include walking ability, quality of life, anxiety symptoms, lower-limb rest pain, and safety. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 4, and week 12. DISCUSSION: Clinical Trial Registration: This trial aims to determine whether an SBDJ-based rehabilitation programme provides additional benefits over ankle pump exercise alone on index-limb haemodynamic status among patients with CLTI following EVT, while exploring its potential effects on functional outcomes and patient-reported outcomes during the early post-EVT rehabilitation period.http://itmctr.ccebtcm.org.cn/, identifier: ITMCTR ITMCTR2022000113.

title: Periprocedural body temperature and clinical outcomes after successful reperfusion in large vessel occlusion stroke.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Functional recovery remains heterogeneous among patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke, even after successful reperfusion. Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 219 patients with large-vessel occlusion acute ischemic stroke (LVO-AIS) who underwent EVT and achieved successful reperfusion, defined as a modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score of 2b-3. Pre and post-EVT body temperatures were recorded. The primary outcome was favorable functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0-2 at 90 days. Logistic regression analyses and exploratory subgroup analyses were performed to evaluate the association between body temperature and clinical outcomes. RESULTS: P P P P P P Among the 219 included patients, 104 (47.5%) achieved favorable functional outcome at 90 days. Pre-EVT temperature was not significantly associated with functional outcome. In unadjusted analysis, each 1 °C increase in post-EVT temperature was associated with lower odds of favorable functional outcome (OR, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.20-0.79;= 0.01) and higher odds of mortality (OR, 2.02; 95% CI, 1.11-3.66;= 0.02). However, these associations were attenuated after multivariable adjustment (adjusted OR, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.19-1.15;= 0.10; adjusted OR, 1.22; 95% CI, 0.49-3.02;= 0.67). In exploratory subgroup analyses, a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and lower odds of favorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15 (adjusted OR, 0.29; 95% CI, 0.08-0.98;= 0.047), although the interaction was not statistically significant (for interaction = 0.64). CONCLUSION: In this exploratory study, body temperature was not independently associated with functional outcome in the overall cohort. Although a potential association between higher post-EVT temperature and unfavorable outcome was observed in patients with baseline NIHSS ≤ 15, the interaction was not significant. This finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective validation with pre-specified subgroup analyses.

Body temperature may constitute a potentially modifiable physiological factor associated with functional outcome. In particular, whether clinical factors, including baseline stroke severity, modify this temperature-outcome association remains uncertain.

title: A comparison of aspiration thrombectomy with catheter-directed thrombolysis in the management of Paget-Schroetter syndrome.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Acute subclavian vein thrombosis secondary to thoracic outlet syndrome (Paget-Schroetter syndrome [PSS]) requires the prompt clearing of thrombus from the subclavian vein through catheter-directed thrombolysis (CDT) or aspiration thrombectomy (ASP). Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP. Venograms were assessed for patency, stenosis, and subclavian post-thrombotic changes (PTC). PTC were graded based on the degree of luminal encroachment and vessel irregularity: mild (<10%), moderate (10%-50%), and severe (50%-99%). Interventions were assessed: (1) within 1 week of the procedure, (2) before subclavian vein decompression, (3) 2 weeks after subclavian vein decompression, and (4) patency on the last venogram. Standardized outcomes were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 110 patients with PSS were treated over 5 years. Of these patients, 54 met the inclusion criteria: 28 underwent CDT and 26 underwent ASP. At 1 week following the procedure, rethrombosis occurred in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 6 (23.1%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .5). Failure to clear thrombosis occurred in 13.8% of patients who underwent ASP. The composite rate of early thrombosis and procedural failure was higher in the ASP cohort. Before PSS surgery, occlusion was noted in 1 (3.6%) patient who underwent CDT and 8 (30.8%) patients who underwent ASP (P < .05). PTC was mild in 13 (46.4%) patients receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP (P < .05); moderate in 5 (17.9%) receiving CDT and 5 (19.2%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (32.1%) receiving CDT and 8 (30.8) receiving ASP. At early follow-up after PSS surgery, PTC was mild in 10 (43.5%) patients receiving CDT and 4 (23.5) receiving ASP; moderate in 2 (8.7%) receiving CDT and 1 (5.9%) receiving ASP; and severe in 9 (39.1%) receiving CDT and 6 (35.3%) receiving ASP. Occlusion was noted in 2 (8.7%) patients receiving CDT and 6 (35%) receiving ASP. Recanalization resulted in final patency in 22 (95%) patients receiving CDT and 15 (88%) receiving ASP. CONCLUSIONS: Both ASP and CDT may be employed for clearing thrombus in PSS; however, they differ in early efficacy, PTC, and patency. Our results suggest that while often more rapid and convenient, ASP may be inferior to CAT in the management of PSS.

Our goal is to systematically compare the outcomes of CDT and ASP in the management of PSS. METHODS: Consecutive patients with PSS at a single institution from 2020 through 2025 were reviewed for management with CDT or ASP.

title: Microbial contributions to aromatic amino acid acquisition in insects.
abstract: Aromatic amino acids (AAA) are essential for insect development and survival, serving as precursors for cuticle formation, immune defenses, and neurotransmitter synthesis. Because insect genomes lack the shikimate pathway, they must obtain AAA from external sources, raising the question of how microorganisms contribute to host AAA availability. Here, we review evidence spanning the continuum of insect-microbe associations, from obligate intracellular symbioses to diverse gut microbial communities. Comparative genomics reveals the repeated retention of shikimate and AAA biosynthetic pathways in intracellular symbionts despite extensive genome reduction, while experimental studies demonstrate that symbiont-derived AAA directly support cuticle maturation, desiccation resistance, and overall host performance. Similar nutritional roles are increasingly suspected in specialized extracellular gut symbioses, suggesting functional convergence between distinct organizational frameworks. Beyond these highly integrated associations, growing evidence indicates that gut microbiota may also influence host AAA homeostasis. Although direct microbial AAA provisioning remains difficult to demonstrate, microbiota disruption consistently affects AAA-dependent traits, including cuticle melanization and neurotransmitter-mediated behaviors. These effects are reinforced by experimental inhibition of microbial AAA biosynthesis. Together, these observations support the view that AAA are a central metabolic currency between insects and their microbial partners, with important consequences for insect physiology, fitness, and adaptation.

Here, we review evidence spanning the continuum of insect-microbe associations, from obligate intracellular symbioses to diverse gut microbial communities.

title: A Novel Hybrid Endovascular Technique for Tympanojugular Paraganglioma: Flow Diversion Followed by Direct Transauricular Squid Embolization.
abstract: Skull-base paragangliomas with persistent internal carotid artery (ICA) supply can be challenging to devascularize safely. We report a 17-yearold male with an Succinate Dehydrogenase Complex Iron Sulfur Subunit B (SDHB)-associated tympanojugular paraganglioma treated using a staged hybrid endovascular strategy after subtotal resection. Persistent supply from a short ICA feeder and circumferential involvement of the petrous ICA precluded safe conventional transarterial embolization. A Surpass Elite flow-diverting stent was deployed across the feeder after dual antiplatelet therapy to preserve parent-vessel patency, reduce tumour inflow, and reinforce the arterial wall. Four months later, protected direct transauricular and transcervical puncture embolization with Squid 12 was performed under intermittent ICA balloon occlusion. Marked tumor devascularization was achieved without embolic or thromboembolic complication, and definitive resection was completed without new neurological or cranial nerve deficit. This staged approach may provide a useful adjunct for selected skull-base paragangliomas with persistent ICA supply when conventional embolization carries unacceptable risk.

title: Association of Estimated Arterial Stiffness with Collateral Status and Functional Outcome after Endovascular Thrombectomy: A Secondary Analysis of the OPTIMAL-BP Trial.
abstract: PURPOSE: Estimated pulse wave velocity (ePWV) is a surrogate of arterial stiffness that may influence stroke outcomes and potentially affect collateral circulation. We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed. Collateral status was assessed using the Tan scale (poor, 0-1; good, 2-3). Poor functional outcome was defined as 3-month modified Rankin Scale score of 3-6. Multivariable logistic and mediation analyses were performed to evaluate the association between ePWV and functional outcomes and to explore direct and indirect pathways. RESULTS: A total of 285 patients were included (mean age, 73.3±11.3 years; 40.4% women). Each 1 m/s increase in ePWV was associated with poor collaterals (adjusted odds ratio [OR] 1.276, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.083-1.503) and poor functional outcome (adjusted OR 1.338, 95% CI 1.121-1.597). In mediation analyses, collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the association between ePWV and poor functional outcome (indirect effect: adjusted β 0.022, 95% CI 0.001-0.053), whereas the direct effect remained significant (adjusted β 0.237, 95% CI 0.115-0.359). Neither the direct effect of ePWV on functional outcome nor the indirect effect through collateral status differed according to BP management strategy. CONCLUSION: Higher ePWV was associated with poor collateral status and unfavorable functional outcome after successful reperfusion. Collateral status accounted for only a small proportion of the observed association between ePWV and functional outcome.

We examined the association of ePWV with collateral status and 3-month functional outcome after successful endovascular thrombectomy and explored the contribution of collateral status to this relationship across blood pressure (BP) management strategies. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this secondary analysis of the Outcome in Patients Treated With Intra-Arterial Thrombectomy-Optimal Blood Pressure Control trial, 285 patients were analyzed.

title: The Central Coupler of ClpXP Controls Intersubunit Communication and Couples Intrasubunit Chemical Energy with Force Generation.
abstract: ClpX is a clockwise hexameric helical arrangement that hydrolyzes ATP to unfold proteins and translocate them into the proteolytic chamber. We investigate the central coupler, a three α-helix module conserved among AAA+ ATPases, which is proposed to enable intersubunit communication and mechanochemical coupling. Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX. By combining single-molecule optical tweezers, biochemical assays and single particle cryo-EM we demonstrate that the central coupler, of the second-highest subunit of the ClpX clockwise helical arrangement, positions its Arginine-finger, sensor-I and sensor-II to contact the ATP of the anticlockwise neighbor subunit to trigger its hydrolysis. Then, the central coupler of the highest subunit rapidly couples the ATP hydrolysis with the downward motion of its substrate-translocating loop, enabling fast force generation to swiftly unfold protein substrates while maximizing the thermodynamic efficiency of the motor.

Although fundamental in AAA+ ATPases, the molecular mechanism underlying these processes remains elusive in ClpX.

title: Precision medicine for futile recanalization after mechanical thrombectomy in acute ischemic stroke: mechanisms, diagnostics, and tailored therapies.
abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has substantially improved outcomes in appropriately selected patients with acute ischemic stroke, yet futile recanalization remains a major clinical challenge. Futile recanalization describes poor functional recovery despite technically successful macrovascular reperfusion, underscoring the incomplete relationship between angiographic reperfusion and tissue-level or microvascular perfusion. This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management. Precision imaging has established a role in tissue-based patient selection, and recent randomized trials have expanded thrombectomy evidence to selected patients with large-core infarction. In contrast, current randomized evidence does not support routine endovascular treatment for unselected medium-vessel occlusion populations. We further examine bridging therapy versus direct mechanical thrombectomy, individualized periprocedural management, biomarkers, and decision support based on artificial intelligence. Clinical and imaging phenotypes may provide prognostic or mechanistic information, but no phenotype-based strategy has been prospectively validated to select bridging therapy or direct thrombectomy. Biomarkers currently remain primarily prognostic or exploratory. Artificial intelligence applications are largely focused on diagnostic and prognostic support. treatment-benefit prediction, by contrast, requires evidence of treatment-effect modification and prospective validation. Experimental studies of microvascular no-reflow and thrombo-inflammation provide biological rationale for targeted interventions but do not establish clinical efficacy. Future research should integrate multimodal imaging, biological profiling, and validated decision-support tools to move beyond angiographic success toward individualized strategies focused on tissue integrity and meaningful functional recovery.

This narrative review summarizes current clinical, mechanistic, and translational evidence on the determinants of futile recanalization and evaluates emerging precision-medicine approaches to its prevention and management.

title: Dickkopf-3 (DKK3) in cardiovascular diseases: from a stress-responsive biomarker to a potential therapeutic target.
abstract: Dickkopf-3 (DKK3) is a secreted glycoprotein that functions as a context-dependent modulator of the Wnt/β-catenin and transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling pathways. Originally studied in development and cancer, DKK3 has recently emerged as a key stress-responsive factor. It is released by epithelial and other cell types under pathological strain and actively participates in fibrotic, inflammatory, and remodeling processes across various organ systems. In cardiovascular medicine, DKK3 is gaining recognition not only as a promising biomarker for renal and vascular injury-conditions closely intertwined with cardiovascular outcomes-but also as a direct mediator in the pathogenesis of specific cardiovascular conditions such as abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) and heart failure. This review synthesizes current knowledge on DKK3, beginning with its fundamental biology and established roles in renal, pulmonary, and dermal fibrosis, which provide crucial mechanistic parallels. We then focus on the evolving evidence of DKK3's involvement in cardiovascular diseases, critically evaluating its biomarker potential for risk stratification in conditions like diabetic kidney disease and its direct pathophysiological roles in vascular smooth muscle cell phenotype switching, myocardial remodeling, and aneurysm formation. We delve into specific molecular mechanisms, including interactions with the ATF6-TGFβ3-Smad2/3 axis and low-density lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1 (LRP1), as revealed by preclinical models. Finally, we explore the therapeutic implications of targeting the DKK3 axis, discuss the challenges posed by its context-dependent dual roles, and outline future research directions necessary to translate these discoveries into clinical applications for cardiovascular patients.

title: Vascular aging biomarkers: the role of ADMA, SDMA, and inflammation.
abstract: Cardiovascular risk assessment based on traditional risk factors may not fully capture subclinical vascular injury and vascular aging, supporting interest in biomarkers reflecting underlying vascular mechanisms. Endothelial dysfunction, altered methylarginine metabolism, and chronic low-grade inflammation represent interconnected processes that may contribute to vascular aging. This narrative review summarizes evidence on the associations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, symmetric dimethylarginine, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with subclinical atherosclerosis and vascular aging. PubMed and Google Scholar were searched between January and August 2026, with priority given to studies evaluating associations of these biomarkers with subclinical vascular changes, vascular aging, and cardiovascular outcomes. ADMA shows the most consistent associations with subclinical atherosclerosis, although these vary across arterial territories and vascular measures. Evidence for SDMA in early vascular disease is more limited, and interpretation is complicated by its dependence on renal function, although some associations persist after adjustment for renal function. IL-6 has biological and genetic evidence supporting a role in atherogenesis, but its associations with subclinical atherosclerosis are not consistently independent of traditional cardiovascular risk factors. hsCRP is an established cardiovascular risk marker and has also been associated with progression of carotid stenosis and arterial stiffness. Differences in vascular endpoints, study populations, confounder adjustment, and analytical methods contribute to heterogeneity across studies. Overall, these biomarkers appear to reflect partly distinct but interconnected components of vascular aging. Their potential relevance may lie in their complementarity; however, current evidence does not establish that combined assessment improves evaluation beyond conventional approaches. Prospective studies should determine whether their combined assessment improves identification of accelerated vascular aging beyond conventional risk assessment.
englishSummary: Cardiovascular risk assessment based on traditional risk factors may not fully capture subclinical vascular injury and vascular aging, supporting interest in biomarkers reflecting underlying vascular mechanisms. Endothelial dysfunction, altered methylarginine metabolism, and chronic low-grade inflammation represent interconnected processes that may contribute to vascular aging. This narrative review summarizes evidence on the associations of asymmetric dimethylarginine, symmetric dimethylarginine, interleukin-6, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein with subclinical atherosclerosis and vascular aging.

title: Case Report: Fatal recurrent rupture of multiple pancreatic pseudoaneurysms following acute alcoholic pancreatitis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Pancreatic pseudoaneurysm (PPA) is a severe and life-threatening vascular complication of pancreatitis. This case highlights the critical need for comprehensive vascular assessment and surveillance in patients with alcoholic pancreatitis to prevent fatal adverse outcomes. CASE PRESENTATION: A 53-year-old man with a 30-year history of heavy alcohol intake (500 mL of 52% ABV Baijiu daily, corresponding to an estimated 205 g pure ethanol per day) presented to our emergency department with hematemesis and hemorrhagic shock on 2 April 2026. He was diagnosed with acute pancreatitis complicated by a pancreatic pseudocyst at another hospital in November 2025 but did not receive standardized follow-up and treatment. Contrast-enhanced CT confirmed rupture of a pancreatic head pseudoaneurysm with hemorrhage extending into the duodenum. Emergency transarterial embolization of the gastroduodenal artery was performed, and hematemesis resolved temporarily. Subsequently, the patient developed progressive abdominal pain, distension, and peritoneal irritation signs. Repeat CT confirmed recurrent intra-abdominal hemorrhage. A second digital subtraction angiography (DSA) identified an unrecognized feeding branch arising from the superior mesenteric artery (SMA) supplying the pancreatic head pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully embolized. The patient's condition stabilized temporarily, with a gradual increase in hemoglobin levels. On 14 April 2026, the patient suffered sudden severe abdominal pain and abdominal distension. Follow-up contrast-enhanced CT revealed enlargement and rupture of a pre-existing tiny pseudoaneurysm in the splenic hilum, resulting in massive intra-abdominal hemorrhage. The patient developed refractory hemorrhagic shock followed by cardiac arrest during preparation for emergency endovascular intervention and ultimately died. Post-embolization hemodynamic changes may have contributed to progressive enlargement and subsequent rupture of the pre-existing lesion, although this causal mechanism cannot be definitively proven in this single case. CONCLUSION: This case illustrates that pancreatitis-associated pseudoaneurysms may be multifocal. Successful control of a dominant bleeding lesion does not eliminate the risk of rupture of the separate pre-existing small pseudoaneurysm, and incomplete initial angiography limited only to the celiac trunk may miss SMA feeding branches, even after technically successful initial endovascular intervention for pancreatitis-associated pseudoaneurysm.

title: Case Report: Pediatric deep vein thrombosis: when pain in the leg becomes a telltale sign.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Deep vein thrombosis is rare in the pediatric population. It carries severe complications such as pulmonary embolism with high mortality. Since it shares presentation with other causes of acute limb pain, diagnosis might be delayed. Early detection of leg pain with immobility, fever, and swelling should raise an alarm for investigating deep vein thrombosis and prompt immediate management. We report a case of a child with chronic thrombocytosis and anemia diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis after sustaining an injury. CASE PRESENTATION: Here we report a case of a two-year-old boy presenting with right leg pain for two days with fever after sustaining a fall while playing. x-ray of the leg ruled out fracture, with further investigation showing a raised D-dimer, and a Doppler ultrasound confirming deep vein thrombosis of the right common femoral vein. Standard-of-care anticoagulants were initiated and later discharged on daily oral anticoagulants for six weeks, with scheduled biweekly follow-up clinics and hematologist review. CONCLUSION: Deep vein thrombosis, though rare in the pediatric population, requires a high index of suspicion in those presenting with limb pain and risk factors such as trauma. Delay in recognition can lead to catastrophic complications such as pulmonary embolism and death.

title: Drug-coated balloon, drug-eluting stent, versus bare-metal stent for vertebral artery ostial stenosis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Stenosis at the origin of the vertebral artery (VAOS) accounts for approximately one in five posterior circulation ischemic events. Bare-metal stents (BMS) have been the conventional endovascular treatment, but restenosis occurs in 11-67% of cases. Drug-coated balloons (DCB) and drug-eluting stents (DES) are alternative strategies; however, no network meta-analysis has compared all three modalities specifically at the vertebral origin. METHODS: Five databases-PubMed, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, CNKI, and Wanfang-were searched from 2010 through May 2026 for studies comparing at least two of DCB, DES, or BMS in adults with symptomatic VAOS. The search identified 499 records; 393 underwent title and abstract screening after deduplication, from which 60 full-text articles were assessed. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted using the netmeta package (R 4.5.2), with Bayesian sensitivity analysis. The primary endpoint was imaging-confirmed restenosis (≥50%). The protocol was registered with PROSPERO (CRD420261413981). RESULTS: N I I 2 2 Seven studies (three randomized trials and four observational cohorts, = 970; range 46-217) met the inclusion criteria. Compared with BMS, both DES (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.17-0.45) and DCB (OR 0.39, 95% CI 0.18-0.83) reduced restenosis. DES and DCB did not differ significantly from each other (OR 1.42, 95% CI 0.58-3.50). Between-study heterogeneity was modest (= 20.5%). Although the point estimate suggests modest heterogeneity, the wide confidence interval and the small number of studies limit precision. Lowin a small network should not be equated with clinical homogeneity. P-scores ranked DES first (88.9%), DCB second (60.7%), and BMS last (0.4%). For perioperative safety, DCB ranked highest (P-score 90.0%). CONCLUSION: Both DES and DCB reduce restenosis compared with BMS in VAOS. Both DES and DCB are associated with lower restenosis rates than BMS. The relative anti-restenosis efficacy of DES versus DCB remains uncertain due to the absence of direct head-to-head comparisons. Treatment selection should be individualized based on lesion characteristics and procedural considerations. The DCB evidence base remains small, and head-to-head comparisons of DES versus DCB at the vertebral origin are needed. title: Effect of delayed remote ischemic preconditioning on major cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events in major vascular surgery: the protocol of DRIPC randomized controlled trial.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Although endovascular therapy has become the mainstream approach for major vascular surgery, patients undergoing such procedures are still classified as high-risk according to clinical guidelines. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) is a promising perioperative intervention strategy that has demonstrated acceptable safety and efficacy. Existing research indicates that delayed remote ischemic preconditioning (DRIPC) offers superior protective effects compared to preconditioning performed within 24 h before surgery. However, there is currently a lack of Level I evidence regarding the efficacy and safety of DRIPC in the perioperative period for vascular surgery patients. This study aims to provide high-level evidence on the effectiveness and safety of this intervention in a clinical setting. METHODS AND ANALYSIS: The trial is a single-center, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled clinical trial. A total of 1,054 patients will be recruited. The primary endpoints of the study include major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) within 30 days postoperatively. ETHICS AND DISSEMINATION: This study has been approved by the Ethics Committee of West China Hospital of Sichuan University (approval number:2025-1846). The results will be submitted to a major clinical journal for peer review and publication. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: identifier ChiCTR2600116987.

title: Embolization of jugular bulb diverticula in the management of pulsatile tinnitus.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Pulsatile tinnitus (PT) caused by a high riding jugular bulb or prominent diverticulum can negatively impact quality of life. This study evaluates the effectiveness of endovascular treatments, including stenting, coiling, and Woven EndoBridge (WEB; Terumo Neuro, Aliso Viejo, CA) devices, for managing jugular bulb diverticula (JBD)-induced PT. METHODS: A retrospective review was conducted from September 1, 2020 to April 30, 2026, identifying twelve patients diagnosed with JBD. Data extracted included demographics, PT characteristics, treatment details, and outcomes. Endovascular interventions were pursued after in depth work-up, often including balloon test occlusion. The outcomes and techniques of various interventions are described. RESULTS: 2 Twelve patients (eight females and four males) underwent endovascular treatment for JBD, with a median age of 40.5 years and a median BMI of 25.8 kg/m. Balloon-test occlusion (BTO) showed at least moderate improvement in 7/8 patients (87.5%). Stent-assisted coiling for the JBD was performed in eleven cases (91.7%), and placement of a WEB was successful in one patient. There were two unsuccessful attempts in placing a WEB device, and treatment was converted to stent-assisted coiling. At an average last follow-up of 7.25 months, nine patients (75%) had complete resolution and three (25%) had significant improvement (25%) of their symptoms. CONCLUSION: Endovascular interventions are safe and effective for treating JBD-related PT. BTO is an important intraprocedural tool that may help predict treatment success. Further investigation into optimal patient selection and the role of specific devices in treating JBD is warranted.

title: Dual-guidewire technique with cerebral embolic protection for brachiocephalic trunk bifurcation stenosis: a case report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe stenosis at the terminal bifurcation of the brachiocephalic trunk involving the origins of the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery is a rare and highly challenging lesion of the supra-aortic vessels. Endovascular intervention carries a high risk of embolization and difficulty in delivering large-diameter stents. CASE SUMMARY: We report a 60-year-old male patient who presented with intermittent dizziness and asymmetric blood pressure in the upper limbs. Color Doppler ultrasound and head and neck CT angiography revealed severe stenosis at the terminal bifurcation of the brachiocephalic trunk (stenosis rate approximately 90%), with the lesion involving the origins of the right common carotid artery and the right subclavian artery, accompanied by right subclavian artery steal phenomenon. The patient underwent brachiocephalic trunk balloon angioplasty and stenting via a single femoral artery access. An embolic protection device was deployed in the C1 segment of the right internal carotid artery for distal cerebral protection. During delivery of the stent, the filter guidewire provided insufficient support; a second guidewire was added as a buddy wire to establish a dual-guidewire rail technique, facilitating successful stent placement. Debris was observed in the retrieved filter. Postoperatively, the severe stenosis was relieved and the steal phenomenon resolved. At 1.5 years of follow-up, the patient reported no recurrence of dizziness, and the inter-arm blood pressure difference remained within the normal range. CONCLUSION: In this selected case with clear antegrade flow direction, a single-access, single-filter strategy appeared feasible and may offer a simplified alternative for similar anatomical presentations. However, further validation in larger case series is warranted. The application of dual-guidewire rail technique to overcome difficulties in large-diameter stent delivery during brachiocephalic trunk intervention has been rarely reported.

title: Phenotypes of diabetic kidney disease and cardiovascular outcomes.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To quantify the association between diabetic kidney disease (DKD) phenotypes and cardiovascular disease (CVD) mortality and incident major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), atrial fibrillation (AF), and peripheral artery disease (PAD). METHODS: [2] In this longitudinal analysis of adults with diabetes from NHANES (N = 5035) and the UK Biobank (UKBB, N = 26,968), participants were categorized by estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR, ml/min per 1.73m) and urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (UACR, mg/g) into four phenotypes: no DKD (eGFR≥60, UACR<30), albuminuria-only (eGFR≥60, UACR≥30), low eGFR only (eGFR<60, UACR<30), and albuminuria+low eGFR (eGFR<60, UACR≥30). We estimated absolute and relative risk of CVD mortality (both cohorts) and incident non-fatal CVD (UKBB), adjusting for demographics, anthropometric and laboratory values, and medications. RESULTS: In both cohorts, the albuminuria+low eGFR phenotype was associated with the highest cardiovascular risk versus no DKD (reference). In NHANES, albuminuria-only was more strongly associated with CVD mortality than low eGFR only: albuminuria-only HR 2.56 (95%CI 1.86-3.53), low eGFR only HR 1.92 (1.35-2.73), albuminuria+low eGFR HR 3.16 (2.27-4.41). In UKBB, the low eGFR only phenotype was associated with higher risk of CVD mortality than the albuminuria-only phenotype: albuminuria-only HR 1.88 (1.66-2.13), low eGFR only HR 2.42 (1.99-2.95), albuminuria+low eGFR HR 4.65 (3.78-5.71). In UKBB, the albuminuria+low eGFR phenotype exhibited the strongest association with MACE, AF, and PAD. Similar patterns were observed with absolute risk calculations. CONCLUSIONS: Across two large cohorts, DKD phenotypes conferred distinct cardiovascular risk profiles. Consistent measurement of both eGFR and UACR in clinical practice may facilitate targeted, preventative cardiovascular care in diabetes.

title: Association Between Leg Venous Reflux and Fluid Accumulation Assessed by Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis: A Generalized Estimating Equation Analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Leg edema is common in chronic venous disease, but its relationship with venous reflux remains unclear. This study investigated the association between the venous filling index (VFI) and the extracellular water-to-total body water ratio (ECW/TBW). METHODS: We analyzed 140 patients with saphenous varicose veins (280 limbs). ECW/TBW was measured using bioelectrical impedance analysis and VFI using air plethysmography. Generalized estimating equations (GEEs) were used to account for within-patient correlation. The primary outcome was ECW/TBW (%) analyzed using GEE linear regression, and the secondary outcome was edema (ECW/TBW ≥0.390) analyzed using GEE logistic regression. RESULTS: The mean age was 64.0 years, and 58.6% of patients were female. The mean ECW/TBW was 0.392 and mean VFI was 2.94 mL/s. In multivariable GEE linear regression, VFI was independently associated with higher ECW/TBW (%) (β = 0.045 percentage points per 1 mL/s increase; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.018-0.072; P = 0.001). In multivariable GEE logistic regression, VFI was independently associated with edema (odds ratio, 1.47; 95% CI, 1.22-1.76; P < 0.001). CONCLUSION: Greater venous reflux was independently associated with fluid accumulation and edema. ECW/TBW may provide an objective measure of venous-related fluid accumulation.

title: Intravenous thrombolysis in acute ischemic stroke after reversal of warfarin anticoagulation in patients with mechanical heart valve prostheses and an INR > 1.7.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Acute ischemic stroke (IS) frequently occurs in patients receiving oral anticoagulant (OAC) therapy. Although warfarin has largely been replaced by direct oral anticoagulants in routine clinical practice, it remains the only approved anticoagulant for certain indications, particularly in patients with mechanical heart valve protstheses. In these patients, the international normalized ratio (INR) is the key determinant of eligibility for intravenous thrombolysis (IVT). We present a potentially effective therapeutic strategy involving rapid reversal of warfarin anticoagulation with four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) followed by IVT. METHODS: We report two patients with similar clinical presentations who were receiving long-term warfarin therapy because of a mechanical aortic valve replacement. 76-year-old man with AIS had complete paralysis of the right lower limb, paresis of the right upper limb, and right central facial palsy. INR was 3.2. The second patient was a 76-year-old woman with dysarthria, left central facial palsy and left-sided hemiparesis. Her admission INR was 1.91. In both patients, CT angiography did not demonstrate arterial occlusion suitable for endovascular therapy. RESULTS: In both patients, four-factor prothrombin complex concentrate (4F-PCC) was administered to achieve rapid normalization of the INR. This was immediately followed by standard IVT. Both patients experienced marked neurological improvement, with no hemorrhagic or thromboembolic complications. At the 3-month follow-up, both had achieved complete functional recovery without residual neurological deficits. In conclusion, it can be stated that the chosen procedure led to an excellent clinical outcome in accordance with previously published cases, in the absence of other standard options for recanalization therapy.

title: Vascular Access Complexity and Thrombectomy Efficiency in Proximal MCA M1 Occlusion: Evaluation of the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy Score.
abstract: Background and Objectives: Materials and Methods: n n Results: p p p p p Conclusions: In this study, it was aimed to investigate the relationship between the Bovine Aortic Arch-Dolichoarteriopathy (B.A.D.) score and the procedural characteristics of mechanical thrombectomy, recanalization success, and 90-day functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with proximal M1 occlusion of the middle cerebral artery (MCA).A total of 220 adult patients who underwent mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion were included in this retrospective, single-center cohort study. The patients were divided into good B.A.D. (<2;= 143) and poor B.A.D. (≥2;= 77) groups. Admission National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS) and Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) scores, collateral status, thrombectomy time intervals, number of passes, first-pass effect (FPE), and Modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction (mTICI) recanalization grades were evaluated. The primary outcome was functional independence at day 90 (mRS 0-2). Associations with procedural and clinical outcomes were evaluated using multivariable logistic and linear regression analyses.The puncture-to-recanalization time was significantly longer in the poor B.A.D. group [67 (50.5-88.0) min vs. 43 (32.0-65.0) min,< 0.001], and the FPE rate was lower (37.7% vs. 51.7%,= 0.046). After adjustment for thrombectomy technique and clinical covariates, poor B.A.D. remained independently associated with lower odds of FPE success (aOR = 0.439, 95% CI: 0.229-0.839;= 0.013). In the procedurally adjusted linear regression model, poor B.A.D. also remained independently associated with longer puncture-to-recanalization time after additional adjustment for the number of thrombectomy passes and thrombectomy technique (B = 0.294, 95% CI: 0.188-0.400;< 0.001). Final mTICI ≥ 2b, ≥2c, and 3 recanalization rates did not differ between the groups. Although 90-day functional independence was lower in the poor B.A.D. group, the difference was not significant (51.9% vs. 63.6%,= 0.092), and no statistically significant independent association between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence was observed in the multivariable analysis.Poor B.A.D. anatomy was associated with greater procedural complexity during mechanical thrombectomy for proximal MCA M1 occlusion, including longer puncture-to-recanalization time and lower odds of FPE success, even after adjustment for available procedural and clinical factors. However, no statistically significant independent association was demonstrated between B.A.D. status and 90-day functional independence, and final recanalization rates did not differ significantly between the groups. These findings suggest that the B.A.D. score may have potential value as a preprocedural marker of vascular access complexity; however, prospective external validation is required before its use for procedural planning can be recommended.

title: When Flow Voids Are Missed: Delayed Diagnosis of Foix-Alajouanine Syndrome-A Case Report.
abstract: Introduction: Case Presentation: Outcome: Conclusions: Foix-Alajouanine syndrome (FAS) is a rare, progressive congestive ischaemic myelopathy caused by a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF). Because of its non-specific clinical presentation and subtle imaging features, FAS is frequently misdiagnosed; in particular, perimedullary flow voids-its characteristic imaging hallmark-are readily overlooked on initial MRI, leading to diagnostic delay and potentially harmful interventions.We report the case of a 66-year-old man who developed progressive myelopathy following revision knee arthroplasty performed under spinal anaesthesia. Initial MRI at another institution demonstrated extensive intramedullary T2 hyperintensity, interpreted as spinal cord infarction, while perimedullary flow voids were present but overlooked. Lumbar puncture and high-dose corticosteroid therapy were followed by marked neurological deterioration. At our centre, re-evaluation of a 3T MRI revealed serpentine perimedullary flow voids, and digital subtraction angiography confirmed an SDAVF at the Th5-Th6 level.Transarterial endovascular embolisation with Onyx resulted in neurological stabilisation and partial recovery, with reduced pain and improved bladder control at follow-up.This case highlights the importance of recognising perimedullary flow voids, which may otherwise lead to delayed diagnosis of SDAVF. In patients with unexplained longitudinally extensive myelopathy, particularly when the clinical course is atypical or worsens after lumbar puncture or corticosteroid therapy, the MRI should be carefully reviewed for flow voids and dedicated spinal vascular imaging considered.
englishSummary: Introduction: Case Presentation: Outcome: Conclusions: Foix-Alajouanine syndrome (FAS) is a rare, progressive congestive ischaemic myelopathy caused by a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula (SDAVF). Because of its non-specific clinical presentation and subtle imaging features, FAS is frequently misdiagnosed; in particular, perimedullary flow voids-its characteristic imaging hallmark-are readily overlooked on initial MRI, leading to diagnostic delay and potentially harmful interventions.We report the case of a 66-year-old man who developed progressive myelopathy following revision knee arthroplasty performed under spinal anaesthesia. Initial MRI at another institution demonstrated extensive intramedullary T2 hyperintensity, interpreted as spinal cord infarction, while perimedullary flow voids were present but overlooked.

title: Paclitaxel retention of drug-coated balloons in veins and arteries under arteriovenous fistula hemodynamics.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: ex vivo Arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) are the preferred vascular access for hemodialysis, but venous stenosis remains a major limitation to long-term patency. Drug-coated balloons (DCBs) have emerged as a promising therapy to inhibit neointimal hyperplasia and reduce restenosis. However, inconsistent clinical outcomes have limited their adoption for AVF stenosis. The unique AVF environment-characterized by high flow, turbulent shear stress, and alternating arterial and venous segments-may influence drug transfer and retention within the vessel wall. Despite its importance, the impact of tissue type under AVF-specific hemodynamics on DCB performance remains poorly understood. This study investigates paclitaxel retention in venous and arterial tissue under simulated AVF conditions using anbioreactor system. MATERIALS AND METHODS: ex vivo The IN.PACT™ AV paclitaxel-coated balloon was deployed for 2 min in porcine veins and arteries within anAVF-simulating bioreactor. Treated vessel segments were collected at 1- and 24 h to quantify tissue paclitaxel concentration. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) was performed at 1 h to assess coating deposition on the luminal surface. RESULTS: p Hemodynamic conditions were comparable between venous and arterial groups, confirming physiologically relevant AVF flow and pressure. On log-transformed tissue paclitaxel concentrations, no statistically significant difference was detected between tissue types at either time point (two-way ANOVA, = 0.163; adjusted geometric mean ratio [vein/artery] = 2.69, 95% CI: 0.65-11.18), and drug levels decreased from 1- to 24 h in both groups. Venous samples exhibited greater variability, particularly at 1 h. SEM analysis revealed heterogeneous coating transfer in both tissues, with clustered deposits in veins and more distributed coverage in arteries. CONCLUSION: ex vivo This study establishes anplatform for mechanistic evaluation of catheter-based drug delivery in vascular access. Under AVF hemodynamics, no statistically significant difference in acute paclitaxel retention was observed between venous and arterial tissues despite structural differences (log-scale two-way ANOVA, adjusted geometric mean ratio [vein/artery] = 2.69, 95% CI: 0.65-11.18). This absence of detectable differences suggests that tissue type alone does not drive DCB performance in AVFs.

However, inconsistent clinical outcomes have limited their adoption for AVF stenosis.
