title: AngioJet rheolytic thrombectomy under superior vena cava filter protection for acute upper extremity deep vein thrombosis in patients with cancer: a single-center, retrospective analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The incidence of upper extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) is increasing, and percutaneous mechanical thrombectomy (PMT) is receiving more attention as a treatment option. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy and clinical outcomes of PMT combined with superior vena cava (SVC) filter protection in cancer patients with acute UEDVT. METHODS: This study included all patients with acute UEDVT who underwent treatment with an 8-Fr AngioJet thrombectomy system (Boston Scientific) under the protection of a retrievable SVC filter between January 1, 2020, and October 1, 2025. The evaluation indicators included technical success rate (defined as a thrombus clearance rate >80%), intraoperative adverse events, degree of limb swelling relief, incidence of pulmonary embolism, and thrombus recurrence during follow-up. RESULTS: A total of 19 patients (10 female; mean age 60.84 ± 11.30 years) were included. All patients had secondary UEDVT and a history of malignant tumors, with 14 cases (73.7%) having a history of central venous catheterization. All procedures achieved technical success, with no severe adverse events such as major bleeding occurring intraoperatively, nor were there any new symptomatic pulmonary embolisms. The average circumference of the affected limb 10 cm above the elbow before surgery was 29.83 ± 2.20 cm, which decreased to 26.98 ± 2.0 cm on the second postoperative day. During the 6-month follow-up, one patient with advanced lung cancer developed swelling of the upper limb on postoperative day 136, confirmed by ultrasound to be a recurrence of deep vein thrombosis; another patient was found to have an asymptomatic mural thrombus on ultrasound examination on postoperative day 28. CONCLUSION: PMT with the 8-Fr AngioJet system and SVC filter protection appears to be a safe and effective treatment option for cancer patients with acute UEDVT.

title: Perioperative Lactate, Survival, and Complications Following Lung Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To examine perioperative lactate and its association with survival and postoperative complications following lung transplantation (LTx). DESIGN: Single-center retrospective cohort study. SETTING: Academic tertiary-care transplant center. PARTICIPANTS: Adult patients undergoing LTx between February 2018 and January 2023. INTERVENTIONS: None. MEASUREMENTS AND MAIN RESULTS: Serum lactate was measured at 6-hour intervals from the start of surgery, and the maximum value within the first 0 to 6 hours was recorded. Patients were categorized into the high-lactate group (upper quartile, ≥4.2 mmol/L) and low-lactate group (lower 3 quartiles). Primary outcomes were 1-year and overall survival. Secondary outcomes included renal failure, venous thromboembolism (VTE), primary graft dysfunction grade 3 (PGD3), mechanical ventilation duration, intensive care unit (ICU) and post-transplant length of stay, and in-hospital mortality. Among 225 recipients (median age, 62.3 years; 34.2% female), high lactate was not associated with 1-year or overall survival. However, recipients with high lactate had higher rates of PGD3 at 72 hours (42.1% v 13.1%, p < 0.001), longer mechanical ventilation duration (3 days v 2 days, p = 0.003), longer ICU stay (11.6 days v 7 days, p = 0.013), and higher in-hospital mortality rate (7% v 0.6%, p = 0.019). No significant differences were observed in renal failure, VTE, or post-transplant length of stay. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated perioperative serum lactate was associated with PGD3 at 72 hours, prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer ICU stay, and in-hospital mortality but not 1-year or overall survival following LTx. These findings suggest that perioperative lactate may aid in identifying high-risk patients early in their postoperative course despite its lack of association with long-term survival.

title: Hemodynamic Analysis of Modified Splenic Arteriovenous Shunt in Pancreas Transplantation.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of a modified splenic arteriovenous shunt technique in pancreas transplantation through intraoperative hemodynamic monitoring and postoperative follow-up. METHODS: A total of 12 patients undergoing simultaneous pancreas-kidney transplantation were enrolled. Under three consecutive intraoperative states (spleen preserved, splenic arteriovenous clamped, and splenic arteriovenous shunt created), color Doppler ultrasound was used to measure peak systolic velocity (PS) and volumetric flow (VF) of the splenic artery and vein at the same point in the distal pancreatic tail, while portal venous pressure was recorded using an intravascular pressure transducer. Postoperative graft function, thrombotic events, and complications were regularly followed up. RESULTS: Compared with the spleen-preserved state, the clamped state showed significant reductions in splenic arterial PS and VF (15.24 ± 4.43 cm/s, 16.62 ± 6.84 mL/min) and splenic venous PS and VF (16.31 ± 3.82 cm/s, 60.32 ± 16.07 mL/min) (P < 0.001). In the shunt state, splenic arterial (54.47 ± 3.45 cm/s, 157.39 ± 11.24 mL/min) and venous (49.27 ± 6.61 cm/s, 177.89 ± 14.15 mL/min) flow parameters showed no significant differences compared with the spleen-preserved state (P > 0.05), but were significantly higher than those in the clamped state (P < 0.001). Portal venous pressure showed no significant differences among the three states (P > 0.05). At a median follow-up of 5 months, no graft thrombosis, pancreatitis, or gastrointestinal bleeding was observed, and patient and graft survival rates were both 100% at the last follow-up. Glycated hemoglobin decreased from 7.37% ± 0.68% preoperatively to 5.81% ± 0.32% (P < 0.005), and left ventricular ejection fraction increased from 59.50% ± 3.23% to 67.33% ± 2.84% (P < 0.005). CONCLUSION: The modified splenic arteriovenous shunt maintains physiological perfusion of the pancreatic allograft without elevating portal venous pressure, and may mitigate the hypoperfusion and blood stasis associated with conventional splenic vessel ligation. Based on the short-term results of this study, this modified technique appears safe and feasible, and may contribute to reducing early thrombotic complications after pancreas transplantation.

title: Vascular Management Strategies and Outcomes of Infectious Arterial Complications Involving the Kidney Transplant Vasculature: A Systematic Review and Evidence-Informed Treatment Framework.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant (KT) vasculature are rare but life-threatening and frequently result in KT loss. The lack of evidence-based guidance for vascular management strategies underscores the need for systematic synthesis to inform clinical decision-making. METHODS: A systematic search was performed from database inception through August 22, 2025, for reports of culture-proven infectious vascular complications-including arterial rupture, detachment, pseudoaneurysm, aneurysm, thrombosis, or stenosis-involving the transplant renal artery, iliac vessels, or arterial anastomosis in KT recipients. Eligible studies reported vascular management strategies. Due to methodological heterogeneity, findings were synthesized narratively using proportion-based comparisons. RESULTS: Eighty reports (1972-2025) comprising 139 cases were included. Candida species were most frequent, followed by Pseudomonas, Aspergillus, and Staphylococcus species. Pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant clinical presentation, typically occuring within the first month after transplantation. Outcome patterns differed by transplant nephrectomy status, with vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrating higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up. Autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern (86.7% uneventful recovery; 6.7% reintervention and mortality), even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable. Covered stent placement was the most frequently reported intervention andshowed favorable outcomes in selected KT-preserving cases (75% uneventful recovery). Primary surgical repair had the highest reintervention proportion (59.1%), whereas arterial ligation had the highest mortality (43.8%) and accounted for all reported limb loss. CONCLUSION: Across five decades of case-based evidence, autologous interposition grafting demonstrated the most favorable outcome pattern and may represent the preferred vascular management strategy when durable arterial reconstruction is feasible, including when transplant nephrectomy is required. Covered stent placement may provide a useful option in selected cases or as a temporizing strategy for hemorrhage control. These findings should guide rather than define management decisions given the heterogeneous evidence base. HIGHLIGHTS: First systematic synthesis of management strategies for infectious arterial complications involving the kidney transplant vasculature Candida was the most frequently reported pathogen; pseudoaneurysm and arterial rupture were the predominant presentations Vascular management strategies performed without transplant nephrectomy demonstrated higher reported proportions of uneventful follow-up Autologous interposition grafting showed the most favorable reported outcome pattern, even when transplant nephrectomy is unavoidable Ligation and primary repair were associated with higher reported mortality and reintervention, respectively.

title: PGC1α/SIRT3-Mediated Oxidative Stress and Downregulation of NLRP3 Expression by Sodium Thiosulfate Pre- and Post-Treatment Accelerates Recovery from Ischemia-Reperfusion-Induced Acute Kidney Injury.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: p p p p p p Renal ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is the leading cause of acute kidney injury (AKI). It is associated with reduced blood flow as encountered in vascular surgery, including aortic aneurysm repair and kidney transplantation. In this study, we investigated whether pre- and/or post-administration of sodium thiosulfate (STS), an FDA-approved hydrogen sulfide donor drug, attenuated IRI-induced AKI in rats.AKI was induced in male rats by clamping both renal arteries for 60 min. At 30 min before clamping, and 30 min after reperfusion, STS was administered at a weigh-based dose to achieve a circulating concentration of 150 μM, after which the rats were kept in metabolic cages for urine and blood collection on postoperative days (POD) 3, 5, and 7. Rats were sacrificed on POD3, POD5, and POD7, and kidneys were harvested for analysis. Sham-operated rats received no treatment.AKI was evidenced by markedly higher acute tubular necrosis score, and renal protein and gene expression of damage markers (KIM-1 and NGAL), as well as markers of oxidative stress (MDA, GSH, and SOD), inflammation (MPO, IL-6), and apoptosis (TUNEL). While significant incremental improvement was observed in the expression of these markers in the pre-treatment only and post-treatment only groups over the POD3-7 observation period compared to untreated control group (< 0.05), superior renal protection was observed in the pre + post-treatment group (< 0.01). Functionally, serum creatinine levels were significantly higher over the POD3-7 observation period in the untreated group relative to pre-treatment and post-treatment groups (< 0.05), and markedly lower in the pre + post-treatment group (< 0.001), which positively correlated with urine output. Urine osmolality was statistically similar to sham-operated rats on POD5 and 7, while all other groups showed decreased urine osmolality on POD3 and 5 (< 0.05). Mechanistically, the protective effect of STS correlated with upregulation of PGC1α and SIRT3 protein and gene expression and downregulation of NLRP3 protein and mRNA expression in the pre + post-treatment group compared to other groups (< 0.05).The present study reports for the first time the protective effect of STS against IRI-induced AKI, and indicates PGC1α, SIRT3, and NLRP3 as molecular targets of STS.

title: Intended Thrombectomy for Basilar Artery Occlusion with Mild Deficits: Evidence from a Multicenter Prospective Registry.
abstract: P Supplemental material is available for this article. Background The role of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) in basilar artery occlusion (BAO) with mild deficits (National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score < 10) remains uncertain. Purpose To compare the outcomes of EVT combined with best medical management (BMM) versus BMM alone in individuals with BAO and mild deficits. Materials and Methods Consecutive eligible patients treated at eight stroke centers between September 2023 and March 2025 were enrolled in a prospective registry. The primary outcome was 90-day functional independence (modified Rankin Scale [mRS] score of 0-2). Secondary outcomes were 90-day excellent outcome (mRS score of 0-1), death, and early neurologic deterioration (END), defined as a four-point or greater increase in NIHSS score within 72 hours. Primary analyses followed an intention-to-treat-like framework with inverse probability weighting (IPW). As-treated and per-protocol sensitivity analyses were used to assess the robustness of the results and the impact of treatment crossover (EVT after END). Results Among 401 participants (mean age, 64.9 years ± 8.9 [SD]; 278 male participants), the median onset-to-arterial-puncture time in the EVT group was 402 minutes (IQR, 271-583 minutes). After multivariable adjustment in the IPW-adjusted data, EVT was associated with higher odds of functional independence (odds ratio [OR], 1.55 [95% CI: 1.17, 2.06]) and excellent outcome (OR, 1.48 [95% CI: 1.09, 2.03]) and lower odds of death (OR, 0.65 [95% CI: 0.45, 0.77]) and END (OR, 0.35 [95% CI: 0.20, 0.61]). Subgroup analyses demonstrated EVT-related functional benefit in participants with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not in those with NIHSS scores of 0-5 (for interaction = .02 for functional independence); however, in participants with NIHSS scores of 0-5, EVT was associated with lower odds of END and death. Sensitivity analyses accounting for treatment crossover showed attenuated functional advantage for EVT. Conclusion In participants with BAO and mild deficits, EVT plus BMM was associated with better outcomes than BMM alone; however, functional benefit was observed in those with NIHSS scores of 6-9 but not those with NIHSS scores of 0-5. title: Case 351: Thalamic Dementia Secondary to Dural Arteriovenous Fistula.
abstract: A 76-year-old man with a medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and dilated cardiomyopathy developed new symptoms of confusion, repeated falls, and urinary incontinence over the course of 3-4 months, which worsened over a 2-week period, leading to presentation at the emergency room. His partner reported that before this, he had no memory or movement disorders, but now he was experiencing memory lapses, such as forgetting his mother's recent death, and functional cognitive problems, including an inability to remember how to perform tasks that were previously simple for him, such as dosing his insulin with meals. At presentation, the patient was awake and alert, oriented to his name and location but not to the date. Full neurologic examinations, including of the motor and sensory systems and cranial nerves, were normal. There were no signs of meningism, no fever or leukocytosis, and no history of recent travel. Serum electrolyte panel and thiamine levels were normal, and he had no history of alcohol or drug abuse. Initial evaluation included noncontrast CT of the head, the results of which prompted multiphasic CT angiography of the head including parenchymal phase imaging and admission for observation and monitoring with serial noncontrast CT of the head. The patient's symptoms worsened during his hospital stay. He also developed facial twitching, increased drowsiness, and seizure episodes. He was therefore evaluated with noncontrast MRI of the brain and then digital subtraction angiography with external carotid artery and internal carotid artery contrast agent injections.

title: Complication Prevention in Combined Abdominoplasty and Gynecologic Procedures: A Multidisciplinary Narrative Review.
abstract: P Level of Evidence: Combined abdominoplasty (ABP) and open gynecologic surgery is an established approach that may reduce anesthesia exposure, shorten convalescence, and lower costs relative to staged procedures, yet its safety profile and optimal perioperative management remain incompletely defined, with a heterogeneous evidence base and no updated synthesis since 2007. The authors conducted a narrative review, searching PubMed, MEDLINE, and Scopus from inception to March 2026 for studies of combined open ABP and gynecologic procedures in adults; 14 studies published between 1983 and 2022 were included, comprising retrospective cohorts, case series, case-control, and observational studies, 1 literature review, and 2 case reports (sample sizes 1-269). Reported outcomes were heterogeneous: some early series described longer operative times and greater morbidity, whereas recent comparative data found combined ABP-hysterectomy associated with a complication rate comparable to or lower than staged surgery (7.7% vs 12.5%;= .04) alongside reduced operative and anesthesia times. Key modifiable risk factors include smoking, obesity, and the American Society of Anesthesiologists class. Formal venous thromboembolism risk stratification using the Caprini model with risk-adjusted prophylaxis, prophylactic antibiotics, maintenance of normothermia, separate instrument sets, and coordinated multidisciplinary planning are the principal evidence-based strategies for complication prevention. Rare delayed complications, notably abdominal-wall endometrioma, are consistently missed by short-term follow-up. Combined ABP and open gynecologic surgery can be performed safely in appropriately selected patients, although the evidence is limited by retrospective designs and outcome heterogeneity; prospective multicenter studies with standardized reporting and long-term follow-up are needed.3 (Therapeutic) For image description, please refer to the figure legend and surrounding text.

title: Stroke and Bleeding Risk in Long-Term Care Residents With Atrial Fibrillation Who Discontinue Anticoagulation.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Atrial fibrillation (AF) leads to more than 100 000 cases of stroke yearly and is particularly prevalent in long-term care (LTC) residents. Anticoagulation (AC) is the mainstay of stroke prevention, but given its risks, clinicians and residents may consider discontinuation at the time of LTC entry. OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between AC discontinuation and stroke and bleeding risk among LTC residents with AF. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This comparative effectiveness research study with target trial emulation used claims data (2020-2021) from LTC facilities in the US serving Medicare beneficiaries. Medicare beneficiaries with AF receiving AC who entered LTC between April 1 and December 31, 2020, were included; those with additional indications for AC, including prosthetic heart valve or venous thromboembolism, were excluded. Analysis was performed in August 2026. EXPOSURE: Discontinuer vs continuer assignment. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The main outcomes were stroke (including ischemic stroke, transient ischemic attack, and systemic embolism) and bleeding, assessed using Medicare claims. A target trial emulation was conducted with clone censor weighting (CCW) analysis. Specifically, eligible LTC residents were assigned (cloned) to each of 2 strategies: AC discontinuation or AC continuation. Clones were then censored when they deviated from their assigned strategy, and inverse probability of censoring weighting was applied to address informative censoring: residents who deviated differing systematically from those who did not. Subdistribution hazard ratios (sHRs) for stroke and bleeding were then calculated to account for competing mortality and a cause-specific hazard ratio (HR) for death. RESULTS: This study included 15 426 LTC residents (mean [SD] age, 82.6 [7.6] years). Most were female (62.6%). AC discontinuers had 187 strokes, 297 bleeding events, and 3684 deaths over a mean (SD) of 128.9 (177.9) days. AC continuers had 321 strokes, 493 bleeding events, and 5475 deaths over a mean (SD) of 279.6 (204.9) days. Discontinuers had similar stroke risk (sHR, 1.07; 95% CI, 0.93-1.23) and bleeding risk (sHR, 1.02; 95% CI, 0.92-1.13) compared with continuers, but discontinuers had higher mortality risk (HR, 1.27; 95% CI, 1.23-1.31). CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this target trial emulation with CCW in a cohort of LTC residents with AF, AC discontinuation was not associated with higher stroke or bleeding risk. Very high mortality, unmeasured confounding, and reliance on claims-based outcome ascertainment may have limited the ability to better understand the consequences of AC discontinuation on stroke and bleeding.

OBJECTIVE: To estimate the association between AC discontinuation and stroke and bleeding risk among LTC residents with AF.

title: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus Bacteremia Associated with Systemic Hemangiomatosis in an Elderly Patient with Ulcerative Colitis: A Case Report.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aggregatibacter aphrophilus, Older patients on biologic therapy for inflammatory bowel disease may be at increased risk for opportunistic infections, reflecting both age-related and immunosuppression-related factors.a HACEK organism, is a rare cause of invasive infection that is typically associated with endovascular disease. We present the case of a 70-year-old male with ulcerative colitis treated with adalimumab who presented with 4 weeks of fevers, chills, night sweats, and weight loss. Endoscopy demonstrated a vascular-appearing esophageal lesion, and MRI revealed diffuse hemangiomatosis involving the esophagus, spleen, and head and neck musculature. Adalimumab was held after discharge, and ulcerative colitis was subsequently managed with mesalamine with achievement of clinical remission. CONCLUSION: A. aphrophilus. title: Porphyromonas gingivalis Deer antler tip cell culture supernatant restores endothelial barrier function and angiotensin converting enzyme 2/endothelial nitric oxide synthase nitric oxide signaling impaired bylipopolysaccharide.
abstract: BACKGROUND/PURPOSE: Porphyromonas gingivalis Pg Periodontal inflammation contributes to endothelial dysfunction, but effective biologically active strategies for vascular protection remain limited. This study investigated whether deer antler tip cell culture supernatant could rescuelipopolysaccharide (-LPS) induced endothelial injury and restore endothelial homeostasis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Pg Velvet antler tissues from the tip, shaft, and burr regions were examined histologically and used for primary cell isolation. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells were exposed to-LPS or indirectly co-cultured with LPS-stimulated THP-1-derived macrophages. Deer antler tip cell culture supernatant was subsequently applied to these endothelial inflammatory models, and its protective effects were assessed by quantitative functional assays, Western blotting, and qPCR. Public venous thromboembolism transcriptomic datasets were analyzed to evaluate the translational relevance of the endothelial injury and repair signatures. RESULTS: Pg- Pg The antler tip showed a vascular-rich regenerative niche with stem/progenitor-associated features. In HUVECs,LPS induced inflammatory activation, oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction, whereas deer antler tip cell culture supernatant attenuated these changes. It also suppressed macrophage-mediated endothelial injury and reduced-LPS induced inflammatory activation in THP-1-derived macrophages. In an optimized endothelial injury model, deer antler tip cell culture supernatant dose-dependently restored endothelial homeostasis- and mechanosensitive-associated gene expression. Public datasets further supported the translational relevance of these endothelial stress signatures. CONCLUSION: Pg Deer antler tip cell culture supernatant protects against-LPS associated endothelial inflammatory injury and may serve as a promising biologically active strategy for vascular protection.

title: Trends in Direct Oral Anticoagulant Use for Cancer-Associated Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) are recommended for selected patients with cancer-associated venous thromboembolism, but their implementation remains heterogeneous. OBJECTIVE: To describe temporal trends in DOAC initiation for cancer-associated venous thromboembolism in France and to identify factors associated with their use. DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This nationwide population-based cohort study included adults without recorded contraindications to DOACs and a first treated venous thromboembolism episode between January 1, 2016, and December 31, 2022. Data were collected from the French National Health Data System, a nationwide claims database covering approximately 99% of the population. Analysis was performed from January to August 2025. EXPOSURES: Patients were classified into active cancer and no active cancer groups. Covariates included calendar period, patient characteristics, cancer type and treatment, venous thromboembolism characteristics, and initial prescriber setting. MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was DOAC initiation within 30 days after the index venous thromboembolism event. Bayesian structural time series models assessed temporal changes across 2016 to 2018, 2019 to 2020, and 2021 to 2022. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with DOAC initiation among patients with active cancer. RESULTS: Among 683 184 patients with incident treated venous thromboembolism (median [IQR] age, 67 [53-77] years; 347 421 female [51.0%]), 91 954 patients (13.5%) had active cancer while 591 230 (86.5%) had VTE not associated with active cancer. DOAC use increased from 15.3% (95% CI, 15.0%-15.7%) in 2016 to 2018 to 32.6% (95% CI, 32.1%-33.2%) in 2021 to 2022 among patients with active cancer, and from 63.5% (95% CI, 63.3%-63.7%) to 81.1% (95% CI, 80.9%-81.2%) among patients without active cancer. DOAC initiation increased beyond expected secular trends in patients with active cancer, with relative increases of 20.5% (95% credible interval, 13.0%-27.8%) in 2019 to 2020 and 41.3% (95% credible interval, 32.9%-50.2%) in 2021 to 2022. DOAC initiation was less frequent among patients with comorbidities, history of bleeding, gastrointestinal or gynecologic cancer, active brain metastases, or systemic treatment, and when the initial prescriber was a hospital-based physician rather than a general practitioner. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort study of patients with incident venous thromboembolism, DOAC use increased substantially in patients with active cancer but remained lower than in patients without active cancer and varied across clinical and care-setting characteristics. This lower uptake may reflect both delayed implementation of recent evidence and the need to individualize anticoagulant selection in complex situations.

title: Introgression Shapes Genetic Variation Associated With Humid Environments in Aedes aegypti Mosquitoes From Saudi Arabia.
abstract: Introgression between genetically distinct populations generates variation that may promote adaptation to diverse environmental conditions. In the mosquito Aedes aegypti, the forest-associated subspecies Aedes aegypti formosus (Aaf) underwent a domestication process approximately 5000 years ago, giving rise to the globally invasive, human-associated arbovirus vector Aedes aegypti aegypti (Aaa). Despite extensive human-mediated transport, the two subspecies remain largely distinct, with admixture documented mainly in coastal Africa and Saudi Arabia. We examined Saudi Arabian Ae. aegypti across climatically contrasting regions - the humid south and arid west- using a Saudi Arabian dataset (11,939 SNPs) to examine within-country genetic and environmental variation and a global dataset (13,455 SNPs) to assess ancestry and admixture in a worldwide context. Genomic analyses revealed strong west-south differentiation, with Jazan Highland showing admixture between subspecies and the highest proportion of Aaf ancestry. Multiple pulses of gene flow into and within southern Saudi Arabia suggest Aaf populations act as a reservoir of genetic variation. Genome-wide scans identified a candidate region associated with the humidity gradient, harbouring an elongase of very long-chain fatty acids (AAEL024147), essential for cuticle production and minimizing water loss. Because the Saudi Arabian genetic background is predominantly the arid-adapted subspecies Aaa, the presence of Aaf ancestry at this locus may reflect localized introgression with adaptive relevance under an increasingly humid environment. Our findings highlight how secondary contact between divergent lineages may contribute to local adaptation in Ae. aegypti, with implications for predicting responses to environmental change.

Despite extensive human-mediated transport, the two subspecies remain largely distinct, with admixture documented mainly in coastal Africa and Saudi Arabia.

title: Improving Apheresis Inlet Flow With a Novel Double-Draw Vascular Access Technique.
abstract: Peripheral intravenous catheters (PIVCs) are the preferred vascular access for apheresis; however, veins that initially appear suitable may develop venous spasms, resulting in poor inlet flow and frequent pressure alarms. Ports used for apheresis can also experience inlet pressure alarms due to catheter or venous occlusion. When conservative measures failed, we implemented a novel double-draw technique in which a second draw line was connected via a four-way stopcock and male-to-male adapter to the initial draw access (either a PIVC or port) to improve inlet flow. The double-draw technique was performed in 26 procedures (therapeutic plasma exchange [TPE], n = 10 and lipoprotein apheresis [LA], n = 16) in 8 patients. During TPE, median negative inlet pressure improved from -179 mmHg (IQR -218 to -69) with single-draw access to -71 mmHg (IQR -78 to -62) following placement of a second draw line (p = 0.0162). Inlet flow rate during TPE improved from median 47 mL/min (IQR, 40-58 mL/min) with single-draw access to 70 mL/min (IQR, 60-75 mL/min) (p = 0.008). During LA, median negative inlet pressure improved from -136 mmHg (IQR -193 to -109) to -59 mmHg (IQR -66 to -47) (p < 0.0001). Median inlet flow rate during LA improved from 70 mL/min (IQR 59-71 mL/min) with single-draw access to median 80 mL/min (IQR 70-80 mL/min) (p = 0.023). Overall 25 of 26 procedures (96.2%) demonstrated an improvement in inlet pressure following implementation of the double-draw technique. All procedures were completed successfully without abandonment of the original access site. The double-draw technique is a novel option for managing inlet pressure alarms during apheresis when conservative measures fail.

title: Subcutaneous and extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillators: a clinical framework for breast surgery, pregnancy, lactation, radiation therapy, and breast imaging.
abstract: The subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator and extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator do not require intravascular, intracardiac, or epicardial leads, making them attractive alternatives to transvenous implantable cardioverter-defibrillators in patients without bradycardia pacing or cardiac resynchronization therapy indications. These systems are especially useful for patients with venous access challenges and those at risk for endovascular infections, including patients with renal failure or those who are immunocompromised. Women with prior or anticipated breast surgery, such as mastectomy or breast reconstruction surgery, or those who are lactating present unique anatomic, procedural, and post-operative quality-of-life considerations. This commentary provides a practical, scenario-based framework for managing this unique patient group. Key considerations include individualized incision and pulse generator planning, proactive multidisciplinary coordination, procedure-specific management, and shared decision-making in patients with prior or anticipated breast augmentation or reduction, pregnancy, lactation, mastectomy, radiation therapy, and breast imaging.

These systems are especially useful for patients with venous access challenges and those at risk for endovascular infections, including patients with renal failure or those who are immunocompromised. title: Evaluating the Impact of Therapeutic Anticoagulation Management in Head and Neck Free Tissue Transfer: A Retrospective Study of 126 Cases.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Existing literature on anticoagulation in head and neck free flap reconstruction largely focuses on postoperative thromboprophylaxis. Less is known about preoperative therapeutic anticoagulation, including how perioperative anticoagulation holds, timing of resumption, and anticoagulant class relate to hemorrhagic, thromboembolic, and flap-related complications. This study evaluates these outcomes in anticoagulated patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction and compares complication rates with matched non-anticoagulated controls. METHODS: A retrospective chart review was performed on patients who underwent free flap reconstruction between 2009 and 2023 and had been on therapeutic anticoagulation for over 1 month preoperatively. A matched control group of non-anticoagulated patients was included for comparison. RESULTS: 126 anticoagulated patients (mean age 71.8 years, 75.4% male) were included. The most common indications for anticoagulation were atrial fibrillation (62.7%) and venous thromboembolism (30.2%). Anticoagulation medications included warfarin (49.2%), apixaban (36.5%), rivaroxaban (12.7%), and dabigatran (1.6%). Anticoagulation was stopped an average of 4.4 days preoperatively and resumed 7.8 days postoperatively. Hemorrhagic complications occurred in 14 patients (11.1%), including hematomas and unrelated bleeding. Thromboembolic complications occurred in 9 patients (7.1%), 6 of which resulted in flap failure. On matched cohort analysis, controls had lower odds of any complication (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.21-0.81, p = 0.010), hemorrhagic or thromboembolic complications (OR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11-0.63, p = 0.003), and hemorrhagic complications specifically (OR 0.26, 95% CI 0.09-0.81, p = 0.020), while thromboembolic complication odds were not significantly different between groups (OR 0.47, 95% CI 0.15-1.44, p = 0.19). CONCLUSIONS: This study highlights the challenges of managing therapeutic anticoagulation in head and neck free flap surgery, where thromboembolic risk during interruption and hemorrhagic complications upon resumption point to the need for clearer guidelines. Evidence-based protocols are needed to replace discretionary practices and improve outcomes.
englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Existing literature on anticoagulation in head and neck free flap reconstruction largely focuses on postoperative thromboprophylaxis. Less is known about preoperative therapeutic anticoagulation, including how perioperative anticoagulation holds, timing of resumption, and anticoagulant class relate to hemorrhagic, thromboembolic, and flap-related complications. This study evaluates these outcomes in anticoagulated patients undergoing head and neck free flap reconstruction and compares complication rates with matched non-anticoagulated controls.

title: Association between admission D-dimer levels and post-stroke epilepsy risk: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Post-stroke epilepsy (PSE) is a severe complication following acute ischemic stroke (AIS), yet early identification of patients at high risk remains challenging. This study evaluated the association between baseline D-dimer levels and incident PSE within one year after AIS. METHODS: 2 In this secondary analysis of a multicenter retrospective cohort, 21,459 patients with first-ever AIS were included. D-dimer was modeled as a log-transformed continuous variable. Multivariable logistic regression with progressive adjustment, restricted cubic spline analysis, and sensitivity analyses were performed. Internal validation was conducted using bootstrap resampling. RESULTS: The median baseline D-dimer level was 0.92 mg/L (IQR 0.65-1.49). PSE occurred in 936 patients (4.36%). After full adjustment, each doubling of D-dimer was associated with a 3.3-fold increase in PSE odds (OR 3.33, 95% CI 2.94-3.78). The association remained consistent in sensitivity analyses excluding patients with deep vein thrombosis (OR 3.86, 95% CI 3.37-4.43), atrial fibrillation (OR 3.50, 95% CI 3.04-4.04), or extreme D-dimer values (OR 3.41, 95% CI 2.99-3.91). A non-linear relationship was observed, with PSE risk rising more steeply at higher D-dimer levels. The C-statistic for the fully adjusted model was 0.968. CONCLUSION: Elevated baseline D-dimer levels were independently associated with an increased risk of PSE within one year after AIS. As a routinely available biomarker, D-dimer may inform risk assessment in acute stroke units; however, external validation in independent cohorts with prospective PSE ascertainment is required before clinical implementation.

title: Signal of venous thromboembolism with ethinyl estradiol vs natural estrogens in oral contraceptives: analysis of the EudraVigilance and Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System databases.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Disproportionality analyses in the Food and Drug Administration Adverse Events Reporting System (FAERS) and EudraVigilance reported lower reporting of venous thromboembolism (VTE) with natural estrogen-based combined oral contraceptives (COCs) than with ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel. However, using ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel as the reference showed reduced reporting only for natural estrogen-based products. We therefore reanalyzed both databases separately, using natural estrogen-based COCs as the reference. METHODS: 2 Previously extracted individual case safety report datasets and published disproportionality analyses were re-examined, using natural estrogen-based contraceptives as the comparator. Proportional reporting ratios (PRRs) were recalculated separately for each database. COCs were categorized as ethinylestradiol-based or natural estrogen-based formulations. Drospirenone-only pills were included for comparison. Analyses used pooled natural estrogen contraceptives, estetrol/drospirenone, or estradiol/dienogest as reference groups. Disproportionality was defined as PRR >2, at least 3 cases, and χ≥ 4. DISCUSSION: Consistent patterns were observed in EudraVigilance and FAERS. Compared with natural estrogen-based COCs, ethinylestradiol-based COCs showed a disproportionate reporting of VTE (EudraVigilance: PRR, 5.10 [95% CI, 4.68-5.56]; FAERS: PRR, 4.21 [95% CI, 3.49-5.08]). In EudraVigilance, when using estetrol/drospirenone as the reference, all ethinylestradiol-based formulations showed disproportionality according to the conventional PRR threshold. A similar trend was noted in FAERS, though not statistically significant, with the drospirenone-only formulation comparable to estetrol/drospirenone. CONCLUSION: This analysis revealed a consistent and disproportionate reporting of VTE associated with ethinylestradiol-based COCs compared with natural estrogen-based alternatives across 2 pharmacovigilance databases. These results, together with prior biological and observational research, support further reevaluation of COC options given the estrogenic component's potential influence on VTE risk.

However, using ethinylestradiol/levonorgestrel as the reference showed reduced reporting only for natural estrogen-based products. We therefore reanalyzed both databases separately, using natural estrogen-based COCs as the reference.

title: When Diabetes Mimics Scleroderma: Cheiroarthropathy and Neuropathic Digital Erosions in Type 2 Diabetes.
abstract: Diabetic cheiroarthropathy is an underrecognized complication of diabetes characterized by limited finger joint extension and thickened, waxy skin of the hands. It can clinically mimic several rheumatologic conditions, particularly systemic sclerosis, creating a diagnostic challenge. We report the case of a 68-year-old man with long-standing type 2 diabetes mellitus who presented with hand stiffness and contractures, scleroderma-like skin thickening, and nonpainful crusted digital erosions, raising concern for systemic sclerosis-associated digital ulceration. He underwent rheumatologic evaluation and received immunosuppressive therapy without improvement in the cutaneous findings, prompting further clinical reassessment. His overall clinical phenotype, including a positive prayer sign, skin thickening confined to the digits, absence of Raynaud phenomenon, normal nailfold capillaries, and negative anti-Scl-70 and anticentromere antibodies, favored diabetic cheiroarthropathy over systemic sclerosis. The digital erosions were considered likely multifactorial, with contributions from unrecognized trauma in the setting of diabetic neuropathy and possible vascular compromise related to peripheral arterial disease and tobacco use. This case highlights the clinical overlap between diabetic cheiroarthropathy and systemic sclerosis, particularly when digital erosions accompany scleroderma-like hand changes. Recognizing this presentation may help prevent misdiagnosis and unnecessary immunosuppression while directing management toward glycemic control, prevention of repetitive trauma, local wound care, and occupational therapy.

title: Short-Term Outcomes of Lower-Extremity Surgical Revascularization for Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Among Yemeni Patients: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) carries a high risk of amputation and mortality. We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen. We enrolled 39 consecutive adults with CLTI (Rutherford categories 4-6) who were selected for and considered fit to undergo open lower-extremity surgical revascularization between December 2022 and September 2024; follow-up was completed in December 2024. The study protocol was reviewed and approved by the Al-Thawra Hospital Ethics Committee (approval no. 33-2026), and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. The study was not registered. This was an exploratory consecutive cohort; no formal sample-size calculation was performed, and no contemporaneous endovascular, nonoperative, or primary-amputation comparator group was included. Primary endpoints were graft patency and limb salvage at three months. Secondary outcomes were secondary patency, postoperative complications, and changes in ankle-brachial index (ABI) and Vascular Quality of Life Questionnaire-6 (VascuQoL-6) scores. Paired comparisons used Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; Fisher's exact tests were used for categorical comparisons. RESULTS: The mean age was 60.9 years (SD 9.7), and 30 patients (76.9%) were male. Diabetes mellitus and hypertension were present in 34 (87.2%) and 30 (76.9%) patients, respectively. Nineteen patients (48.7%) had ischemic rest pain, and 20 (51.3%) had tissue loss. Great saphenous vein (GSV) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) grafts were used in 28 (71.8%) and 11 (28.2%) patients, respectively. At three months, primary patency was 84.6% (33/39 grafts; 95% CI 70.3%-92.8%), secondary patency was 89.7% (35/39 grafts; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%), and limb salvage was 89.7% (35/39 patients; 95% CI 76.4%-95.9%). Given the small cohort, the confidence intervals around these estimates were relatively wide. Among the 35 patients with limb preservation, mean ABI increased from 0.35 (SD 0.11) to 0.55 (SD 0.12; mean difference 0.21, 95% CI 0.19-0.23; p<0.001), and mean VascuQoL-6 score increased from 10.3 (SD 2.9) to 16.6 (SD 4.0; mean difference 6.3, 95% CI 5.6-7.1; p<0.001). Complications occurred in nine patients (23.1%). In an exploratory unadjusted subgroup analysis, GSV use was associated with higher primary patency than PTFE use (92.9% vs 63.6%, p=0.042). CONCLUSION: In this single-center prospective cohort, open surgical revascularization was feasible and was associated with 89.7% limb salvage and 84.6% primary patency at three months. Improvements in ABI and VascuQoL-6 were observed among patients with limb preservation. Autologous GSV use was associated with higher primary patency; this finding requires confirmation in larger, adjusted studies.

We evaluated short-term clinical, hemodynamic, and quality-of-life outcomes after open lower-extremity surgical revascularization in a Yemeni cohort. METHODS: This single-center prospective observational cohort study was conducted at Al-Thawra Modern General Hospital, Sana'a, Yemen.

title: Association of the Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index with Ascending Aortic Diameter and Dilatation: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
abstract: Background and Objectives Materials and Methods n n Results p p p p Conclusions : Complete blood count-derived inflammatory indices are inexpensive and widely available, but data on their relationship with ascending aortic size are limited. This study examined the association between the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) and ascending aortic diameter, and compared these indices according to the presence of ascending aortic dilatation (AAD) defined by a 40 mm threshold.: In this single-centre retrospective cross-sectional study, 251 patients aged 18 years or older (mean age, 53.1 ± 16.7 years; range, 18-95 years; 160 men) who underwent thoracic computed tomography angiography were grouped by maximum tubular ascending aortic diameter (<40 mm,= 158; ≥40 mm,= 93). Inference for the primary linear model was based on heteroscedasticity-consistent (HC3) standard errors. Height and weight were not recorded, so the models could not be adjusted for body size.: In unadjusted comparisons, platelet and neutrophil counts, creatinine and all five inflammatory indices were nominally higher in the dilated group (all< 0.05), whereas C-reactive protein did not differ. In the primary adjusted model, each 100-unit increase in SII was associated with a 0.59 mm greater ascending aortic diameter (HC3 95% CI 0.28 to 0.90; β = 0.197;< 0.001), approximately 1.6 mm across the interquartile range of SII; the model explained 26.9% of the variance. Higher SII was also associated with AAD in the secondary logistic model (odds ratio per 100 units, 1.34; 95% CI 1.17 to 1.53;< 0.001). Discrimination was weak (area under the curve for SII, 0.658; 95% CI 0.590 to 0.726); the sample-derived cut-off gave a positive likelihood ratio of 1.38, and its 2.5-97.5th percentile interval on bootstrap internal validation was 305 to 579. None of the 75 correlations survived false discovery rate adjustment, and the SII-by-sex interaction was not significant (= 0.621).: Higher SII was associated with a greater ascending aortic diameter and with the presence of AAD after adjustment for the measured covariates; because body size could not be accounted for, residual confounding cannot be excluded. The adjusted difference was modest and discrimination was weak. These findings do not support the use of SII as a standalone diagnostic marker for ascending aortic dilatation.

title: Integrated Analysis of Serotonin-Related Biomarkers in Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Based on Machine Learning and Single-Cell Sequencing Data.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: Serotonin, as an important neurotransmitter and signaling molecule, can affect thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA) by regulating vascular cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and immune status. This research aimed to conduct a comprehensive analysis to pinpoint serotonin-related biomarkers in TAA and to elucidate their potential molecular mechanisms.Biomarkers were selected and validated through differential expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), machine learning algorithms, and expression verification. Moreover, the constructed nomogram, enrichment analysis, immune infiltration analysis, and compound prediction validated the regulatory roles of the biomarkers in TAA. The single-cell dataset was analyzed to determine key cells and perform pseudo-time analysis. Simulated knockout of biomarkers was performed to determine their underlying functions and related pathways. Finally, reverse transcription quantitative PCR (RT-qPCR) was employed to confirm the expression levels of the biomarkers.Overall, two biomarkers (CD300A and CLU) were determined to be associated with serotonin in TAA. The nomogram showed good performance in predicting TAA risk. These biomarkers were significantly enriched in the hematopoietic cell lineage and natural killer (NK) cell mediated cytotoxicity. Biomarker expression was significantly correlated with the infiltration proportions of M2 macrophages and neutrophils. The biomarkers were stably bound to tetrachlorodibenzodioxin and bisphenol A. Moreover, pseudo-time analysis demonstrated a notable correlation between biomarker expression and the differentiation status of monocytes/macrophages/dendritic cells (MonoMac/DC). Genes perturbed by knockout were enriched in the pyrimidine metabolism and RIG-I-like receptor signaling pathway. Finally, RT-qPCR validated that CLU was downregulated and CD300A was upregulated in the TAA group.Biomarkers (CD300A and CLU) associated with serotonin in TAA were identified, with their expression trends validated by RT-qPCR. This work provides novel bioinformatic insights, and direct functional experiments are required to support future therapeutic development for TAA.

title: Transcatheter Electrosurgical Aortic Septotomy Across the Spectrum of Type B Aortic Dissection: Feasibility, Technical Lessons, and Bailout Strategies.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter electrosurgical aortic septotomy (TEAS) has been introduced to optimise luminal geometry during endovascular repair of complex type B aortic dissection (TBAD), but data across dissection phases and on complication management remain limited. This study reports early outcomes, quantitative common lumen creation, and bailout strategies from a consecutive single centre experience. METHOD: Eight consecutive patients underwent TEAS, between December 2024 and January 2026, as an adjunct to thoracic endovascular aortic repair or physician modified fenestrated endograft for acute, subacute, or chronic TBAD, including post-type A repair and genetic aortopathy. Pre-procedural and follow up computed tomography angiography (CTA) quantified true lumen and common lumen cross sectional area. Septotomy technical success, peri-operative outcomes, complications, and early follow up were assessed. RESULTS: 2 2 The mean age was 51.1 ± 17 years; five were men. Two patients were acute, two subacute, and four chronic; two had Marfan syndrome, both redo cases after previous open repair. Septotomy technical success was 100%. The median cross sectional area increased from 174.5 mm(pre-procedural true lumen) to 1 007 mm(follow up CTA common lumen) after TEAS (5.3 fold increase). There were no 30 day, in hospital, or aortic related deaths. Three major procedure related complications (38%) occurred, all in non-acute cases and all managed endovascularly: one iliac lamellar dislodgement requiring kissing stents, one external iliac rupture treated with stent grafting, and one delayed superior mesenteric artery occlusion managed with stenting. All acute cases were uneventful. Median clinical follow up was 32 days (range 22 - 308) and median imaging follow up was 20 days (range 2 - 265), with no late deaths, no aortic re-interventions, and no aneurysmal dilatation of the non-stented TEAS treated segment. CONCLUSION: TEAS may be considered across acute, subacute, and chronic TBAD, including redo and connective tissue disease cases, enabling reproducible common lumen creation and landing zone optimisation. All complications were recognised and managed endovascularly and were observed only in non-acute dissections, although the sample size precluded meaningful assessment of any relationship between dissection phase and technical risk. These findings support TEAS as a feasible adjunct in carefully selected complex dissections, offer practical principles for safe adoption, and reflect an early experience that may be influenced by the learning curve of this technically demanding procedure.

title: Integrated Transcriptomic and Single-Cell Analyses Identify CCR2-Dependent Monocyte-Smooth Muscle Cell Crosstalk in Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Aortic aneurysm (AA) involves inflammatory recruitment and vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) remodeling, but the cellular contribution of candidate chemokine receptors remains unclear. We prioritized reproducible AA-associated genes, localized their cellular sources, and tested whether monocyte CCR2 influences human aortic smooth muscle cells (HASMCs). METHODS: Differentially expressed genes shared by GSE57691 and GSE7084 underwent enrichment, protein-protein interaction, regulatory-network, and drug-gene analyses. Hub genes were assessed in GSE9106 and localized in GSE166676 single-cell RNA-sequencing data. CCR2-silenced THP-1 monocytic cells were indirectly co-cultured with HASMCs. CCR2 knockdown was verified by quantitative PCR; HASMC remodeling-related proteins and 24-h scratch-wound closure were evaluated. RESULTS: p p p We identified 107 common upregulated genes and ten immune-related hubs. CCR2 was monocyte-enriched and higher in AA cells overall (= 0.00799) and AA monocytes (= 0.00440). THP-1 co-culture increased COL3A1 and SPP1, decreased α-SMA and TPM, and increased HASMC wound closure. CCR2 silencing partially reversed these changes and decreased wound closure versus siNC-THP-1 cells (< 0.01). CONCLUSIONS: Multi-omic evidence and non-contact co-culture support CCR2-dependent monocyte-HASMC paracrine crosstalk in AA-associated remodeling. The responsible mediators and in vivo relevance require further study.

title: Cardiovascular and mortality outcomes with JAK versus TNF inhibitors in rheumatoid arthritis: a target trial emulation (CARDINAL-RA).
abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aims to compare cardiovascular and mortality outcomes of Janus kinase inhibitors (JAKi) versus tumor necrosis factor inhibitors (TNFi) in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) at elevated cardiovascular risk using target trial emulation. METHODS: Within TriNetX, adults with RA aged ≥50 years and ≥1 cardiovascular risk factor initiating JAKi or TNFi were compared in a new-user, active-comparator design. Improved 1:1 propensity score matching incorporated demographics, cardiovascular risk factors, comorbidities, individual conventional synthetic DMARDs, oral corticosteroids, prior non-TNF biologic exposure, and baseline inflammatory markers. The primary outcome was MACE (nonfatal myocardial infarction or nonfatal ischemic stroke); the secondary outcomes were all-cause mortality, heart failure hospitalization, and venous thromboembolism (VTE), with cataract as a prespecified negative control. Follow-up began 90 days after initiation. Cox models estimated hazard ratios, with 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidences and absolute risk differences per 1,000. Cohorts were separately matched by agent, sex, cardiovascular-risk stratum, and index era; E-values quantified sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. RESULTS: p In 18,757 matched pairs, JAKi was not associated with excess MACE (HR 1.002, 0.923-1.088; +2.11 per 1,000). All-cause mortality, a secondary outcome, was higher with JAKi (HR 1.158, 1.058-1.268; = 0.0014; +10.4 per 1,000; E-value 1.586), whereas heart failure hospitalization (HR 1.019, 0.955-1.088) and VTE (HR 1.054, 0.961-1.156) did not differ; the negative control showed no excess (HR 0.934, 0.867-1.007). No agent showed a significant excess in MACE or mortality (mortality HR 1.052 tofacitinib, 1.213 baricitinib, and 1.090 upadacitinib); the only nominally significant agent-level finding was VTE with baricitinib (HR 1.364, 1.028-1.809; 198 events). A three-component composite including death was non-significant (HR 1.058, 0.992-1.127). No consistent effect modification was seen by sex, cardiovascular risk burden, or index year. CONCLUSION: JAKi initiation was not associated with excess MACE (primary outcome), heart failure hospitalization, or VTE. A modest excess in all-cause mortality was observed as a secondary outcome, with no signal for any individual agent. This association was of modest robustness (E-value 1.586) and was not reproduced in any agent-specific cohort, so residual channeling bias cannot be excluded. The null MACE result should not be read as class-wide cardiovascular safety reassurance nor the mortality signal as an established causal effect.

title: Reevaluating hypercoagulability in the portal vein and the impact of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt on platelet activation in cirrhosis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: In liver cirrhosis, dysregulated hemostasis predisposes patients to both hemorrhagic and thrombotic complications. The portal vein (PV) is a frequent site of thrombosis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Whether the PV constitutes a locally hypercoagulable environment remains controversial, as previous studies have reported conflicting findings regarding portal venous platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction, and coagulation factor alterations. METHODS: We enrolled 34 patients with liver cirrhosis undergoing transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) implantation. Platelet count, activation, and reactivity were assessed by flow cytometry before and after TIPS, as well as across multiple vascular compartments, including the PV, superior mesenteric vein, hepatic vein, and peripheral vein. In addition, we measured key coagulation factors involved in secondary hemostasis in the indicated vessels. RESULTS: Platelet counts declined with advancing liver disease, but no changes in platelet activation or reactivity were observed. Despite elevated platelet counts in the PV, we found no evidence of increased platelet activation or reactivity. Moreover, no compartment-specific differences were detected in the selected conventional coagulation parameters assessed, except for lower fibrinogen levels in the PV compared with the hepatic vein. TIPS implantation did not lead to a short-term increase in platelet activation. CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort, we found no evidence of increased portal venous platelet activation or reactivity. Apart from lower fibrinogen levels in the PV compared with the hepatic vein, the selected conventional coagulation parameters assessed did not show consistent compartment-specific differences. These findings do not support the concept of a PV-specific hypercoagulable state as assessed by the present platelet activation and reactivity measures and selected coagulation assays. Rather, they suggest that relief of portal hypertension and reduction of venous stasis may be more relevant for thrombosis risk than changes in platelet activation alone.

The portal vein (PV) is a frequent site of thrombosis, but the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Whether the PV constitutes a locally hypercoagulable environment remains controversial, as previous studies have reported conflicting findings regarding portal venous platelet activation, endothelial dysfunction, and coagulation factor alterations.

title: Treatment patterns and safety outcomes after splenectomy or thrombopoietin receptor agonists as second-line therapy for immune thrombocytopenia: Korean claims-based study.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Splenectomy and thrombopoietin receptor agonists (TPO-RAs) are recommended second-line therapies for immune thrombocytopenia. Although guidelines recommend tailoring second-line treatments to patient characteristics, this approach is often unclear in real-world practice. OBJECTIVES: We examined claims-based time to next treatment (TTNT) and safety outcomes after splenectomy or TPO-RA as a second-line therapy using nationally representative Korean claims data. METHODS: Patients diagnosed with immune thrombocytopenia between 2002 and 2021 were included. From the eligible cohort, we identified patients whose index second-line treatment was splenectomy (group 1) or TPO-RA without prior splenectomy (group 2). Propensity score matching was performed between patients in both groups who had received corticosteroids as first-line treatment. RESULTS: After matching, 447 group 1 and 57 group 2 patients were analyzed. Subsequent treatment was administered to 82.3% and 61.4% of patients in groups 1 and 2, respectively. Median TTNTs were 5.80 and 3.03 months in groups 1 and 2, respectively. Estimated TTNT curves diverged after 24 months, with a longer TTNT observed in the TPO-RA group. Pneumococcal infections occurred in 3.1% of patients in group 1 and none in group 2. Venous thromboembolism (VTE) occurred in 10.5% and 15.7% of patients in groups 1 and 2, respectively. The observed time to VTE was shorter in group 2 than in group 1. CONCLUSION: Patients treated with TPO-RAs as a second-line therapy showed a longer TTNT after 24 months, whereas VTE occurred earlier in the TPO-RA group. However, these findings should be interpreted with caution because of residual confounding.

Although guidelines recommend tailoring second-line treatments to patient characteristics, this approach is often unclear in real-world practice. OBJECTIVES: We examined claims-based time to next treatment (TTNT) and safety outcomes after splenectomy or TPO-RA as a second-line therapy using nationally representative Korean claims data.

title: Acute-on-Chronic Limb Ischemia Mimicking Cellulitis: A Diagnostic Pitfall.
abstract: Acute-on-chronic limb ischemia may present with clinical features that overlap with inflammatory conditions, potentially delaying recognition of arterial compromise. We report a case of an elderly woman with long-standing polycythemia treated with hydroxyurea who presented with progressive right foot pain, marked swelling, erythema, tenderness, and bluish discoloration of the hallux. She was discharged from the emergency department but returned the next night with worsening pain. Soft-tissue ultrasonography demonstrated diffuse subcutaneous edema without a localized collection, supporting an initial provisional diagnosis of cellulitis. Despite preserved motor function and sensation, progressive ischemic discoloration, prolonged capillary refill, and abnormal distal pulse findings prompted further vascular assessment. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) demonstrated a 6.2-cm right popliteal arterial thrombus with impaired distal perfusion. Her D-dimer was within the laboratory reference range at 0.40 µg/mL FEU, while the hematocrit was markedly elevated at 55.3%. Intravenous unfractionated heparin was initiated, resulting in improvement in pain and swelling and clinical stabilization, while definitive revascularization options were considered. The patient subsequently elected to pursue definitive treatment in her home country, precluding assessment of long-term limb-salvage outcomes. This case emphasizes the importance of careful and repeated vascular assessment in a painful, discolored limb, particularly before neuromotor deficits develop. Laboratory findings, including D-dimer, should be interpreted within their validated clinical context and should not supersede clinical evidence of impaired arterial perfusion.

We report a case of an elderly woman with long-standing polycythemia treated with hydroxyurea who presented with progressive right foot pain, marked swelling, erythema, tenderness, and bluish discoloration of the hallux. She was discharged from the emergency department but returned the next night with worsening pain.

title: Blue Toe Syndrome and Acute Kidney Injury Following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Biopsy-Proven Case of Cholesterol Embolization Syndrome.
abstract: Cholesterol embolization syndrome (CES) is an underrecognized complication of arterial instrumentation caused by embolization of atheromatous debris into small- and medium-sized arteries. Acute kidney injury (AKI) is well described after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), but biopsy-proven CES after TAVR is rarely reported. Its delayed presentation may be mistaken for contrast-associated nephropathy, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, or systemic vasculitis. A 77-year-old man with chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and peripheral artery disease underwent transfemoral TAVR for severe aortic stenosis. Preprocedural computed tomography angiography showed a "shaggy aorta." One month later, he developed intermittent, painless violaceous discoloration of the left first through third toes. Approximately 2.5 months after TAVR, serum creatinine had risen from a baseline of 1.2-1.5 mg/dL to 4.24 mg/dL, prompting admission. Microscopic hematuria, mild eosinophilia (0.64 ×10³/µL), elevated inflammatory markers, and dysmorphic erythrocytes raised concern for glomerulonephritis and vasculitis, and empiric intravenous methylprednisolone was given while diagnostic evaluation proceeded. Kidney biopsy demonstrated atheroembolic cholesterol clefts in intrarenal arteries with ischemic changes, without glomerulonephritis or immune complex deposition. Preserved pedal pulses with an ankle-brachial index of 1.21 and toe-brachial index of 0.98 supported distal microembolization rather than large-vessel occlusion. Corticosteroids were stopped, nephrotoxins withheld, aspirin resumed, and high-intensity statin therapy was initiated; creatinine improved to approximately 3.1 mg/dL by discharge. CES should remain in the differential for progressive AKI with blue toe syndrome after TAVR, even when presentation is delayed, and initial findings suggest immune-mediated disease.

Its delayed presentation may be mistaken for contrast-associated nephropathy, rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis, or systemic vasculitis.

title: Venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer: a comparison of primary cytoreductive surgery versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To compare the incidence and temporal distribution of venous thromboembolism in patients with distant-stage uterine cancer treated with primary cytoreductive surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy versus neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval cytoreductive surgery. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study used the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program-Medicare data to identify women aged ≥65 years with Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program Summary Stage distant uterine cancer diagnosed from 2008 to 2017 who underwent both hysterectomy and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Treatment was classified by the sequence of surgery and chemotherapy within 6 months of diagnosis. Venous thromboembolism, comprising pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis, was identified from claims. Patients with baseline venous thromboembolism (6 months before through the month of diagnosis) were excluded from the primary analysis. Cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was estimated using competing risk methods (death as a competing event) and compared via Gray's test. Multi-variable analysis evaluated factors associated with venous thromboembolism during the first 6 months after diagnosis, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and tumor characteristics. Landmark, time-varying treatment-phase, and first-treatment-anchored sensitivity analyses were performed to address immortal time and time-zero misalignment. RESULTS: Of 1977 patients, 186 (9.4%) had venous thromboembolism prior to diagnosis and were excluded, leaving 1791 patients for analysis: 74.7% underwent primary cytoreductive surgery and 25.3% received neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy use increased from 17.6% (2008) to 35.5% (2017). Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher baseline venous thromboembolism prevalence (14.7% vs 7.5%, p<.001) and comorbidity burden. Overall, 568 venous thromboembolism events occurred; cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 20.1% at 6 months, 33.6% at 24 months, and 49.3% at 60 months. Neoadjuvant chemotherapy patients had higher early cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence (23.0% vs 19.1% at 6 months; 40.8% vs 31.5% at 24 months), with convergence by 60 months (46.5% vs 49.2%; Gray's test p=.054). In multi-variable analysis, the adjusted risk ratio for early venous thromboembolism with neoadjuvant chemotherapy versus primary cytoreductive surgery was 1.21 (95% confidence interval 0.97-1.51), an imprecise estimate that does not exclude a clinically meaningful increase in early risk. CONCLUSIONS: Among older patients with distant-stage uterine cancer, venous thromboembolism was common, affecting approximately 1 in 5 patients within 6 months and nearly 1 in 2 within 5 years. The cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence did not differ significantly between primary cytoreductive surgery and neoadjuvant chemotherapy. Events occurred earlier in the neoadjuvant chemotherapy group, a pattern that may reflect baseline differences between the groups and differential ascertainment as much as treatment sequence. Our findings support the need for a prospective evaluation of treatment-phase-specific thromboprophylaxis.

title: Genetic Patterns in Familial Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm Disease.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: We examined familial patterns and phenotypes of thoracic aortic aneurysms and dissections (TAAD) in the 3746 patients currently populating our Yale Aortic Institute Database. METHODS: Patient charts and electronic medical records were retrospectively reviewed for the entire cohort. TAAD disease was categorized as syndromic (with extra-aortic manifestations) or non-syndromic (without) for each patient. Family patterns and whole exome sequencing results were assessed. Family history was considered 'proven' when a patient's relative(s) had an arterial aneurysm or dissection confirmed by an imaging study, surgical treatment, or postmortem examination. Family history was termed 'likely' when at least one relative suffered sudden death at ages ≤50 for males and ≤60 for females, and 'possible' with a history of sudden death at any age. RESULTS: p p p p Of the 3746 patients in the database, family history of aneurysm or dissection and connective tissue status was able to be determined for 3113 patients, divided into 109 (3.5%) syndromic and 3004 (96.5%) non-syndromic TAAD patients. Findings were as follows: (1) In the syndromic group, 46 (42.2%) patients had a 'proven' family history, 6 (5.5%) had a 'likely' family history, 4 (3.7%) had a 'possible' family history, and 18 (16.5%) had 'none'. For 35 patients (32.1%) their family history was unknown. (2) In the non-syndromic group, 587 (19.5%) patients had 'proven' family history, 147 (4.9%) had 'likely' family history, 210 (7.0%) had 'possible' family history and 1444 (48.1%) had no family history, thus representing sporadic TAAD. A total of 616 (20.5%) had an unknown family history. (3) There was a significant difference between the rate for 'proven' and 'none' family history between the syndromic and non-syndromic groups (42.2% vs. 19.5% and 16.5% vs. 48.1%, respectively;< 0.001). (4) Syndromic patients presented at a significantly younger age than non-syndromic or sporadic patients (41.2 vs. 63.3 or 63.6;< 0.001). (5) There was no significant difference in age of presentation between familial non-syndromic (patients with 'proven', 'likely', and 'possible' family history) and sporadic patients (63.3 vs. 63.6;= 0.64). (6) Overall, of the 3746 patients in the database, 631 patients (25 syndromic, 552 non-syndromic, and 54 with unknown status) underwent Whole Exome Sequencing (WES). Sequencing revealed 170 disease-causing or suspicious variants [13 pathogenic, 16 likely pathogenic, 7 not classified, and 134 Variants of Uncertain Significance (VUS)] found in the exomes of 141 (22.3%) patients (12 syndromic, 103 non-syndromic TAAD patients plus a remaining 26 of unknown connective tissue status). Seventy (49.6%) of these patients had a 'proven' family history. (7) Familial TAAD patients were more likely to find a variant in their WES result than patients without a family history (70 vs. 26;< 0.001). Recognition of these strong familial patterns, even in non-syndromic cases, encourages intensive investigation of family in order to save lives by detecting silent TAA disease. CONCLUSIONS: Our large-scale, clinical and sequencing-based study clearly demonstrates the strongly familial and genetically mediated nature of thoracic aortic disease. We vividly demonstrate and characterize this familial nature of TAAD, both clinically and by genetic sequencing. Our findings strongly support vigorous family investigation when a new patient is diagnosed with thoracic aortic aneurysm, as well as vigorous application of whole exome sequencing for these families.

title: Anatomical Predictors of Endovascular Technical Success in Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia: The Role of GLASS and Diabetes.
abstract: Background: Methods: Results: Conclusions: n n p p p p p p Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is associated with high rates of major adverse limb events and mortality, particularly in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM). The Global Limb Anatomic Staging System (GLASS) standardizes anatomical assessment and supports revascularization planning. This study evaluated the association of anatomical complexity and diabetes with immediate technical success after infrainguinal endovascular treatment.This single-center retrospective study included 136 patients undergoing infrainguinal endovascular procedures for CLTI between May 2021 and May 2023, stratified into diabetic (= 85) and non-diabetic (= 51) groups. Anatomical complexity was assessed using GLASS. Technical success was defined as restoration of inline flow to the foot. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed.Technical success was achieved in 74.3% of procedures, without significant differences between diabetic and non-diabetic patients (75.3% vs. 72.5%,= 0.723). Success declined progressively from 86.3% in GLASS stage I to 75.5% in stage II and 53.1% in stage III (= 0.003; trend= 0.001). In multivariable analysis, GLASS FP (femoropopliteal) grade ≥2 (adjusted OR 8.068, 95% CI 3.018-21.562;< 0.001) and tibioperoneal trunk occlusion (adjusted OR 4.874, 95% CI 1.271-18.687;= 0.021) were independently associated with technical failure, whereas diabetes was not. The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.820, 95% CI 0.744-0.897;< 0.001).Anatomical complexity was associated with immediate technical success in CLTI, whereas no independent association with diabetes was detected in this cohort. GLASS may provide clinically relevant preprocedural risk stratification and support endovascular planning.

title: The Venification of the Artery: Insights from Single-Cell Transcriptomics of a Porcine Arteriovenous Fistula Model.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The maturation of an autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) depends on the coordinated hemodynamic adaptation of the inflow artery and the outflow vein. While venous remodeling has been extensively studied, the mechanisms of arterial adaptation are poorly understood. We addressed this knowledge gap with the first temporal single-cell atlas of the porcine AVF model. METHODS: Six Yorkshire pigs underwent bilateral femoro-femoral AVF creation for tissue harvest at 2 and 21 days postoperatively or sham operation to collect native vessels after 2 days. Arteries and veins were analyzed by droplet-based single-cell RNA sequencing, histology, and immunohistochemistry. RESULTS: HEY2, HEYL CCN3, CCN5 DKK2, SFRP4 C3, C7, CFD All fistulas were patent, with flows reaching 1185.0 ± 170.6 mL/min despite mild to moderate neointima formation in the veins. Arteries and veins demonstrated >60% endothelial denudation and increased neovascularization. Arterial remodeling was characterized by a progressive increase in venous-like transcriptional features. Arteries presented a venous-like endothelial cell (EC) composition at 21 days postop and a temporal increase in venous-associated phenotypes of myofibroblasts and fibroblasts. In both vessels, the latter populations were the main bearers of mechanosensitive signatures at 2 days. Despite the temporal convergence in phenotypes, arteries and veins retained vessel-selective characteristics. Arterial ECs expressed high levels of nitric oxide synthase, whereas venous ECs were largely inflammatory. Arterial myofibroblasts and fibroblasts had higher expression of Notch signaling transducers () and cellular communication network factors (), while Wnt signaling regulators () and complement genes () were upregulated in veins. Anti-inflammatory macrophages increased in both vessels during remodeling, likely contributing to the maturation of the fistulas. CONCLUSION: These analyses challenge the traditional paradigm of exclusive vein arterialization and support a complementary process of arterial venification after anastomosis. Recognition of this underappreciated phenomenon may reshape our understanding of AVF biology and guide the discovery of both vascular-wide and vessel-selective anti-stenotic therapies.

While venous remodeling has been extensively studied, the mechanisms of arterial adaptation are poorly understood. We addressed this knowledge gap with the first temporal single-cell atlas of the porcine AVF model.
