title: One-year outcomes of percutaneous deep vein arterialization in the Dutch LimFlow registry.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Percutaneous deep vein arterialization (pDVA) offers a potential endovascular alternative for reducing the risk of major amputation in patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) who have no standard revascularization options "no-option" CLTI (NO-CLTI). METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months. Secondary outcomes included limb salvage, overall survival, patency, pain scores, wound healing, transcutaneous oxygen pressure, and quality of life (QoL). RESULTS: A total of 26 limbs of 23 patients with NO-CLTI (mean age, 64 ± 12 years; 20 men) were included, all classified as Rutherford category 5 and 17 (77.3%) as Wound Ischemia and foot Infection stage 4. Thirteen (53.8%) patients suffered from diabetes mellitus and six (21.7%) from renal insufficiency. Technical success was 100%. Amputation-free survival was 69.2%, limb salvage 80.8%, and overall survival 88.5% at 12 months. Primary patency, primary-assisted patency, and secondary patency rates at 12 months were 6.6%, 27.3%, and 35.7%, respectively. Reinterventions were performed to maintain patency in 85% of the limbs and 58% for maturation of the pDVA. Median time to wound healing was 6.9 months, with 73.4% healed at 12 months. Pain scores decreased significantly (P <.001) in 12 months. QoL improved from a mean of 37% to 68% on the VascuQoL-25, though these analyses were based on limited available data. CONCLUSIONS: pDVA in patients with NO-CLTI is safe and effective at 12 months, preventing major amputation and mortality in the majority of patients. QoL also appeared to improve following pDVA. These observations warrant confirmation in larger studies. CLINICAL RELEVANCE: This study strengthens existing evidence on the effectivity and safety of percutaneous deep vein arterialization using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical) in patients with "no-option" chronic limb-threatening ischemia. Our data demonstrated a 100% technical success rate and comparable amputation-free survival and limb salvage to other percutaneous deep vein arterialization studies. Notably, this prospective and well-phenotyped cohort uniquely incorporated patient-reported outcome measures, showing improvements in pain, transcutaneous oxygen pressure and quality of life.

METHODS: In this prospective, multicenter registry conducted in the Netherlands between May 2020 and June 2024, patients with NO-CLTI underwent pDVA using the LimFlow system (Inari Medical). The primary end point was amputation-free survival at 12 months.

title: Cardiovascular involvement in gram-negative bloodstream infection: Timing, phenotypes, and mechanisms.
abstract: Gram-negative bloodstream infection (GN-BSI) is associated with a heterogeneous spectrum of cardiovascular manifestations extending beyond the hemodynamic consequences of sepsis. Epidemiological evidence identifies a transient period of heightened cardiovascular vulnerability, with myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke clustering close to BSI onset, alongside myocardial dysfunction, arrhythmias, thrombotic complications, and direct vascular or endovascular infection. These phenotypes likely reflect different interactions between systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, immunothrombosis, underlying cardiovascular disease, and pathogen-specific factors. Persistent bacteremia, prosthetic cardiovascular material, vascular disease, and selected Gram-negative pathogens may identify settings warranting greater cardiovascular attention. However, current evidence remains limited by predominantly retrospective designs, heterogeneous outcome definitions, non-standardized cardiovascular assessment, and limited integration of microbiological and cardiovascular data. This review integrates clinical, epidemiological, and mechanistic evidence to define the timing, phenotypes, and mechanisms of cardiovascular involvement in GN-BSI and proposes a phenotype-driven framework for cardiovascular interpretation and future research.

Epidemiological evidence identifies a transient period of heightened cardiovascular vulnerability, with myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke clustering close to BSI onset, alongside myocardial dysfunction, arrhythmias, thrombotic complications, and direct vascular or endovascular infection. These phenotypes likely reflect different interactions between systemic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, immunothrombosis, underlying cardiovascular disease, and pathogen-specific factors.

title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion. METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: P P P P Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0];=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9];=0.03). CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

title: Reverse Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Complicated by Neurogenic Pulmonary Edema in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage: A Case Report.
abstract: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (TTC) is a recognized and potentially severe cardiac complication in patients with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Reverse TTC (rTTC), a rare variant characterized by basal hypokinesis with apical sparing, is infrequently reported in this setting. The coexistence of rTTC with neurogenic pulmonary edema has not been previously described and represents a complex neurocardiac interaction that can significantly worsen outcomes. We report the case of a previously healthy 30-year-old man who presented with high-grade aSAH secondary to rupture of an anterior communicating artery aneurysm. His course was complicated by neurogenic pulmonary edema, refractory hypoxemia, hemodynamic instability, and rTTC. Management required early airway protection, bronchoscopy, vasopressor support, and complex stent-assisted endovascular coiling. Echocardiography demonstrated reduced left ventricular ejection fraction with basal hypokinesis and apical sparing, consistent with rTTC. Careful hemodynamic management was essential to balance cerebral perfusion against myocardial dysfunction. With multidisciplinary critical care and structured rehabilitation, the patient achieved favorable neurological and functional recovery. This case highlights that rTTC in aSAH is not a benign condition and may be associated with increased morbidity when combined with neurogenic pulmonary edema due to massive catecholamine surge. Early recognition using bedside echocardiography, prompt aneurysm securing, and balanced hemodynamic support are critical for improving outcomes.

title: Single-cell landscape of lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity across type-stratified craniofacial lesions in polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.
abstract: BACKGROUND: GNAS Polyostotic fibrous dysplasia (POFD) is a mosaic skeletal disorder driven by somaticmutations that constitutively activate Gsα-cAMP signaling, producing fibro-osseous craniofacial deformities. POFD lesions are histologically classified into three subtypes-Type I (connective-tissue predominant), Type II (cancellous-bone predominant), and Type III (sclerotic-bone predominant)-yet the immune microenvironment across these categories remains undefined. This study aims to dissect lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity and inter-cellular communication networks among distinct POFD histological categories. METHODS: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing on maxillary lesion tissues from three age- and sex-matched POFD patients classified as Type I (n=1), Type II (n=1), and Type III (n=1). After stringent quality control, 24,567 cells (median 1,762 genes/cell) were integrated and clustered. Ligand-receptor interactions were inferred using CellChat. RESULTS: + + + + + LTB TXNIP FTH1 PABPC1 S100A8/9 CXCL8 CCL2/3/4 IL1B Four major lineages were resolved: mesenchyme, lymphoid, myeloid, endovascular. Lymphoid representation differed across subtypes (Type I 1.00%, Type II 5.10%, Type III 10.90%), whereas endovascular fractions showed an inverse pattern (Type I 25.10%, Type II 9.90%, Type III 4.50%). Sub-clustering identified five lymphoid and six myeloid subsets. CD4T cells were most abundant in Type I (51.10%) but less represented in Type II (36.50%) and Type III (29.30%). CD8T cells constituted 2.10%, 11.90%, and 11.20% across Types I-III, respectively; germinal-center (GC) B cells were undetectable in Type I, minor in Type II (~1.60%), and prominent in Type III (~29.20%). Among myeloid cells, M1 macrophages comprised 9.90% in Type I, 25.70% in Type II, and 15.30% in Type III; osteoclasts were abundant in Type I (35.40%) but scarce in Types II and III (<5%). Dendritic cells (DCs) were absent in Type I yet detectable in Type II (1.90%) and Type III (2.60%). Network-central genes included,,, andfor CD4and GC B cells, and,,, andfor M1 macrophages and monocytes. Inter-cellular communication networks differed markedly by subtype: Type I and II displayed relatively simple interactomes, whereas Type III exhibited densely interconnected signaling with strengthened M2 macrophage-monocyte, M2 macrophage-GC B cell (CXCL12-CXCR4, APP-CD74), and GC B cell-monocyte axes, alongside attenuated CD4T cell-GC B cell (CLEC2D-KLRB1, ADGRE5-CD55) and M1 macrophage-CD4T cell crosstalk. Pathway enrichment revealed subtype-specific activation of oxidative phosphorylation, NF-κB, and antigen-presentation cascades across lymphoid and myeloid compartments. CONCLUSIONS: This study provides the first single-cell immune atlas of POFD, delineating lymphoid and myeloid heterogeneity across three histological subtypes. The identified subtype-specific markers and inter-cellular communication architectures offer candidate biomarkers for diagnostic stratification and reveal potential immunomodulatory targets for this disfiguring bone disorder.

title: Analysis of real-world multicenter experience with the large-bore CLEANER-Vac Thrombectomy System: An analysis of 200 patients.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE), encompassing deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represents a significant clinical entity associated with elevated morbidity and mortality rates. Conventional therapeutic approaches, such as systemic anticoagulation and thrombolytic agents, frequently yield suboptimal thrombus resolution. Mechanical thrombectomy has introduced a paradigm shift, enabling expeditious thrombus extraction while mitigating the chronic outcomes of suboptimally treated VTE and sequelae inherent to fibrinolytic therapies. The CLEANER Vac Thrombectomy System (Argon Medical Devices) is designed for controlled percutaneous venous thrombectomy. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-world procedural efficacy, safety profile, and clinical utility of the CLEANER Vac system in a multicenter cohort comprising 200 patients presenting with symptomatic venous thrombus. METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter investigation included data from 200 patients who underwent intervention between October 2024 and January 2026 across 26 U.S. institutions. Eligible participants were adults aged ≥18 years with imaging-confirmed acute (<14 days) or subacute (14-28 days) VTE. Primary end points included thrombus clearance efficacy, segmented venous involvement, estimated blood loss, and intraprocedural adverse event incidence. RESULTS: The study cohort had a mean age of 64.5 (range, 25-90) years, with a gender distribution of 52% female (n = 104) and 48% male (n = 96). An average of 2.2 venous segments were treated per patient (range, 1-5). Mean preprocedure clot burden was 88.0%, which decreased to 10.5% postprocedure, culminating in a mean thrombus clearance of 88.0%. Overall, 76.0% of patients (n = 152) achieved ≥90% clot resolution. Adjunctive rotational maceration was used in 30% of cases, balloon venoplasty in 38%, and stent placement in 15%. Mean device utilization time was 8.0 minutes, with an average of 2.4 device passes per patient. Mean estimated blood loss was 320 (range, 50-750) mL. The overall complication rate was 2.4% (n = 5), consisting exclusively of minor access-site hematomas not attributed to the device. No serious adverse events were device-attributable within the 200-patient cohort. Procedures were predominantly classified as peripheral venous interventions (70%), with the remaining 30% encompassing alternative indications (eg, in-stent restenosis and transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt revisions). CONCLUSIONS: In this cohort of 200 patients, the CLEANER Vac system demonstrated high procedural efficacy (88.0% mean clot clearance, 76% achieving ≥90% resolution) and a favorable overall safety profile. The findings support the potential role of this system in enabling rapid, single-session VTE treatment with constrained hemorrhagic liability and morbidity compared with catheter-directed thrombolysis. Prospective, longitudinal studies are warranted to evaluate long-term outcomes and delineate optimal patient stratification.

title: Outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair for uncomplicated subacute type B aortic dissection in the IRAD registry.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for uncomplicated type B acute aortic dissection (TBAAD) remains controversial. Compared with best medical therapy (BMT), TEVAR has demonstrated benefits for aortic remodeling; however, this intervention has procedure-related risks. METHODS: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection database was queried from January 1996 to September 2023 for all uncomplicated TBAAD cases. Patients receiving TEVAR during the subacute phase (sTEVAR; 15-90 days) and BMT were included in this study. Baseline comorbidities were recorded. The primary outcome was survival at 4 years. The secondary outcomes included delayed aortic interventions, progression of aortic disease, new dissection, rehospitalization, rupture, and stroke. RESULTS: During the study period, 1373 patients with uncomplicated TBAAD were entered into the registry and had follow-up data available. In addition, 63 patients (4.6%) underwent sTEVAR, and 1310 (95.4%) received BMT. The 4-year survival rate was similar between the groups (sTEVAR 87% vs BMT 84%, P = .925). At 3 years, the sTEVAR group had higher rates of new dissection (13.9% vs 4.8%, P = .002), all within 1 year of TEVAR. Progression of dissection, aneurysmal degeneration, reintervention, rupture, stroke, and rehospitalization were comparable between the groups. CONCLUSIONS: Compared with BMT, sTEVAR led to similar survival rates. New dissection was higher in the sTEVAR group. TEVAR may have a role in uncomplicated subacute TBAAD, and further randomized trials are essential to identify which patients benefit from this intervention.

Compared with best medical therapy (BMT), TEVAR has demonstrated benefits for aortic remodeling; however, this intervention has procedure-related risks. METHODS: The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection database was queried from January 1996 to September 2023 for all uncomplicated TBAAD cases.

title: Intraportal Rupture of a Hepatic Hydatid Cyst Complicated by Arterioportal Fistula and Hepatic Artery Pseudoaneurysm.
abstract: A 71-year-old woman with known hepatic hydatid disease presented with fever, abdominal pain, vomiting, and jaundice. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) with MR cholangiopancreatography revealed rupture of a right hepatic hydatid cyst with intraportal hydatid dissemination associated with a hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm and an arterioportal fistula. The patient rapidly developed severe acute cholangitis with multiorgan failure. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) allowed extraction of the hydatid material and biliary stenting, followed by selective endovascular embolization of the hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm. Despite combined endoscopic and interventional management, the patient progressed to refractory multiorgan failure and died. The present case illustrates a rare and life-threatening vascular complication of hepatic hydatid disease, emphasizing the importance of early imaging diagnosis and multidisciplinary management. In the present case, simultaneous portal and arterial involvement was associated with an unfavorable outcome.

title: The Effectiveness of Autologous Platelet-Rich Plasma Topical Application Versus Injection in the Healing of Chronic Venous Ulcers.
abstract: Introduction Chronic venous leg ulcers (VLUs) are common lower-limb wounds associated with delayed healing, recurrence, pain, impaired mobility, reduced quality of life, and increased healthcare costs. Although compression therapy remains the standard treatment, many ulcers heal slowly or remain resistant, highlighting the need for effective adjunctive therapies. Autologous platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is rich in platelets and growth factors that promote angiogenesis, fibroblast proliferation, collagen synthesis, granulation tissue formation, and re-epithelialization, making it a promising regenerative therapy for chronic venous ulcers. However, existing evidence is limited due to small sample sizes, methodological heterogeneity, and variability in PRP preparation. Systematic reviews have therefore recommended well-designed prospective randomized trials to establish its efficacy and safety. Aims and objectives The study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of PRP topical application, PRP injection, and saline dressings in chronic VLUs, with the primary objective based on complete ulcer healing and percentage reduction in ulcer size, while assessing ulcer recurrence and early treatment-related complications constituted the secondary endpoints. Recurrence here is defined as re-appearance of the ulcer after its complete healing at the same site. Methodology This prospective randomized controlled trial was conducted over 18 months at JSS Medical College and Hospital, Mysuru, Karnataka, India. A total of 63 adults with chronic VLUs (>6 weeks) were randomly allocated into three groups: group A (topical PRP dressing), group B (local PRP injection), and group C (saline dressing). All patients received a standard four-layer compression therapy. Autologous PRP was prepared using a double-spin centrifugation technique and administered weekly for four weeks. Patients were followed for six months. Primary outcomes included complete ulcer healing and percentage reduction in ulcer area, while recurrence and treatment-related complications were assessed as secondary outcomes using SPSS Version 28 (p < 0.05). Results Baseline comparability was noted among groups for age, sex, BMI, HbA1c, platelet count, ankle-brachial pressure index, ulcer duration, and initial ulcer area. At six weeks, complete healing of the ulcer was much greater in group B (33.3%) than in group A (9.5%) and group C (0%) (p = 0.0064). At three months, the mean ulcer area was minimal in group B (1.30 ± 1.61 cm²) compared to group A (3.15 ± 3.01 cm²) and group C (6.19 ± 4.49 cm²) (p < 0.0001). The percentage reduction in ulcer area at three months was highest in group B (91.80 ± 8.05%), followed by group A (78.29 ± 17.68%) and group C (62.34 ± 19.06%). The mean healing duration was the shortest in group B (11.20 ± 2.18 weeks) (p = 0.0001). The rates of recurrence and complications were minimal and similar. Conclusion Autologous PRP is a safe and effective adjunct for chronic VLUs. Both PRP topical application and injection improved healing compared with saline dressing, while PRP injection achieved earlier healing, greater ulcer area reduction, and shorter healing time, making it the preferred PRP delivery method.

title: Perioperative Predictors and Temporal Trajectories of Postoperative Cognitive Decline After Carotid Endarterectomy: A Prospective Cohort Study.
abstract: BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Carotid artery stenosis is a well-established risk factor for vascular cognitive impairment. Although carotid endarterectomy (CEA) reduces the risk of ischemic stroke, its effect on cognitive function remains uncertain. Most previous studies have relied on mean changes in cognitive scores and have not defined postoperative cognitive decline using patient-level thresholds for the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA). Moreover, few studies have integrated perioperative variables across baseline, intraoperative, and postoperative domains to examine heterogeneity in cognitive outcomes. We therefore defined postoperative cognitive decline using threshold-based MoCA changes and prospectively evaluated perioperative factors associated with distinct cognitive outcomes after CEA. METHODS: We prospectively enrolled older patients undergoing elective CEA under general anesthesia. Of 183 patients screened, 162 were ultimately enrolled and analyzed. All patients were managed according to standardized anesthetic and surgical protocols. Preoperative clinical, laboratory, and imaging variables, intraoperative hemodynamic parameters, and postoperative clinical indicators were collected. The primary outcome was cognitive decline at discharge, defined as a decrease of ≥2 points from baseline in the MoCA score. The secondary outcome was cognitive decline at 30 days, defined as a ≥3-point decrease in the telephone MoCA (t-MoCA) score relative to the corresponding baseline domains. RESULTS: Among the 162 enrolled patients, preoperative triglyceride level, preoperative cerebral hypoperfusion volume, surgical laterality, intraoperative mean arterial pressure (MAP) decline, and visual analogue scale (VAS) on postoperative day 1 were independently associated with early postoperative cognitive decline. A prediction model incorporating these five factors achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.752 (95% CI: 0.670-0.835) for cognitive decline before discharge. For 30-day cognitive decline, the model demonstrated an AUC of 0.717 (95% CI: 0.606-0.828). All patients with complete 30-day follow-up were stratified into four cognitive trajectory subtypes, and their longitudinal cognitive changes were visualized using a Sankey diagram. CONCLUSIONS: A perioperative model incorporating metabolic, cerebral perfusion, surgical, hemodynamic, and pain-related variables may help identify patients at increased risk of cognitive decline after CEA. The trajectory analysis further reveals heterogeneous postoperative cognitive patterns, including transient, delayed, and persistent decline. These findings support individualized perioperative risk assessment and structured cognitive follow-up. However, no internal or external validation was performed, and further testing is required in larger multicenter cohorts.

title: Incidence, timing, severity, and predictors of venous thromboembolism after open abdominal wall reconstruction.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolic events, including deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, represent serious and potentially preventable complications following open abdominal wall reconstruction. This study aimed to determine the incidence and predictors of venous thromboembolic events after open abdominal wall reconstruction. METHODS: A single-institution prospectively maintained database was queried for open abdominal wall reconstruction (2010-2025). Standard statistical analyses and multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of venous thromboembolic events. RESULTS: 2 2 Among 2,907 open abdominal wall reconstructions, 49 venous thromboembolic events (1.7%) occurred: 31 pulmonary embolisms ± deep vein thrombosis and 18 deep vein thromboses alone. Average body mass index was 34.6 ± 10.0 kg/m, and 18.4% had prior venous thromboembolic events. Preoperative chemoprophylaxis was administered in 77.6% of venous thromboembolic event cases, and 93.8% of patients who received postoperative chemoprophylaxis had no interruption. Compared with patients without venous thromboembolic events, those with venous thromboembolic events had larger defect sizes (314.5 ± 222.7 vs 199.8 ± 187.5 cm; P < .001) and longer operative times (233.4 ± 74.9 vs 187.2 ± 84.4 minutes; P < .001). Among 29 classified pulmonary embolisms, 13 were nonmassive, 12 submassive, and 4 massive/fatal. Advanced interventions were required in 12.2%, 16.3% required transfusion, and 16.3% underwent inferior vena cava filter placement. Among venous thromboembolic event patients, 40.8% required intensive care unit transfer, with 20.4% requiring reintubation. Average length of stay was longer in venous thromboembolic event patients (11.4 ± 9.8 vs 5.7 ± 8.8 days; P < .001). Multivariable regression identified body mass index (odds ratio, 1.09; 95% confidence interval, 1.04, 1.14; P < .001), prior venous thromboembolic events (odds ratio, 4.51; 95% confidence interval, 1.91, 10.62; P < .001), and operative time (odds ratio, 1.005; 95% confidence interval, 1.001, 1.010; P = .008) as independent predictors of venous thromboembolic event. CONCLUSION: Postoperative venous thromboembolic event following open abdominal wall reconstruction is uncommon but associated with significant morbidity and mortality. Higher body mass index, prior venous thromboembolic event, and longer operative time independently predicted venous thromboembolic event, highlighting the need for improved risk stratification and prevention strategies.

title: Balloon Landmark-Assisted Re-entry Using a Re-entry Catheter for Femoropopliteal Chronic Total Occlusion: A Case Report.
abstract: Re-entry catheters are effective devices for achieving true lumen re-entry during endovascular therapy (EVT) for femoropopliteal chronic total occlusion (FP-CTO). However, accurate orientation of the catheter may be difficult when angiographic visualization of the target lumen is inadequate. We report a case of successful revascularization using an inflated balloon as a fluoroscopic landmark to facilitate re-entry catheter orientation. An 81-year-old man presented with symptomatic left lower extremity ischemia caused by FP-CTO. Two previous EVT procedures had failed because guidewire re-entry into the true lumen could not be achieved after subintimal passage. During the third EVT, the retrograde guidewire remained within the true lumen, whereas the antegrade guidewire advanced within the subintimal space. Because angiographic localization of the re-entry point was difficult, a 5 mm balloon was inflated within the subintimal space and used as a fluoroscopic landmark to determine the orientation of the re-entry catheter. After balloon deflation, the re-entry cannula was advanced from the true lumen toward the subintimal space, enabling successful guidewire passage and subsequent stent implantation. The procedure was completed using only 25 mL of contrast medium. The patient's symptoms resolved, and the ankle-brachial index improved from 0.64 to 1.08. This case suggests that an inflated balloon may serve as a useful fluoroscopic landmark for re-entry catheter orientation when conventional angiographic localization is difficult. In this case, the technique facilitated re-entry catheter orientation and successful guidewire crossing despite limited angiographic visualization. Its potential contribution to contrast minimization, particularly in patients with impaired renal function, requires further evaluation.

We report a case of successful revascularization using an inflated balloon as a fluoroscopic landmark to facilitate re-entry catheter orientation.

title: Feasibility and Clinical Outcomes of a 6-Month Home-Based Telerehabilitation Program in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Disease: A Prospective Single-Arm Study.
abstract: p p p p (1) Background: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity and functional impairment. This study evaluated the feasibility and adherence of a 6-month home-based telerehabilitation (TR) program and longitudinal changes in functional capacity, health-related quality of life (HRQoL), and selected cardiometabolic parameters. (2) Methods: This prospective, single-arm study enrolled 42 patients with PAD. Daily ambulation was monitored using a Xiaomi Smart Band 8, and participants received weekly telephone counseling. Assessments were performed at baseline, 3 months, and 6 months. (3) Results: Median daily step count increased from 5868 to 6905 steps/day (< 0.001), whereas attainment of progressively increasing weekly targets decreased from 58.33% to 16.66% (< 0.001). Median 6 min walk test (6MWT) distance increased from 390 m to 445 m at 6 months, a 55 m increase (= 0.001). HRQoL, systolic blood pressure, body mass index, and total cholesterol showed significant longitudinal changes, while resting ankle-brachial index and selected cardiopulmonary exercise testing parameters remained relatively stable (> 0.05). (4) Conclusions: The TR program was feasible and accompanied by increased activity and improved walking capacity. The divergence between absolute activity and target attainment supports multidimensional adherence assessment. Causal effects cannot be established given the single-arm design.

title: Endovascular Recanalization of Non-Acute Vertebrobasilar Occlusion in Progressive Posterior Circulation Ischemia: A Case Report.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Unlike acute basilar artery occlusion, non-acute vertebrobasilar occlusion has limited evidence for intervention and requires individualized risk assessment. CASE PRESENTATION: A 62-year-old woman developed progressive vertigo, diplopia, dysarthria, and gait ataxia over ten days. Dual antiplatelet therapy was started after posterior circulation ischemia was suspected, but symptoms continued to progress. MRI showed acute to subacute left cerebellar infarction, and CTA showed absent antegrade basilar opacification with collateral distal filling. DSA showed distal left vertebral artery occlusion, retrograde basilar filling through posterior communicating artery collaterals, and hypoplastic right vertebral artery. Endovascular recanalization was performed after multidisciplinary review and informed consent. Intraluminal crossing, stepwise angioplasty, and stent reconstruction restored antegrade basilar flow without angiographic complications. NIHSS improved from 5 to 2 at discharge, and mRS was 1 at 30 days. No follow-up vascular imaging was available. CONCLUSIONS: This case illustrates technical feasibility in selected non-acute vertebrobasilar occlusion, but does not establish medical treatment failure, causal recovery, generalizable safety, or long-term durability.

title: The Current State of Digital Variance Angiography: A Literature Review.
abstract: Digital variance angiography (DVA), also referred to as kinetic imaging angiography, is an imaging technique that enhances vascular visualization by analyzing contrast flow motion. Although digital subtraction angiography (DSA) remains the current standard of care, DVA has demonstrated potential improvements in image quality and reductions in both radiation exposure and contrast use. This literature review aimed to evaluate currently available literature focusing on the use of DVA during angiographic procedures. The review was conducted using PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science, with the process being reflected in a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) flowchart. Across multiple clinical applications, DVA consistently demonstrated higher objective image quality metrics including contrast-to-noise ratio (CNR) and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) as compared with DSA. Several studies reported that expert reviewers observed improved subjective image quality and substantial reductions in radiation exposure. In addition, DVA has also been shown to facilitate reduced use of contrast, potentially decreasing contrast-related complications and healthcare costs. Collectively, current evidence suggests that DVA represents a promising advancement in angiographic imaging, with the potential to deliver superior image quality with reduced radiation exposure and contrast use.

title: Long-Term Cardiovascular, Thromboembolic, and Malignancy Safety of Janus Kinase (JAK) Inhibitors in Dermatologic and Rheumatologic Populations: A Narrative Comparative Review.
abstract: Janus kinase inhibitors are increasingly used in dermatology and rheumatology, but concerns about cardiovascular events, thromboembolism, and malignancy continue to influence long-term treatment decisions. This narrative comparative review examines evidence from randomized trials, integrated safety analyses, long-term extensions, selected observational studies, and regulatory sources, focusing on rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, atopic dermatitis, and alopecia areata. Topical agents and selective tyrosine kinase 2 inhibition are considered separately because of important differences in systemic exposure and pharmacology. The original, informally assembled evidence base was supplemented by a targeted literature update. ORAL Surveillance identified an important safety signal for tofacitinib compared with tumor necrosis factor inhibitors in patients with rheumatoid arthritis and cardiovascular risk factors. Long-term dermatology studies have generally reported low absolute event rates, although younger study populations, restrictive eligibility criteria, limited long-term comparator data, and treatment discontinuation affect how these findings should be interpreted. Observational studies in dermatology have produced mixed results, including thromboembolic associations that warrant further investigation. Psoriatic arthritis provides additional evidence across the clinical boundaries of both specialties. Differences in patient populations, study design, outcome definitions, and statistical measures limit direct comparisons across studies. Treatment decisions should follow indication-specific prescribing requirements and consider cardiovascular disease, prior thrombosis, smoking, age, malignancy history, and available alternatives. Additional long-term comparative studies are needed to better distinguish patient-, disease-, and treatment-related risks.

title: Anticoagulation Dilemma in a Patient With Pulmonary Embolism and Massive Haemoptysis.
abstract: The development of worsening haemoptysis in a patient with pulmonary embolism presents a significant treatment challenge, especially in a low-resource setting where advanced interventions such as bronchial artery embolization may not be readily available. We present the case of a 40-year-old morbidly obese woman who was transferred to our facility with recurrent lower-limb deep vein thrombosis and a new diagnosis of bilateral pulmonary embolism. Following initiation of oral anticoagulation with apixaban, she developed worsening haemoptysis that persisted despite dose adjustments. She was subsequently stabilized and discharged on a vitamin K antagonist (warfarin). This case highlights the clinical challenges encountered in managing anticoagulation in the setting of significant bleeding and underscores the importance of individualized anticoagulation therapies.

title: Chronic Venous Disease as a Prognostic Factor for Venous Thromboembolism: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: This systematic review aimed to evaluate chronic venous disease as a prognostic factor for subsequent venous thromboembolism. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science were systematically searched. REVIEW METHODS: This systematic review was conducted according to Cochrane Prognosis Methods Group guidance and reported in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. The primary outcome was venous thromboembolism, defined as deep vein thrombosis and/or pulmonary embolism. Certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) framework. RESULTS: 2 2 2 2 Seven longitudinal, prognostic factor studies including 3 760 257 participants were included, of whom 702 325 had chronic venous disease and 3 057 932 served as controls. Six studies evaluated varicose veins, whereas one more broadly evaluated chronic venous disease. Pooled unadjusted analysis identified an increased risk of venous thromboembolism (risk ratio [RR] 2.25, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.09 - 2.43, I= 0%; p = .83, moderate certainty of evidence) and deep vein thrombosis (RR 5.23, 95% CI 4.92 - 5.56, I= 64.6%; p = .059, moderate certainty of evidence) among chronic venous disease individuals compared with controls. Crude time to event analysis replicated these findings, demonstrating an increased venous thromboembolism hazard among the chronic venous disease group (hazard ratio [HR] 2.52, 95% CI 1.88 - 3.37, I= 0%; p = .80, moderate certainty of evidence). However, in the adjusted time to event analysis, which included two studies comprising 2 320 327 participants, the association was attenuated and fell marginally short of statistical significance (adjusted HR 1.76, 95% CI 0.97 - 3.19, I= 74.0%; p = .050, very low certainty of evidence). CONCLUSIONS: Although the available evidence, predominantly derived from studies evaluating varicose veins, consistently indicated higher unadjusted venous thromboembolism estimates among chronic venous disease individuals, adjusted prognostic data were limited and heterogeneous, resulting in very low certainty. Chronic venous disease may represent a clinically relevant marker of subsequent venous thromboembolism, but the magnitude and independence of this prognostic effect remain uncertain, highlighting the need for adequately adjusted longitudinal studies.

title: Mechanical Characterization and Ex Vivo Evaluation of a Novel Constraining Device for Safe Endovascular Endograft Explantation.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Open surgical conversion after endovascular aortic repair is morbid and performed without disease-specific instruments. We evaluated the feasibility, and mechanical characteristics of the EVAx, a novel single-use device designed to disengage, collapse, and constrain suprarenal aortic fixation barbs during open endograft explantation. METHODS: Slide and constrainment testing were performed across 5 endograft configurations spanning 3 platforms: Endurant II (25, 36 mm) (Medtronic), Treo (28 mm) (Terumo), and Zenith (28, 36 mm) (Cook). Endografts were embedded in a silicone aortic model (25 mm inner diameter), and 3 operators each performed 5 trials per configuration (n = 150). The EVAx was compared with the modified syringe technique in bovine aortic specimens across 3 operators, with the primary objective of evaluating macroscopic intimal injury after aortic endograft explant. Additionally, constraining arms underwent uniaxial compression to failure on an Instron load frame in intended- and reverse-loading orientations. RESULTS: The EVAx successfully advanced over the Endurant and Treo platforms in all trials (100%) and the Zenith platform in 90%, with the 36-mm Zenith showing the lowest slide success (80%). Constrainment success was 100% for the Endurant 36 mm and Treo, 80% for the Endurant 25 mm, and 80% and 47% for the Zenith 28 mm and 36 mm. The EVAx produced no macroscopic intimal injury across all operators, whereas one specimen removed with a syringe showed barb puncture sites. Constraining arms failed at a peak force of 25 N. CONCLUSION: The EVAx demonstrates early feasibility in ex vivo testing for safe suprarenal endograft constrainment, with reproducible benchtop performance and reduced aortic wall trauma compared with the modified syringe technique. These results offer promise of reduced aortic wall trauma utilizing the EVAx, a disease-specific device for endograft removal.

title: [Effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement].
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the effects of digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation on clinical outcomes in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). This study has been registered with the U.S. National Library of Medicine Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier NCT02803294. METHODS: Data from 1012 patients who underwent TAVR at the Second Affiliated Hospital, Zhejiang University School of Medicine, between March 2013 and January 2023 were retrospectively analyzed. Patients receiving conventional rehabilitation were assigned to the control group, whereas those receiving a digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation program, comprising preoperative screening and functional preparation, intraoperative eligibility assessment, postoperative stepwise rehabilitation management, and intelligent home-based rehabilitation, were assigned to the observation group. Propensity score matching was performed to adjust for baseline confounding. Postoperative intensive care unit (ICU) stay and hospital stay, the incidence of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR, and functional outcomes, including the five-meter walking test, six-minute walking test, and Katz index, were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: vs P vs P P P After propensity score matching, 251 patients were included in each group. Compared with the control group, the observation group had shorter postoperative ICU stays [0 (0, 1) h. 0 (0, 0) h,<0.01] and postoperative hospital stays [8 (7, 11) d. 3 (1, 7) d,<0.01]. No apparent increase in the incidence of adverse events was observed in the observation group at 30 days, 1 year, or 2 years after TAVR. The time required to complete the five-meter walking test was shorter in the observation group than in the control group at 30 days, 1 year, and 2 years after TAVR (all<0.01). Results of six-minute walking test and Katz index showed no significant differences between the groups (both>0.05). CONCLUSIONS: Digital-driven cardiac rehabilitation may shorten hospital stay and improve selected functional outcomes in patients undergoing TAVR without increase in postoperative cardiovascular and cerebrovascular adverse events.

title: What Preclinical Medical Students Value When Choosing a Surgical Career: A Cluster Analysis.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Understanding what students value when choosing a surgical career and whether early exposure changes them is crucial for effective recruitment. This study used a prospective preclinical surgical skills course to evaluate specialty choice factors and determine whether improved skills influence them or interest in the sponsoring specialty. METHODS: Forty-seven preclinical medical students enrolled in an 8-wk vascular surgery-sponsored elective skills course. Students completed standardized precourse and postcourse surveys assessing interest in surgery and the sponsoring specialty, confidence in surgical abilities, perceptions of surgery, and eleven specialty choice factors. K-means cluster analysis identified groups of factors by importance. Surgical performance was assessed using knot tying and suturing metrics. Normally distributed variables were compared using paired t-tests; non-normal and Likert scale variables using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. RESULTS: Students significantly improved across all skills metrics. Median attending-rated competency scores improved from 1 to 4/5 for knot tying and suturing (both P < 0.001). Interest in the sponsoring specialty did not change and remained lower than interest in surgery overall (P < 0.01). K-means clustering identified a high-importance cluster comprising personality fit, early specialty exposure, attending lifestyle, mentorship, attending workload, and income potential, and a low-importance cluster comprising residency-related factors including training length, research years, competitiveness, resident lifestyle, and resident workload. The only factor that changed postcourse was early exposure (P = 0.010). CONCLUSIONS: Preclinical students prioritize attending-level factors and early exposure over residency-related factors when choosing a specialty. Despite significant skill improvement, interest in the sponsoring specialty did not increase. Recruitment efforts should prioritize mentorship, early exposure, and attending lifestyle-not skills training alone.

title: Associations Between miR-145, TGF-β Signaling, and Aortic Wall Remodeling in Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
abstract: Background/purpose: Methods Results Conclusions p Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is characterized by pathological remodeling of the aortic wall, involving vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) dysfunction, extracellular matrix degradation, and alterations in signaling pathways. MicroRNA-145 (miR-145) is involved in the regulation of VSMC phenotype, whereas transforming growth factor-beta (TGF-β) signaling has context-dependent effects on vascular remodeling. This study used a dataset to explore potential associations between miR-145 expression, TGF-β/SMAD signaling, VSMC phenotypic characteristics, and structural features of the aortic wall.: Aortic tissue samples were obtained from 324 patients with AAA during aneurysm-related surgical treatment. Control tissues were collected from macroscopically healthy aortic segments of 324 subjects undergoing elective cardiothoracic or vascular surgery. Tissue samples were analyzed for miR-145 expression, TGF-β signaling, vascular smooth muscle cell markers, and histopathological characteristics of aortic wall remodeling.: miR-145 was significantly downregulated in AAA tissue compared to control. RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry revealed increased TGF-β1/TGFBR signaling, SMAD2/3 activation, and KLF4 expression, accompanied by reduced expression of the VSMC contractile genes ACTA2, TAGLN, and MYH11, in AAA tissue. The lower expression level of miR-145 correlated significantly with TGF-β/SMAD pathway activation, VSMC phenotypic switching, more pronounced medial degeneration and elastic-fiber fragmentation, and increased aortic diameter (< 0.001).: Lower miR-145 expression was associated with TGF-β/SMAD pathway-related activity, altered VSMC phenotype, and structural remodeling of the aortic wall in AAA tissue. These findings identify a potential association between miR-145 dysregulation and TGF-β-associated vascular remodeling; however, they do not establish a direct functional signaling axis or causal relationship. Further mechanistic studies are required to clarify the underlying molecular interactions.

title: Scapulothoracic Disarticulation of the Right Upper Limb After a Car-to-Obstacle Collision: A Case Report.
abstract: This report details the case of a 26-year-old man, victim of a car-to-barrier collision followed by a rollover. The patient, found conscious, was intubated by the pre-hospital team and admitted in severe hypovolemic shock, with extensive injury to the shoulder and right upper limb. After hemodynamic stabilization, the team performed bilateral chest drainage, a massive transfusion protocol, and a forequarter amputation of the right upper limb with ligation of the subclavian vessels, in a joint procedure by the orthopedic and vascular surgery teams. Postoperatively, he remained in the intensive care unit (ICU), developing ventilator-associated pneumonia, treated with meropenem and vancomycin. After 10 days, the patient was transferred to a ward. He was discharged from the hospital after 15 days of hospitalization and continued with outpatient follow-up, where he presented with phantom limb pain initially treated with gabapentin and controlled with physiotherapy. In the end, he was definitively discharged with good healing, pain improvement, and favorable clinical evolution.

title: Hybrid management of primary aortic mural thrombus with mesenteric embolization.
abstract: Primary aortic mural thrombus with visceral embolization is a rare and life-threatening condition without an established treatment strategy. We report the case of a 40-year-old woman with thoracoabdominal primary aortic mural thrombus and embolization to the superior mesenteric and common hepatic arteries. She was treated using a hybrid approach consisting of large-bore aspiration thrombectomy with the Symphony Thrombectomy System (Imperative Care, Inc), temporary aortic flow control using a trilobed occlusion balloon, intravascular ultrasound-guided thoracic endovascular aortic repair, and selective conversion to open superior mesenteric artery thrombectomy with patch angioplasty. The patient recovered without bowel resection or distal embolic complications, demonstrating the feasibility of this staged hybrid strategy.

She was treated using a hybrid approach consisting of large-bore aspiration thrombectomy with the Symphony Thrombectomy System (Imperative Care, Inc), temporary aortic flow control using a trilobed occlusion balloon, intravascular ultrasound-guided thoracic endovascular aortic repair, and selective conversion to open superior mesenteric artery thrombectomy with patch angioplasty.

title: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae RkMsn4, a zinc finger transcription factor, regulates carotenoid and lipid metabolism to enhance tolerance to environmental stress in.
abstract: Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Rhodosporidium kratochvilovae Red yeasts serve as indispensable microbial resources for the production of carotenoids and lipids; however, environmental stress factors often limit their performance during industrial fermentation. The zinc-finger transcription factors Msn2/Msn4 act as central regulators of stress responses in yeasts. However, researchers have not yet systematically elucidated the similarities and differences in the mechanisms underlying the regulatory effects of Msn2/Msn4 under different stress conditions. In this study, we compared the shared and stress-specific regulatory functions of RkMsn4 inYM25235 under conditions of glucose starvation, 15 °C low temperature, and 4% NaCl salt stress. RkMsn4 contributed to the activity of the oxidative defense systems, including antioxidant enzymes, carotenoids, and glutathione, and the remodeling of membrane lipids, including phospholipids and unsaturated fatty acids (UFAs) across all three stress conditions. Additionally, RkMsn4 regulated stress-specific metabolic regulation by modulating branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) and aromatic amino acid (AAA) metabolism under glucose starvation conditions and promoting the utilization of exogenous sucrose and fructose under salt stress. By conducting weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), we identified candidate genes potentially associated with carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide practical insights for improving tolerance to stress and metabolic productivity of red yeasts in industrial bioprocesses.IMPORTANCERed yeasts are important microorganisms for the production of carotenoids and lipids, but their performance is often limited by environmental stress. Understanding how red yeasts respond to environmental stress is crucial for advancing their application in industrial fermentation. This study reveals the stress response mechanisms mediated by the transcription factor RkMsn4 inYM25235 under glucose starvation, low temperature, and salt stress, as well as its regulatory role in carotenoid and lipid metabolism. These findings provide valuable insights for enhancing the stress resistance and productivity of red yeasts in industrial applications.

title: Venous Thromboembolism in Severe Renal Insufficiency: 20 Years of Contemporary Management and Clinical Outcomes.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients with severe renal insufficiency have been systematically excluded from randomized trials of anticoagulation for venous thromboembolism (VTE), leaving uncertainty regarding their management in clinical practice. OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this study was to describe the clinical profile, temporal trends in management, and phase-specific outcomes of patients with acute VTE and severe renal insufficiency. METHODS: We analyzed 5,763 patients with acute VTE and creatinine clearance < 30 mL/min enrolled in Registro Informatizado de Enfermedad TromboEmbólica (2005-2024). Baseline characteristics, anticoagulant strategies, and 90-day outcomes were evaluated across 4 calendar periods and during the early (days 0-10) and late (days 11-90) treatment phases. RESULTS: Mean age was 81 years; 69% were women, 56% presented with pulmonary embolism (PE), 16% had creatinine clearance <15 mL/min, and 3.6% were receiving hemodialysis. Over time, severe renal dysfunction and hemodialysis became more frequent. Initial treatment remained predominantly low-molecular-weight heparin, whereas vitamin K antagonist use declined and direct oral anticoagulant use increased. At 90 days, recurrent VTE occurred in 1.3% of patients, major bleeding in 5.1%, and 20% died. During the first 10 days, fatal PE exceeded fatal bleeding (2.0% vs 0.3%), whereas during days 11 to 90 fatal bleeding exceeded fatal PE (0.7% vs 0.3%). CONCLUSIONS: Patients with VTE and severe renal insufficiency are elderly, medically complex, and experience high short-term mortality. The relative balance between fatal PE and fatal bleeding changes over time, with fatal PE predominating early and fatal bleeding thereafter, while real-world management frequently differs from product labels and guideline recommendations.

title: Working toward the future of transcatheter aortic valve replacement: integrating computational modeling with patient-specific clinical care.
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is rapidly evolving to become the standard of care for aortic stenosis (AS) patients, as opposed to open-heart surgery. The emergence of new commercial TAVR devices, as well as technological advancements in AS diagnosis and procedural planning, combat post-TAVR complications but pose new challenges with patient selection and optimal timing of valve replacement. Computational modeling is a powerful tool that may help streamline solutions for heart teams facing these complexities. AREAS COVERED: This narrative review outlines the evolving landscape of TAVR patients - with a primary focus on AS - and examines the paradigm shift toward computational modeling in diagnostics, procedural planning, and intraoperative guidance. Mechanistic and AI-accelerated modeling studies were identified via PubMed, with publication dates ranging from January 2016-April 2026, while additional sources were identified without a publication date constraint. EXPERT OPINION: TAVR indications and available devices will continue to increase. Improved device durability is increasingly necessary as the mean age of TAVR patients decreases and life expectancy increases. Emerging computational techniques, such as radiomics and AI/ML tools to enhance standard imaging modalities, hold promise in identifying who and when to treat for AS or AR. Digital twins may facilitate TAVR planning and optimal treatment pathways for individual patients.

title: Modified DrySeal Sheath U-turn Technique with Sheath Escalation and a Triple Coaxial System for Complex Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis Placement: A Retrospective Cohort.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Standard Gore Excluder Iliac Branch Endoprosthesis (IBE) placement precedes endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) main body deployment. This sequence is unavailable after previous EVAR and may be unsuitable with short common iliac arteries or a limited renal to internal iliac artery (IIA) distance. The original ipsilateral U-turn technique enables post main body IBE placement by redirecting a 12 F sheath towards the IIA through the same femoral access. Limited working space within the sheath and wire device interaction may impede delivery. This paper describes two modifications intended to address these delivery limitations: U-turn sheath escalation to ≥ 14 F (modification 1) and a 20/16/12 F triple coaxial sheath system (TCSS). Procedural feasibility and early outcomes for the original and modified U-turn techniques are reported. METHODS: Consecutive limbs treated at one centre with the original or modified U-turn technique between December 2023 and December 2025 were reviewed retrospectively; outcomes were summarised descriptively. RESULTS: The technique was used in 46 limbs of 34 patients: 37 during initial EVAR and nine after previous EVAR. The original 12 F technique, modification 1, and TCSS were used in 15, 18, and 13 limbs, respectively. Technical success was achieved in all limbs. Computed tomography within one month showed no type I or III endoleak; one bridging stent graft occluded in the TCSS group. There were no pelvic ischaemic complications or external iliac artery dissections or perforations. Three percutaneous closure failures required suture repair. CONCLUSION: The U-turn approach enabled post-main body IBE placement in selected patients. When access and U-turn space were adequate, the U-turn sheath was generally escalated to ≥ 14 F; the original 12 F configuration was retained when either was limited, and TCSS was reserved for bridging expected to benefit from pathway separation or distal support. These off label strategies require careful planning. Prospective multicentre studies should assess reproducibility, comparative safety, and durability.

The original ipsilateral U-turn technique enables post main body IBE placement by redirecting a 12 F sheath towards the IIA through the same femoral access.

title: Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction From Proximal Intimo-Intimal Intussusception: A Fatal Complication of Acute Type A Aortic Dissection.
abstract: Acute type A aortic dissection is a highly time-sensitive cardiovascular emergency in which mechanical obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) by a prolapsing intimo-intimal intussusception flap represents a rare and often fatal complication, producing severe hemodynamic compromise that may be refractory to conventional resuscitative measures. We report a 26-year-old woman with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome who was transferred for evaluation of a large proximal type A aortic dissection and suffered a witnessed cardiac arrest shortly after arrival. Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) demonstrated a dissection flap prolapsing into the subvalvular LVOT during diastole, disrupting aortic valve coaptation and causing aortic insufficiency (AI), while moving anterograde during systole to obstruct forward flow. Despite transient return of spontaneous circulation, resuscitation ultimately failed, and veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was not pursued because of the underlying aortic dissection, AI, prolonged resuscitation, and concern for hypoxic-ischemic brain injury. This case highlights the diagnostic value of real-time TEE in identifying structural causes of cardiac arrest. This case also illustrates the hemodynamic consequences of a rare and often fatal complication of aortic dissection.

title: The association of rural residence with aneurysm presentation and loss to follow-up after endovascular aneurysm repair in the Vascular Quality Initiative.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Early recognition, timely access to care, and diligent follow-up are essential components of care for patients with aortic aneurysms. Rural patients have significant barriers to care and may present for surgery with larger aneurysms and be more likely to be lost to follow-up (LTFU). The purpose of this study was to assess the effects of rurality on clinical presentation of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA) and follow-up after endovascular aortic aneurysm repair. METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative's U.S. endovascular aortic aneurysm repair module (2003-2021) was used for analyses (n = 62,503). Patients were categorized as residing in an urban or rural area using rural-urban commuting area codes. Univariate analyses were performed to describe differences in sociodemographic, intraoperative, and follow-up factors. We fit unadjusted and adjusted logistic regression models to assess the association between rurality and aneurysm size, symptomatic presentation, adverse cardiovascular events, death, loss to follow-up, and follow-up type. RESULTS: A total of 79% (n = 49,372) of patients were classified as urban and 21% (n = 13,131) as rural with several significantly different demographic variables. On multivariable analyses, residing in a rural compared with urban area was significantly associated with 9% higher odds of undergoing repair with an aneurysm diameter of >6.5 cm [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 1.09; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.03-1.15], an 18% increase in the odds of presenting with an urgent AAA compared with elective (aOR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.11-1.24) and a 14% increase in the odds of being LTFU (aOR, 1.14; 95% CI, 1.05-1.23). Finally, of the patients who did follow-up, rural compared with urban residence was associated with a 10% lower odds of having in-person follow-up (aOR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95), but was associated with 13% higher odds of having any follow-up imaging (aOR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.04-1.23). CONCLUSIONS: This study found that rural patients had higher odds of large aneurysms at time of repair, higher odds of requiring urgent repair, and being LTFU. When they did have follow-up, it was less likely to be in-person. This suggests geographic disparities in quality of and access to appropriate AAA screening, repair and follow-up. Addressing this disparity will require coordinated multidisciplinary efforts, efficient referral pipelines, and reliable surveillance mechanisms postoperatively. Future efforts should aim to develop and implement evidence-based care delivery strategies for AAA care for patients in rural settings, such as primary care clinician education, telehealth platforms and travel assistance.

title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative contemporary benchmarks: Carotid artery stenting.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Carotid artery stenting (CAS) utilization and indications have evolved substantially with the introduction of transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR), recent regulatory expansion, and renewed attention following contemporary trial data. We sought to establish contemporary real-world benchmark outcome rates for CAS and characterize temporal trends and modality adoption within the Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI). METHODS: We analyzed all CAS procedures recorded in the VQI from 2011 to 2024. Contemporary benchmark analyses were restricted to procedures performed from 2021 to 2024, selected to reflect recent practice following the coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic and the maturation of TCAR adoption, and stratified by symptomatic status and modality [TCAR vs transfemoral CAS (TFCAS)]. Primary outcomes included in-hospital stroke, death, myocardial infarction, and major adverse cardiovascular events. One-year ipsilateral stroke and mortality were assessed among patients with available long-term follow-up data. Temporal trends in utilization were evaluated across the full study period and in relation to regulatory milestones, outcomes were compared by operator volume and physician-level TCAR adoption patterns were examined among Physicians with an established pre-2016 TFCAS practice. RESULTS: A total of 119,240 CAS procedures were identified across 821 centers and 3991 physicians, including 78,997 performed during the 2021 to 2024 benchmark period. TCAR comprised 73.6% of procedures performed during 2021 to 2024. In-hospital stroke rates were lower with TCAR than TFCAS in both asymptomatic (0.9% vs 1.4%) and symptomatic patients (1.8% vs 2.8%), as were death (0.3% vs 0.7% asymptomatic; 0.5% vs 1.8% symptomatic) and major adverse cardiovascular events (1.5% vs 2.1% asymptomatic; 2.5% vs 4.4% symptomatic; all P < .05). One-year ipsilateral stroke was lower after TCAR in symptomatic patients (5.6% vs 8.5%; P < .001) but did not differ significantly in asymptomatic patients (2.8% vs 3.4%; P = .054); 1-year mortality was lower after TCAR in both strata (3.0% vs 4.5% asymptomatic; 5.0% vs 7.6% symptomatic; both P < .001). In 2016, TCAR accounted for 7% of CAS procedures and TFCAS 93%, shifting to 76% and 24% respectively by 2023; annual TFCAS volume remained relatively stable through 2020 before increasing thereafter. Following the October 2023 Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services National Coverage Determination extending standard-risk coverage to both modalities, TCAR volume fell 11.5% (P = .008) and then declined 0.6% per month through December 2024, whereas TFCAS volume rose 11.2% (P = .026). Among 97 physicians with established pre-2016 TFCAS practice who subsequently adopted TCAR and remained active through 2022 to 2024, TCAR accounted for 85% of CAS volume by 2024, with lower pre-existing TFCAS volume associated with faster TCAR adoption. CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary VQI practice, TCAR is associated with lower unadjusted in-hospital and 1-year stroke and mortality rates compared with TFCAS regardless of the symptomatic status. TCAR adoption grew rapidly from 2016 through 2023 before declining following the October 2023 Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services policy change. As CAS utilization expands in the setting of evolving policy and trial evidence, these findings provide contemporary real-world benchmarks and underscore the need for continued registry-based surveillance.

title: Obesity-Related Traits Partially Mediate the Impact of Obstructive Sleep Apnea on the Risk of Venous Thromboembolism.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although observational studies have suggested an association between obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) and thromboembolism, causal evidence remains to be established. METHODS: Linkage disequilibrium score regression (LDSC) was used to evaluate the genetic correlations between OSA and thromboembolism. Based on the results of LDSC, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) analyses were performed to investigate the causal relationships between OSA and thromboembolism traits, such as venous thromboembolism (VTE), pulmonary embolism (PE), deep vein thrombosis (DVT), and phlebitis and thrombophlebitis (not including DVT) (PT), including reverse associations. Four common MR methods, in addition to Bayesian weighted MR analysis, were applied to evaluate causality. Multivariable analyses were conducted after adjustment for potential confounders, including sedentary behaviors (e.g., driving, computer use, and television watching), smoking, and alcohol consumption. Mediation analysis was performed to assess the mediating role of obesity-related traits. RESULTS: LDSC identified genetic correlations between OSA and thromboembolic subtypes (VTE, PE, and PT). Univariate MR indicated that OSA genetically predicted an increased risk of VTE, PE, and PT, with no evidence of significant reverse causality. After adjusting for confounders, OSA remained significantly associated with these traits. Mediation analyses revealed that the effect of OSA on thromboembolism was partially mediated by obesity-related traits. CONCLUSION: This study identified a positive causal association between OSA and specific thromboembolic subtypes, with no evidence of reverse causality. Obesity may partially mediate the effect of OSA on thromboembolism.

title: Perioperative outcomes after thoracic aortic surgery in Johannesburg: a retrospective observational cohort study, 1995-2023.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Thoracic aortic diseases require complex surgery, and outcomes data from African populations are scarce. We described the patient characteristic profile, documented risk factors, and perioperative outcomes of patients undergoing thoracic aortic surgery at a quaternary hospital in South Africa. METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study reported per the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines, we included patients aged 18 yr or older who underwent open thoracic aortic surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital between 1995 and 2023. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. We assessed correlates using modified Poisson regression with robust variance (risk ratios [RRs]). RESULTS: P vs Of 366 patients (median age 48 yr [inter-quartile range 37-59]; 219 [59.8%] male), diagnoses were dissection in 157 (42.9%), aneurysm in 157 (42.9%), traumatic rupture in 26 (7.1%), and other in 26 (7.1%). In-hospital mortality was 21.9% (80 of 366; 95% confidence interval [CI] 17.7-26.4) and did not differ significantly across diagnosis groups (=0.693), being identical after dissection and aneurysm (22.9% in each). Prolonged operative duration (>600 min) was the only variable independently associated with mortality (adjusted RR 7.2; 95% CI 1.5-34.9), an imprecise, sparse-data estimate. Mortality was numerically higher in female than male patients (26.2%19.2%) but this difference was not significant after adjustment (adjusted RR 1.30; 95% CI 0.89-1.89); age and diagnosis were not independently associated. CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital mortality after thoracic aortic surgery was 21.9%. Prolonged operative duration was associated with in-hospital mortality, although the estimate was imprecise, and operative duration is likely to be a marker of procedural complexity and adverse intraoperative course rather than an independently modifiable risk factor. The findings support intensive postoperative care.

METHODS: In a retrospective cohort study reported per the Strengthening the Reporting of Observational Studies in Epidemiology guidelines, we included patients aged 18 yr or older who underwent open thoracic aortic surgery at Charlotte Maxeke Johannesburg Academic Hospital between 1995 and 2023.

title: Nutritional Interventions for Patients with Intermittent Claudication: Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and the Case for Exercise-Adjunct Strategies: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) is a common atherosclerotic condition affecting over 200 million people worldwide, and supervised exercise therapy remains the best-supported first-line treatment for claudication. However, real-world adherence to exercise programs is persistently low, largely because the ischemic leg pain that exercise is intended to treat is itself a primary barrier to participation. This narrative review synthesizes the mechanistic rationale and clinical trial evidence for five classes of nutritional intervention proposed as potential adjuncts to exercise in patients with intermittent claudication: omega-3 fatty acids/fish oil, L-arginine and other nitric oxide precursors, carnitine derivatives, antioxidant vitamins, and dietary nitrate (beetroot juice and related sodium nitrate/nitrite forms). Across these categories, mechanistic rationale is generally strong, but clinical translation to improved walking distance is inconsistent and depends heavily on route of administration, dose, and combination with exercise. Carnitine derivatives, particularly propionyl-L-carnitine, showed relatively consistent walking-distance improvement, though evidence remains limited and further confirmatory studies are needed. Dietary nitrate showed benefit primarily when combined with supervised exercise, suggesting potential as an adjunct rather than a standalone therapy, particularly for patients with limited exercise tolerance. L-arginine, despite a compelling mechanistic rationale, showed no benefit in the best-powered trial available. Antioxidant vitamins demonstrated route-dependent effects, with acute intravenous administration showing more promise than chronic oral supplementation. Overall, nutritional interventions for patients with intermittent claudication represent mechanistically diverse approaches with markedly uneven supporting evidence. Further well-designed, adequately powered trials are needed to clarify their efficacy, safety, and place alongside exercise in clinical practice.

title: Cardiometabolic Risk-Driven Diagnosis of Cerebellar Infarction Presenting as Isolated Transient Vertigo: A Case-Based Review.
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance Case Presentation Conclusions : Vertigo is a common manifestation of posterior circulation ischaemia, and obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and dyslipidaemia are established cardiometabolic risk factors for the underlying atherosclerotic disease. Brief, isolated episodes may be diagnostically challenging because bedside findings can be normal after symptom resolution, despite clinically significant cerebrovascular disease. We present a case in which an adverse cardiometabolic risk profile-rather than the clinical presentation itself-prompted the vascular imaging that established the diagnosis, together with a targeted review of comparable reports;: We investigate the case of a 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidaemia, obesity, and known asymptomatic right internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis presented after a single spontaneous episode of rotatory vertigo lasting five minutes, which resolved completely before assessment. Neurological and structured neuro-otological examinations were normal. Because of his cardiometabolic and vascular risk burden, further imaging was pursued: CT angiography demonstrated progression of the right ICA stenosis to 85%, chronic occlusion of the left vertebral artery, and mild stenosis of the right vertebral artery, and brain MRI subsequently confirmed a small acute ischaemic lesion in the left cerebellar hemisphere. Management combined carotid artery stenting with a personalised, multidisciplinary secondary prevention plan addressing his full cardiometabolic risk profile. At three months, he remained asymptomatic, with NIHSS and modified Rankin Scale scores of 0. A targeted, CABARET-guided literature review of six comparable case reports showed that our patient carried the most extensive cardiometabolic burden yet had the mildest and most transient presentation, in contrast to the recurrent or progressive symptoms typical of the comparator reports;: A single brief episode of isolated vertigo may be the only manifestation of acute posterior circulation ischaemia, even when bedside findings are normal. In patients with an adverse cardiometabolic and vascular risk profile, a reassuring examination should not preclude further neurovascular investigation, and early, risk-guided recognition-supported by personalised, multidisciplinary care-may provide an important opportunity for stroke prevention.

title: Primary Glomus Tumor of the Inferior Vena Cava Diagnosed by Endovascular Biopsy: A Rare Incidental Finding.
abstract: Glomus tumors are uncommon mesenchymal neoplasms with modified smooth muscle differentiation that classically arise in the subungual region but may occur at extradigital, visceral, and intravascular sites. Although primary intravascular glomus tumors have been reported, apparent primary origin within the inferior vena cava (IVC) represents an unusual presentation and must be distinguished from secondary caval involvement by an extravascular tumor. A 44-year-old man with hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and osteoarthritis underwent musculoskeletal imaging for persistent right shoulder and upper back pain following a fall. Imaging incidentally demonstrated a 1.7-cm infrarenal IVC intraluminal abnormality initially interpreted as bland thrombus, while PET-CT showed no 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-avid malignancy. Endovascular evaluation demonstrated an obstructive intraluminal mass, and biopsy revealed uniform round-to-oval cells arranged around branching vascular channels. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated strong diffuse smooth muscle myosin heavy chain positivity with negative CAM 5.2 and chromogranin staining, supporting the diagnosis of glomus tumor. Subsequent surgical resection confirmed a 2.5-cm glomus tumor with smooth muscle actin (SMA) and caldesmon positivity and a low Ki-67 proliferative index (<1%). This case demonstrates the diagnostic challenge of an indeterminate intraluminal IVC lesion and emphasizes the importance of distinguishing apparent primary caval origin from secondary IVC tumor involvement. Endovascular tissue sampling can provide a minimally invasive means of establishing a diagnosis when imaging findings are inconclusive, and the integration of imaging, histomorphology, immunohistochemistry, and surgical pathology is essential for definitive classification.
